shloka_text: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः। सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते।।6.28।।
translation: Thus, constantly uniting the self with the Supreme, the yogi, freed from all sins, easily attains the supreme bliss of constant contact with Brahman.
meaning: The yogi who thus constantly unites their mind with the Supreme Self becomes liberated from all sins. Such a yogi easily experiences the supreme bliss that arises from constant contact with Brahman. This bliss transcends all worldly pleasures, being eternal and boundless. This state signifies the perfection of self-realization. Established in this ultimate joy, the yogi becomes liberated in this very life.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.28)

shloka_text: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि। ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः।।6.29।।
translation: A yogi whose consciousness is united with God and who possesses equal vision everywhere sees the Self situated in all beings, and all beings in the Self.
meaning: A yogi who has united their consciousness with the Supreme through yoga attains equal vision everywhere. Such a yogi sees their own Self situated within all beings. Simultaneously, they perceive all beings as existing within their own Self. This perspective enables them to see the same divine essence in all living entities. This equal vision is a symbol of true knowledge and spiritual unity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.29)

shloka_text: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति। तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति।।6.30।।
translation: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, for him I am never lost, nor is he ever lost to Me.
meaning: The devotee who perceives Me (the Supreme Lord) pervading everywhere is truly wise. Such a devotee sees all beings and objects as situated within Me. For such a devotee, I am never lost, meaning I am always manifest in their heart. Similarly, that devotee is never lost to Me, meaning they are always situated in My consciousness. This represents the pinnacle of exclusive devotion and knowledge. This relationship is eternal and unbreakable.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.30)

shloka_text: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः। सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते।।6.31।।
translation: The yogi who, established in unity, worships Me, who resides in all beings, dwells in Me, no matter how he may be living.
meaning: The yogi who worships Me, the Supreme Self residing in all beings, with a sense of unity, is a true knower. They understand that all living entities are parts of the same ultimate reality. Such a yogi, regardless of how they are living their life, always dwells in Me. Their consciousness remains absorbed in Me, even while engaged in worldly activities. This state represents a wonderful synthesis of Karma Yoga and Jnana Yoga.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.31)

shloka_text: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन। सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः।।6.32।।
translation: O Arjun, that yogi is considered supreme who, by analogy to himself, sees equality everywhere, whether in happiness or in sorrow.
meaning: O Arjun, that yogi who, by analogy to their own self, perceives happiness and sorrow equally in all beings, is considered supreme. They experience the joys and sorrows of others as if they were their own. This equal vision fills them with compassion and empathy for all living entities. Such a yogi does not discriminate against any being. This state is a symbol of universal love and spiritual unity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.32)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन। एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम्।।6.33।।
translation: Arjun said: O Madhusudan, this system of Yoga which You have described as being based on equanimity, I do not see its steady continuance, due to the mind's restlessness.
meaning: Arjun told Lord Krishna that the Yoga of equanimity He described seems difficult to comprehend. Due to the mind's inherent restlessness, Arjun cannot perceive a steady state for this Yoga. He believes the mind is so unstable that concentrating it appears almost impossible. This question highlights the natural tendency of the human mind and the challenges of the yogic path. Arjun's doubt represents a common problem faced by all spiritual aspirants.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.33)

shloka_text: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्। तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्।।6.34।।
translation: O Krishna, the mind is indeed restless, turbulent, strong, and obstinate. To control it, I consider as difficult as controlling the wind.
meaning: Arjun told Lord Krishna that the mind is inherently extremely restless. It is turbulent, powerful, and obstinate, making it very difficult to control. Arjun feels that subduing the mind is as challenging as trying to control the wind. This statement clearly illustrates the mind's formidable power and its instability. This represents a significant obstacle on the path of yoga, one that practitioners frequently experience.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.34)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं। अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते।।6.35।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: O mighty-armed one, undoubtedly the mind is restless and difficult to restrain. But, O son of Kunti, it can be controlled by practice and detachment.
meaning: Lord Krishna, answering Arjun's question, acknowledged that the mind is undoubtedly restless and difficult to restrain. He stated that controlling the mind is certainly difficult, but not impossible. The Lord revealed two primary methods for controlling the mind: practice and detachment. Practice means the continuous effort to repeatedly fix the mind on the Supreme Self. Detachment signifies non-attachment to worldly objects and desires.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.35)

shloka_text: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः। वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः।।6.36।।
translation: For one whose mind is unbridled, Yoga is difficult to attain; this is My opinion. But by one whose mind is controlled and who strives by right means, it is possible to achieve.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarified that for one whose mind is uncontrolled, the attainment of Yoga is extremely difficult. It is His firm opinion that success on the path of Yoga cannot be achieved without subduing the mind. However, for one whose mind is controlled and who strives continuously by appropriate means, it is certainly possible to attain Yoga. This verse underscores the importance of self-control and effort in the right direction for spiritual practice.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.36)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः। अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति।।6.37।।
translation: Arjun said: O Krishna, what destination does one attain who, though endowed with faith, is not self-controlled, and whose mind deviates from Yoga, thus failing to achieve perfection in Yoga?
meaning: Arjun posed an important question to Lord Krishna. He wanted to know what destination awaits a person who, though endowed with faith, lacks self-control and whose mind deviates from the path of Yoga. Such an individual strays from the path without achieving the complete perfection of Yoga. Arjun's inquiry is for all aspirants who fail to attain completeness in their spiritual practice. This question sheds light on the obstacles encountered midway through spiritual discipline and their consequences.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.37)

shloka_text: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति। अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि।।6.38।।
translation: O mighty-armed Krishna, does he not perish like a scattered cloud, having deviated from both paths, bewildered on the path to God-realization, and without any support?
meaning: Arjun further clarified his doubt, asking whether such a person does not perish, having fallen from both worlds. He wanted to know if they fail to attain both worldly pleasures and spiritual perfection. Arjun likened them to a scattered cloud, unable to find stability anywhere. This question highlights the plight of a practitioner who becomes bewildered on the path to God-realization. It expresses concern for the yogi who deviates from their spiritual journey.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.38)

shloka_text: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः। त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते।।6.39।।
translation: O Krishna, You alone are fit to completely dispel this doubt of mine. For, other than You, no one else can be found to remove this doubt.
meaning: Arjun humbly requested Lord Krishna to completely dispel his profound doubt. He clearly stated that no one else besides Lord Krishna was capable of removing such a spiritual uncertainty. This demonstrates Arjun's complete faith and trust in the Lord. This verse also highlights the importance of the Guru in the Guru-disciple tradition. Arjun knew that only the omniscient Lord could provide a satisfactory answer to this profound question.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.39)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते। नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति।।6.40।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: O Partha, there is no destruction for him either in this world or in the next. For, My dear friend, no one who strives for God-realization ever meets with an evil destination.
meaning: Lord Krishna assured Arjun that a yogi who deviates from the path does not suffer destruction either in this world or the next. He clarified that no one who performs auspicious actions ever meets with an evil destination. This is the Lord's unwavering principle: spiritual endeavors are never in vain. Even if a person does not achieve complete perfection in Yoga, their efforts continue to accumulate. This verse provides inspiration and reassurance to the spiritual aspirant.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.40)

shloka_text: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः। शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते।।6.41।।
translation: The unsuccessful yogi, having attained the worlds of the virtuous and dwelt there for many years, is then born in the house of pious and prosperous people.
meaning: Lord Krishna explained that the unsuccessful yogi first goes to the worlds of the virtuous. There, they reside happily for many years, enjoying the fruits of their accumulated merits. Subsequently, they are born into the family of pious and prosperous individuals. This birth provides them with a favorable environment for spiritual advancement. This demonstrates that no effort made on the path of Yoga ever goes in vain.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.41)

shloka_text: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्। एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम्।।6.42।।
translation: Or, if he is more advanced, he is born into a family of wise yogis. Indeed, such a birth is very rare in this world.
meaning: Lord Krishna further stated that if the unsuccessful yogi is more advanced, they are born directly into a family of wise yogis. Such a birth is considered extremely rare in this world, as it offers the best opportunity for spiritual progress. Being born into such a family provides an individual with spiritual values and an environment from childhood. This helps them to resume their yogic practices from their previous life. This state signifies a higher level of spiritual development.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.42)

shloka_text: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम्। यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन।।6.43।।
translation: O descendant of the Kurus, there he regains the understanding of his previous life and strives even more diligently for perfection.
meaning: Lord Krishna informed Arjun that in such a birth, the unsuccessful yogi regains the intellectual connection from their previous life. This means that the spiritual knowledge and impressions acquired in their past life are reawakened. Subsequently, empowered by that previous practice, they strive with even greater enthusiasm to achieve perfection. This process demonstrates that spiritual progress is never interrupted but continues across subsequent births.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.43)

shloka_text: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः। जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते।।6.44।।
translation: By that very previous practice, he is surely carried forward, even against his will. Even an inquirer of Yoga transcends the ritualistic principles of the Vedas.
meaning: Lord Krishna explained that due to their previous life's practice, the aspirant is drawn towards Yoga, even against their will. This attraction is so strong that they unknowingly progress on the spiritual path. Even an inquirer of Yoga, one who merely wishes to know about Yoga, transcends the results of ritualistic actions (Shabda Brahman). This implies that mere spiritual curiosity elevates an individual beyond material bondage.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.44)

shloka_text: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः। अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्।।6.45।।
translation: But the yogi who strives with great effort, being purified from all material desires, attains perfection after many births, and then reaches the supreme destination.
meaning: Lord Krishna stated that the yogi who strives with great effort becomes purified from all sins and material desires. Through continuous practice and spiritual discipline over many births, they attain complete perfection. Thus purified and perfected, they ultimately reach the supreme destination. This supreme destination is the state of liberation or attainment of God. This verse illustrates the continuity of spiritual practice and its ultimate fruit.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.45)

shloka_text: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः। कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन।।6.46।।
translation: A yogi is superior to ascetics, superior even to men of knowledge, and superior to ritualistic performers. Therefore, O Arjun, become a yogi.
meaning: Lord Krishna explained the importance of the superiority of a yogi to Arjun. He stated that a yogi is superior to ascetics because they do not merely inflict pain upon the body but also control the mind. They are superior even to men of knowledge, as they not only acquire knowledge but also experience it. A yogi is also superior to those who perform ritualistic actions with desires, because they act without attachment to the fruits of their labor. Therefore, the Lord advised Arjun to become a yogi.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (6.46)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः। असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु।।7.1।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: O son of Pritha, listen to how you can know Me completely, without any doubt, by practicing devotion with your mind attached to Me and taking refuge in Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna begins this chapter by instructing Arjuna on the path to knowing Him completely. He emphasizes that a devotee whose mind is attached to Him and who takes refuge in Him can truly comprehend His divine nature. This knowledge is free from all doubts and connects the soul with the ultimate truth. By following this path, the practitioner becomes liberated from the illusions of Maya. This chapter will further elaborate on the Lord's superior and inferior energies.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.1)

shloka_text: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः। यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते।।7.2।।
translation: I shall now declare unto you in full this knowledge, along with its practical realization, by knowing which nothing further remains to be known in this world.
meaning: Lord Krishna promises to reveal a supreme knowledge to Arjuna, one that encompasses both theoretical understanding and practical realization. He states that upon attaining this knowledge, nothing else in this world will remain to be known. This profound wisdom leads to self-realization and dispels all doubts, guiding the soul towards ultimate truth. It is the essence of the Bhagavad Gita, leading humanity towards perfection and liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.2)

shloka_text: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये। यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।।7.3।।
translation: Among thousands of men, hardly one strives for perfection; and among those who strive and achieve perfection, hardly one knows Me in truth.
meaning: Lord Krishna highlights the rarity and difficulty of the spiritual path in this verse. He states that out of thousands of human beings, only a few strive for perfection or self-realization. Even among those who strive and achieve some level of perfection, very few truly come to know Him in His ultimate reality. This underscores that knowing God in truth is an extremely rare achievement, resulting from profound spiritual practice. Such knowledge is not merely intellectual but is attained through faith and devotion. Therefore, the grace of the Lord is the key to this supreme understanding.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.3)

shloka_text: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च। अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा।।7.4।।
translation: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego—these are My eightfold separated material energies.
meaning: Here, Lord Krishna describes His inferior nature, which forms the basis of the material world. This material energy is divided into eight elements: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego. All these elements are various manifestations of the Lord's own power, from which this visible universe is constructed. This nature is inert and cannot act on its own, but is operated solely by the will of the Lord. This material nature binds the living entity and connects it to worldly experiences. Thus, the Lord creates this vast cosmos through His own energy.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.4)

shloka_text: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम्। जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत्।।7.5।।
translation: O mighty-armed one, this is My inferior nature. But know that beyond this, there is My superior nature, which comprises the living entities by whom this entire universe is sustained.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies the distinction between His two primary energies: the inferior and the superior nature. He refers to the eight elements described previously as His inferior, or material, nature. In contrast, He reveals to Arjuna His superior nature, which is conscious and constitutes the living entities. This superior nature is the source of all living beings and is what sustains this entire material universe. The living entities, as part of the superior nature, imbue the inert inferior nature with consciousness and operate it. Thus, the Lord creates, sustains, and dissolves the creation through these two energies.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.5)

shloka_text: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय। अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा।।7.6।।
translation: Know that all created beings have their origin in these two natures. I am the origin of the entire universe, and also its dissolution.
meaning: Lord Krishna declares that both His inferior (material) and superior (spiritual) natures are the origin of all created beings. He clarifies that all living entities arise from the combination of these two energies. Furthermore, the Lord proclaims Himself as the ultimate source and the final dissolution of the entire universe. He is the creator, maintainer, and destroyer of creation, thereby establishing His supreme authority. This verse illustrates the Lord's omnipresence and omnipotence, affirming Him as the fundamental basis of all existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.6)

shloka_text: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय। मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव।।7.7।।
translation: O conqueror of wealth, there is nothing superior to Me. All that exists is strung upon Me, like pearls on a thread.
meaning: Lord Krishna emphatically declares His supreme superiority and uniqueness. He tells Arjuna that there is no truth higher than Him; He is the ultimate reality. He sustains this entire universe within Himself, just as pearls are strung on a thread. Just as the thread is the foundation for the pearls, the Lord is the foundation for all creation. This analogy clearly illustrates His omnipresence and His position as the fundamental cause of all existence. Thus, the Lord is the controller and maintainer of the entire creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.7)

shloka_text: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः। प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु।।7.8।।
translation: O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the radiance in the moon and the sun. I am the sacred syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in ether, and the ability in humans.
meaning: Lord Krishna illustrates His omnipresence through various examples. He states that the life-giving taste in water is He Himself. The radiance and brilliance in the moon and the sun are also His manifestations. The sacred syllable Om, found in all the Vedas, is His divine sound, symbolizing the ultimate truth. The power of sound in the ether is also Him. Furthermore, the valor, prowess, and ability found in human beings are also His divine essence. Through these examples, the Lord establishes that He is the fundamental basis and essence of all creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.8)

shloka_text: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ। जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु।।7.9।।
translation: I am the pure fragrance of the earth, and the brilliance in fire. I am the life-force in all beings, and the penance in ascetics.
meaning: Lord Krishna further elucidates His omnipresence by stating that the pure and captivating fragrance of the earth is His own form. The burning power and light within fire are also Him. The life-force that sustains all living beings is also His energy. The power of penance and determination found in ascetics is likewise a part of Him. Through these examples, the Lord demonstrates that He is the source of all fundamental qualities and powers in creation. He is present in the very essence of everything.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.9)

shloka_text: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम्। बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्।।7.10।।
translation: O son of Pritha, know Me as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intellect of the intelligent, and the splendor of the splendid.
meaning: Lord Krishna further elaborates on His supreme existence. He tells Arjuna to know Him as the eternal seed of all beings, meaning He is the fundamental and imperishable source of all life. He is the power of discernment and knowledge inherent in the intelligent, which aids them in making correct decisions. Additionally, He is the brilliance, radiance, and influence present in splendid individuals, making them distinguished. This verse re-establishes the Lord's omnipresence and His role as the origin of all qualities. He is indeed the fundamental basis of all creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.10)

shloka_text: बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम्। धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ।।7.11।।
translation: O best of the Bharatas, I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and attachment. I am also the sexual desire in beings that is not contrary to dharma.
meaning: Lord Krishna continues to describe His divine potencies. He states that the strength found in the strong is His own form, but this strength must be devoid of desire and attachment. This implies that strength should be used for righteousness and justice, not for selfish motives or personal gratification. Furthermore, He is also the sexual desire in beings that is not contrary to dharma. This indicates that desires aligned with the principles of righteousness are also manifestations of the Lord. Thus, the Lord is the ultimate source of all virtuous qualities and dharmic inclinations.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.11)

shloka_text: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये। मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि।।7.12।।
translation: Know that all states of being—whether they be of goodness, passion, or ignorance—originate from Me alone. But I am not in them; rather, they are in Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains that all states of being, whether born of goodness, passion, or ignorance, originate from His own power. He clarifies that all these qualities and the conditions arising from them emanate from Him. However, the Lord also states that He is not bound by these qualities; rather, these qualities and the creation formed by them reside within Him. This demonstrates His detachment and His position as the supreme controller. He is not subject to the modes of nature, but is their master. This is proof of His inconceivable power.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.12)

shloka_text: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत्। मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम्।।7.13।।
translation: Deluded by these three modes of material nature (goodness, passion, and ignorance), the entire world does not know Me, who am beyond these modes and imperishable.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains the reason for the ignorance of beings in the world. He states that the entire universe is deluded by the states of being arising from the three modes of material nature (goodness, passion, and ignorance). Due to this delusion, living entities fail to recognize the imperishable Supreme Lord, who is beyond these modes and is the ultimate truth. This is the effect of Maya, which covers the intellect of the living entity and prevents it from knowing its true nature. As long as a being remains under the influence of these modes, it cannot truly know the Lord. Liberation from this ignorance is the ultimate goal.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.13)

shloka_text: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया। मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते।।7.14।।
translation: This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who surrender unto Me alone can easily cross beyond it.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the power of His Maya and the means to overcome it. He states that His divine Maya, composed of the three modes of nature, is exceedingly difficult to surmount. It is impossible to overcome it by one's own strength. However, the Lord also reveals a simple and certain path: those devotees who surrender exclusively unto Him are liberated from the bondage of this Maya. This surrender is the only way to transcend the influence of Maya. Thus, by the grace of the Lord alone, a living entity can cross beyond Maya and attain the ultimate truth.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.14)

shloka_text: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः। माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः।।7.15।।
translation: Those who are evil-doers, foolish, the lowest among men, whose knowledge is stolen by Maya, and who have adopted an atheistic nature, do not surrender unto Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes those who do not surrender to Him. He states that evil-doers, foolish individuals, and the lowest among men, whose intellect has been stolen by Maya, adopt a demoniac nature. Such people do not worship the Lord nor do they surrender to Him. Their intellect becomes corrupted by material desires and ego, preventing them from perceiving the ultimate truth. This demoniac disposition keeps them away from the spiritual path and traps them in worldly bondage. For such individuals, the path to liberation becomes exceedingly difficult.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.15)

shloka_text: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन। आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ।।7.16।।
translation: O best among the Bharatas, Arjuna, four kinds of pious people worship Me: the distressed, the seekers of knowledge, the seekers of material gain, and those who are situated in knowledge.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the pious individuals who engage in His devotion. He states that four types of people worship Him: the distressed (those in sorrow or difficulty), the inquisitive (those who desire to know the ultimate truth), the seekers of material gain (those who desire worldly pleasures or wealth), and the wise (those who have already attained self-knowledge). All these devotees turn towards the Lord as a result of their pious deeds. Although their motives may differ, they all receive the Lord's grace. This verse illustrates the Lord's magnanimity and His acceptance of all types of devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.16)

shloka_text: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते। प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः।।7.17।।
translation: Among them, the wise devotee, who is ever steadfast and devoted to Me alone, is the best. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise, and the wise are exceedingly dear to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna declares the wise devotee to be the best among the four types of devotees. A wise devotee is one who is ever steadfast and exclusively devoted, meaning their mind is always absorbed in the Lord, and their devotion is free from any other motive. The Lord states that He is exceedingly dear to such a wise devotee, and that wise devotee is also exceedingly dear to Him. This reciprocal relationship of love indicates the profound connection between the Lord and the wise devotee. The wise devotee knows the Lord in His true nature and is therefore inseparably connected to Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.17)

shloka_text: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम्। आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम्।।7.18।।
translation: All these (four types of devotees) are indeed noble, but the wise one, I consider to be My very Self. For he, being united with Me, is situated in Me alone as the supreme goal.
meaning: Lord Krishna considers all types of devotees noble, as they are all connected to Him in some way. However, He declares the wise devotee to be His very Self, which is His supreme opinion. The wise devotee considers his soul to be non-different from the Lord and remains fully situated in Him. He regards the Lord as his ultimate goal and refuge, which is the supreme destination. This state signifies the unity of the individual soul and Brahman, where the wise devotee establishes complete harmony with the Lord. Thus, the wise devotee is the closest to the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.18)

shloka_text: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते। वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः।।7.19।।
translation: After many births and deaths, he who is actually in knowledge surrenders unto Me, knowing Me to be the cause of all causes and all that exists. Such a great soul is very rare.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains that the attainment of ultimate knowledge is the result of a long spiritual journey. After many births of pious deeds and spiritual practices, a truly wise person understands the truth that 'Vasudeva is everything'. With this realization, he surrenders unto the Lord. Such great souls, who recognize the Lord as the ultimate cause and essence of all creation, are exceedingly rare. This verse signifies the pinnacle of knowledge and devotion, where the living entity completely surrenders to the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.19)

shloka_text: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः। तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया।।7.20।।
translation: Those whose knowledge has been carried away by various material desires surrender to other celestial gods, following specific rules and regulations, being controlled by their own nature.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes those who worship other celestial gods. He states that individuals whose intellect has been swayed by various material desires surrender to other deities according to their own nature. Such people follow specific rules and rituals to appease those gods. This indicates that the primary motivation for their devotion is not self-knowledge or the pursuit of ultimate truth, but rather the fulfillment of worldly desires. Influenced by their nature and the modes, they are attracted to deities who grant limited results. This path does not lead them to ultimate liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.20)

shloka_text: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति। तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम्।।7.21।।
translation: Whoever desires to worship any deity with faith, I make that faith of his steady and unwavering in that very deity.
meaning: Lord Krishna re-establishes His omnipotence and omnipresence. He states that whatever form of deity a devotee desires to worship with faith, He Himself makes that devotee's faith in that particular deity steady and unwavering. This implies that the power and influence residing in all deities are but a part of the Lord. He is the ultimate source of all forms of faith, regardless of which deity it is directed towards. This verse demonstrates that the Lord respects the desires of all beings and grants them results according to their faith.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.21)

shloka_text: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते। लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान्।।7.22।।
translation: Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that deity and obtains his desires, for those desires are certainly granted by Me alone.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies that the results obtained by devotees through the worship of other deities are also granted by Him. He states that when a devotee worships a deity with unwavering faith, they obtain their desired outcomes. These desires are, in fact, determined and granted by the Lord Himself. This means that no deity can grant results by its own power; rather, all results are obtained solely by the supreme will and power of the Lord. This demonstrates the Lord's supremacy and His position as the ultimate source of all powers.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.22)

shloka_text: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम्। देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि।।7.23।।
translation: But the fruit gained by those of small understanding is perishable. The worshipers of the celestial gods go to the celestial gods, whereas My devotees come to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna highlights the perishable nature of the fruits obtained from worshipping other deities. He states that the results gained by people of small understanding through the worship of demigods are temporary and perishable. Worshippers of demigods ultimately go to the realms of those demigods, which are themselves mortal. In contrast, the Lord's devotees attain Him directly, who is supreme and imperishable. This verse establishes the superiority of devotion to the Lord, as it leads to eternal liberation and the supreme abode. Therefore, a wise person should take refuge in the Lord alone.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.23)

shloka_text: अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः। परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम्।।7.24।।
translation: Unintelligent men, not knowing My supreme, imperishable, and excellent nature, think that I have assumed this manifested form (as a human being).
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the ignorance of those who fail to recognize Him in His true form. He states that less intelligent individuals do not know His unmanifest, supreme, imperishable, and excellent nature. Such people mistakenly believe that the Lord has assumed a manifested form at a particular time, as if He takes birth like ordinary human beings. They are unable to comprehend the Lord's divine and eternal nature. This ignorance keeps them distant from the Lord's true form and traps them in the illusion of Maya. The Lord's nature is eternal, pure, and free.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.24)

shloka_text: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः। मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम्।।7.25।।
translation: I am not manifest to everyone, being veiled by My Yoga-Maya. Therefore, this deluded world does not know Me as the unborn and imperishable.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the effect of His Yoga-Maya. He states that He is not manifest to everyone because He is veiled by His Yoga-Maya. Consequently, foolish and ignorant people do not recognize Him as unborn and imperishable. Yoga-Maya is the Lord's internal potency, which reveals Him to His devotees and conceals Him from non-devotees. This Maya deludes the living entity and prevents it from understanding the Lord's divine form. Only through pure devotion and the grace of the Lord can this veil be pierced, and He can be known.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.25)

shloka_text: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन। भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन।।7.26।।
translation: O Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, present, and future, but no one truly knows Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna declares His omniscience. He tells Arjuna that He knows all beings of the past, present, and future. Nothing is hidden from His sight, as He is the knower of all three times. However, He also states that no one truly knows Him in His essence. This indicates that the Lord's knowledge is infinite, while the knowledge of living entities is limited. Due to His Maya, living beings fail to recognize His true nature. Only by His grace can He be fully known.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.26)

shloka_text: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत। सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप।।7.27।।
translation: O scion of Bharata, O conqueror of enemies, all living beings are born into delusion, bewildered by the dualities of desire and aversion.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains the fundamental reason for the delusion of living beings in the world. He states that all living entities are born into delusion due to the dualities arising from desire and aversion. This delusion of dualities keeps them entangled in opposing feelings like happiness-sorrow, gain-loss, honor-dishonor, etc. Entangled in these dualities, the living entity turns away from its true self and from the Lord. This delusion prevents them from understanding spiritual truths and keeps them bound in the cycle of the material world. Liberation from this delusion is the ultimate goal.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.27)

shloka_text: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्। ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः।।7.28।।
translation: But those pious persons whose sins have been completely eradicated, being freed from the delusion of dualities, worship Me with firm resolve.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the fortunate souls who engage in His devotion. He states that only those pious individuals whose sinful reactions have been completely eradicated are freed from the delusion of dualities. Such pure-hearted devotees worship the Lord with firm resolve. Their minds are free from the dualities of desire and aversion, allowing them to focus intently on the Lord. This verse indicates that the destruction of sins and the accumulation of pious deeds pave the way for devotion to the Lord. Such devotees alone attain supreme peace and liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.28)

shloka_text: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये। ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम्।।7.29।।
translation: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death by taking refuge in Me, they know that Brahman, the complete knowledge of the individual self, and all about fruitive action.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes those devotees who take refuge in Him to achieve liberation from old age and death. He states that such devotees, who strive by taking shelter in Him, truly know Brahman in its essence. They also gain complete knowledge of Adhyatma (the individual self and the Supreme Self) and all about Karma (the principles of action and its results). This indicates that taking refuge in the Lord not only grants liberation but also bestows supreme knowledge. This knowledge frees them from worldly bondage and grants them eternal peace.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.29)

shloka_text: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः। प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः।।7.30।।
translation: Those who know Me as the governing principle of the material manifestation, of the celestial gods, and of all sacrifices, they, with minds fixed on Me, know Me even at the time of death.
meaning: This verse emphasizes the importance of understanding the Supreme Lord in His all-encompassing aspects. It states that those who perceive Krishna as Adhibhuta (the governing principle of the material world), Adhidaiva (the controller of all celestial beings), and Adhiyajna (the ultimate enjoyer of all sacrifices) possess true knowledge. Such devoted souls, whose minds are constantly absorbed in Him, are able to remember Him even at the critical moment of death. This unwavering remembrance at the time of departure ensures their liberation from the cycle of birth and death. Therefore, cultivating this comprehensive understanding of the Lord throughout life is crucial for attaining ultimate spiritual realization.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (7.30)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम। अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते।।8.1।।
translation: Arjuna said: O Supreme Person! What is that Brahman? What is Adhyatma? What is Karma? What is called Adhibhuta, and what is Adhidaiva?
meaning: Arjuna expresses his eagerness to understand the profound meanings of Brahman, Adhyatma, and Karma from Shree Krishna. He wishes to know the true nature of Adhibhuta and Adhidaiva in this world. This inquiry reflects Arjuna's intense desire for spiritual advancement and knowledge. Through these questions, he seeks to comprehend the mysteries of life and death. This verse serves as the introduction to the Eighth Chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, where Shree Krishna will clarify these complex concepts.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.1)

shloka_text: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन। प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः।।8.2।।
translation: O Madhusudana! Who is Adhiyajna in this body, and how does He reside here? And how are You to be known by those of steadfast mind at the time of death?
meaning: Arjuna here inquires about the nature of Adhiyajna and His dwelling within the body. He also wishes to know how the Lord can be known by steadfast individuals at the final moments of death. This question reflects humanity's natural curiosity about the fear of death and the destination thereafter. Remembering the Lord at the time of death is considered extremely important for those with controlled minds. Shree Krishna will answer these questions, clarifying the immortality of the soul and the path to the ultimate destination.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.2)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते। भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः।।8.3।।
translation: The Blessed Lord said: The indestructible, transcendental living entity is called Brahman, and its eternal nature is called Adhyatma. The offering that causes the manifestation of living beings is called Karma.
meaning: Lord Shree Krishna, answering Arjuna's questions, states that the Supreme Indestructible is Brahman. The individual soul's own nature is called Adhyatma, which is the true identity of the soul. Actions like yajna, charity, and penance, which cause the manifestation and development of living beings' material bodies, are called Karma. These actions motivate the soul to take birth in various species and perpetuate the cycle of transmigration. Thus, the Lord has provided the fundamental definitions of Brahman, Adhyatma, and Karma.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.3)

shloka_text: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम्। अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर।।8.4।।
translation: O best of the embodied! The perishable material nature is Adhibhuta, and the cosmic form of God, the universal soul, is Adhidaiva. And I Myself am Adhiyajna in this body.
meaning: Lord Shree Krishna further explains that perishable material nature is called Adhibhuta. The cosmic form of God, the universal soul, who is the lord of all celestial beings, is Adhidaiva, the regulator of the universe. Most importantly, the Lord Himself declares that He is Adhiyajna within every body. This means that He alone is the enjoyer and bestower of the results of all sacrifices and actions. This verse highlights the omnipresence of the Lord and His presence within all embodied beings.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.4)

shloka_text: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम्। यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः।।8.5।।
translation: And whoever, at the time of death, thinking of Me alone, leaves the body, he attains My nature; there is no doubt about this.
meaning: This verse emphasizes the profound importance of remembering the Lord at the time of death. The Lord states that whoever, at the final moment, leaves the body while remembering Him alone, attains His divine nature. This is an immutable truth about which there should be no doubt whatsoever. It indicates that the fruit of one's lifelong spiritual practice depends on the consciousness at the very last moments. Therefore, constant remembrance of the Lord is a guaranteed path to liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.5)

shloka_text: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्। तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः।।8.6।।
translation: O son of Kunti! Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits his body at the end of life, that state he will attain without fail, having been absorbed in that state of being throughout his life.
meaning: This verse further clarifies the principle of consciousness at the time of death. The Lord states that whatever state of being a person remembers at the end of life, that alone he attains. This occurs because the individual has been absorbed in that particular state throughout their life. This principle demonstrates that our thoughts and actions determine our future birth. Therefore, we should always remain absorbed in pure and spiritual thoughts so that the same consciousness prevails at the time of death.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.6)

shloka_text: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च। मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम्।।8.7।।
translation: Therefore, O Arjuna, always remember Me and also fight. With your mind and intellect surrendered to Me, you will surely attain Me, without a doubt.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord instructs Arjuna to constantly remember Him and perform his duty. He states that one should fight while remembering Him at all times, implying the integration of one's actions with divine consciousness. By surrendering one's mind and intellect to the Lord, one will undoubtedly attain Him. This is a wonderful synthesis of Karma Yoga and Bhakti Yoga, where spiritual goals are achieved even while performing worldly duties. This teaching demonstrates that it is possible to remain in God-consciousness while fulfilling worldly responsibilities.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.7)

shloka_text: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना। परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन्।।8.8।।
translation: O Partha! With a mind engaged in the practice of Yoga, and not deviating to anything else, one who constantly meditates attains the Supreme Divine Person.
meaning: This verse describes the path to attaining the Supreme Person through the practice of Yoga. The Lord states that only a person whose mind is engaged in the practice of Yoga and is not deviating attains the divine Person. It is essential for the mind not to wander elsewhere and to constantly contemplate the Lord. This emphasizes the importance of continuity and concentration in spiritual practice. Thus, the highest spiritual goal can be achieved only through regular practice and unwavering meditation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.8)

shloka_text: कविं पुराणमनुशासितार मणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः। सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूप मादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्।।8.9।।
translation: One who meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Controller, smaller than the atom, the Sustainer of all, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun, and beyond the darkness of ignorance—that Supreme Person.
meaning: This verse provides a detailed description of the divine qualities of the Supreme Person. The Lord is described as omniscient, ancient, the controller of all, and subtler than the atom. He is the sustainer and nourisher of the entire creation, possessing an inconceivable form. His effulgence is like the sun, and He is entirely beyond the darkness of ignorance. Only one who constantly remembers such a Supreme Person can attain Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.9)

shloka_text: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव। भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक् स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम्।।8.10।।
translation: One who, at the time of death, with an unmoving mind, endowed with devotion and the power of Yoga, fixes his life-breath perfectly between the eyebrows, attains that Supreme Divine Person.
meaning: This verse describes the method by which yogis attain the Supreme Person at the time of death. An individual must keep their mind steady and filled with devotion at the final moment. Using the power of Yoga, fixing the life-breath between the eyebrows is a crucial practice. One who thus meditates on the divine Person with a concentrated mind attains Him. This method highlights the necessity of deep spiritual practice and unwavering determination.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.10)

shloka_text: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति विशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः। यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति तत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये।।8.11।।
translation: That which the knowers of the Vedas call the Imperishable, into which ascetics free from attachment enter, and desiring which celibates practice celibacy—that state I shall briefly explain to you.
meaning: Lord Shree Krishna now describes that supreme state which the knowers of the Vedas call the Imperishable. This is the same goal into which ascetics, free from attachment, enter and attain ultimate peace. Desiring this very state, celibates observe strict celibacy. The Lord assures Arjuna that He will briefly explain this supreme state to him. This verse points towards the ultimate goal of liberation and the spiritual practices required to achieve it.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.11)

shloka_text: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च। मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम्।।8.12।।
translation: Restraining all the gates of the senses, confining the mind within the heart, and fixing the life-breath in the head, one who is situated in yogic concentration.
meaning: This verse describes a specific method of Yoga practiced at the time of death. It involves restraining all the gates of the senses, meaning withdrawing the mind from sense objects. Stabilizing the mind within the heart and fixing the life-breath in the head are crucial steps. These actions are performed through deep yogic concentration, enabling the mind to become focused. Thus, the yogi gains complete control over their body and mind to remember the Lord in the final moments.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.12)

shloka_text: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन्। यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम्।।8.13।।
translation: One who departs, quitting the body while chanting the single syllable 'Om', which represents Brahman, and remembering Me (Shree Krishna), attains the supreme goal.
meaning: This verse describes the method of leaving the body while chanting 'Om' and remembering the Lord. 'Om' is the single-syllable Brahman, symbolizing the formless aspect of God, and its chanting is considered highly sacred. Simultaneously, remembering Lord Shree Krishna is also supremely essential. A person who thus quits the body undoubtedly attains the supreme destination. This method presents a synthesis of worshipping God in both His personal and impersonal aspects.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.13)

shloka_text: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः। तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः।।8.14।।
translation: O Partha! For that yogi who constantly and regularly remembers Me with an undeviating mind, I am easily attainable, being ever-devoted.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Shree Krishna highlights the importance of unalloyed devotion. He states that for the yogi who constantly remembers Him with an undeviating mind, He is easily attainable. 'Ananya-chetāḥ' means one whose mind is not distracted by anything else. Such a constantly devoted yogi experiences no difficulty in attaining the Lord. This verse demonstrates that true devotion and concentration are the simplest paths to realizing God.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.14)

shloka_text: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्। नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः।।8.15।।
translation: Having attained Me, the great souls never again take birth in this temporary world, which is full of miseries, because they have achieved the highest perfection.
meaning: This verse describes the ultimate fruit of attaining the Lord. The Lord states that great souls who attain Him never again take birth in this temporary world, which is full of miseries. Such great souls have achieved the highest perfection, thereby becoming liberated from the cycle of birth and death. This liberation is the supreme goal of human life, where eternal bliss is attained. This teaching inspires devotees to turn towards the Lord so that they too may achieve this supreme state.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.15)

shloka_text: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन। मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते।।8.16।।
translation: O Arjuna! All the worlds, up to the abode of Brahma, are subject to return, meaning those who go there must take birth again. But, O son of Kunti, having attained Me, there is no rebirth.
meaning: This verse explains that all worlds in the material realm, even up to the abode of Brahma, are subject to return. This means that living beings who go to these worlds must eventually take birth again. Lord Shree Krishna clarifies that only after attaining Him is there no rebirth. This highlights the uniqueness of the Lord's abode and its eternal nature. Therefore, the supreme goal is to attain the Lord's supreme abode, from which one never returns.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.16)

shloka_text: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः। रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः।।8.17।।
translation: Those who know that Brahma's one day lasts for a thousand yugas and his night also lasts for a thousand yugas, they are the knowers of day and night.
meaning: This verse describes the immense time cycle of Brahma. Brahma's one day is equivalent to a thousand Mahayugas, and his night is equally long. Those who understand this measure of time are truly the knowers of the essence of time. This illustrates how vast and illusory the concept of time is in the material world. This knowledge makes us aware of the transience of material existence and the eternity of the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.17)

shloka_text: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे। रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके।।8.18।।
translation: At the advent of Brahma's day, all manifested beings emanate from the unmanifested. And at the fall of Brahma's night, they dissolve into that very unmanifest, called the unmanifest.
meaning: This verse describes the process of creation and dissolution within Brahma's day and night cycle. At the beginning of Brahma's day, all manifested entities emanate from the unmanifest nature. When Brahma's night arrives, all these manifested entities dissolve back into that very unmanifest. This cycle continues repeatedly, illustrating the temporary nature of material creation. This knowledge helps us understand that the material world is not eternal but part of a cyclical process.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.18)

shloka_text: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते। रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे।।8.19।।
translation: O Partha! This multitude of beings, repeatedly taking birth, helplessly dissolves at the advent of Brahma's night and becomes manifest again at the advent of his day.
meaning: This verse describes the cyclical birth and death of beings in the material world. The multitude of beings, meaning all creatures, repeatedly take birth during Brahma's day. At the advent of Brahma's night, they helplessly dissolve into the unmanifest. Then, with the advent of day, they manifest again, and this cycle continues endlessly. This indicates that living entities in the material world remain trapped in this cycle of birth and death, even against their will.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.19)

shloka_text: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः। यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति।।8.20।।
translation: But beyond this unmanifested nature, there is another unmanifested, eternal existence, which does not perish even when all beings perish.
meaning: This verse introduces an eternal, divine unmanifested existence that is beyond the material unmanifest nature. This unmanifested state is distinct from and superior to the unmanifest of material creation. Its characteristic feature is that it never perishes, even when all beings cease to exist. This supreme truth is the abode of the Lord, which is eternal and imperishable. This verse points us towards a permanent spiritual reality beyond the transience of the material world.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.20)

shloka_text: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम्। यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।।8.21।।
translation: That which is called the unmanifest and imperishable is said to be the supreme destination. Having attained which, one never returns; that is My supreme abode.
meaning: This verse further clarifies that eternal unmanifested existence, which is called imperishable. This imperishable unmanifest is referred to as the supreme destination or the highest goal. Lord Shree Krishna states that having attained this, human beings never return to this material world. That supreme abode is the Lord's own eternal dwelling place. This verse illustrates the ultimate goal of liberation and the glory of the Lord's divine abode.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.21)

shloka_text: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया। यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।।8.22।।
translation: O Partha! That Supreme Person, within whom all beings reside and by whom this entire universe is pervaded, is attainable only by unalloyed devotion.
meaning: This verse emphasizes unalloyed devotion as the sole means to attain the Supreme Person. The Lord states that the Supreme Person, within whom all beings reside, can only be attained through unalloyed devotion. He is the Supreme Person by whom this entire universe is pervaded and who is present within everything. Unalloyed devotion means love for the Lord alone, without any other desires or distractions. This verse simultaneously reveals the supremacy of devotion and the omnipresence of the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.22)

shloka_text: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः। प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ।।8.23।।
translation: O best of the Bharatas! I shall now describe to you the times at which yogis, departing from the body, attain either non-return or return.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Shree Krishna proposes to describe two distinct paths to Arjuna. These paths are for yogis who, after leaving the body, either attain return or non-return. Return means taking birth again in this world, while non-return means achieving liberation. The Lord here highlights the significance of time, which influences the destination after death. This knowledge will assist yogis in understanding the art of departing the body at the opportune moment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.23)

shloka_text: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम्। तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः।।8.24।।
translation: Fire, light, day, the bright fortnight of the moon, and the six months of the sun's northern course—departing in these, the knowers of Brahman go to Brahman.
meaning: This verse describes the 'bright path' or Devayana, which leads to liberation. Those knowers of Brahman who depart their bodies during fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, and the six months of the sun's northern course. They attain Brahman and do not return to this material world. All these auspicious times and symbols represent the path of knowledge and light. This path is for those who have practiced self-realization throughout their lives and are free from attachment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.24)

shloka_text: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम्। तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते।।8.25।।
translation: Smoke, night, and also the dark fortnight of the moon, and the six months of the sun's southern course—departing in these, the yogi attains the lunar light and returns again.
meaning: This verse describes the 'dark path' or Pitriyana, which leads to return. Those yogis who depart their bodies during smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the sun's southern course. They attain the lunar light, where they enjoy the fruits of their pious deeds. Upon the exhaustion of their merits, they return again to this mortal world. This path is for those who have performed fruitive actions and are still bound by material desires.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.25)

shloka_text: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते। एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः।।8.26।।
translation: Indeed, these two paths, the bright and the dark, are considered eternal for the world. By one, one goes to non-return, and by the other, one returns again.
meaning: This verse summarizes the two eternal paths, the bright (Shukla) and the dark (Krishna). These two paths determine the destination of living beings after death in the material world. One who takes the bright path attains liberation and does not return. Whereas, one who takes the dark path enjoys the fruits of their pious deeds and then returns to this world. This knowledge helps us understand the importance of our actions and consciousness so that we can choose the right path.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.26)

shloka_text: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन। तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन।।8.27।।
translation: O Partha! Knowing these two paths, no yogi ever becomes bewildered. Therefore, O Arjuna, be steadfast in Yoga at all times.
meaning: This verse highlights the importance of knowing these two paths. The Lord states that no yogi who knows these bright and dark paths ever becomes bewildered. This knowledge helps the yogi make correct decisions and remain focused on their goal. Therefore, the Lord instructs Arjuna to be steadfast in Yoga at all times, meaning to remain constantly in God-consciousness. This teaching demonstrates that through knowledge and practice, one can become free from the illusions of Maya.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.27)

shloka_text: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम्। अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम्।।8.28।।
translation: The yogi, knowing this secret, surpasses all the meritorious results declared for the study of the Vedas, performance of sacrifices, austerities, and charities, and attains the Supreme, original abode.
meaning: This verse establishes the supremacy of the knowledge of Yoga. The Lord states that a yogi who knows the secret of these two paths and the ultimate truth. Such a yogi surpasses all the meritorious results obtained from the study of the Vedas, performance of sacrifices, austerities, and charities. This yogi ultimately attains the Supreme and original abode, which is the eternal dwelling of the Lord. This indicates that Yoga, imbued with devotion and knowledge, is superior to all other religious activities and grants the highest liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (8.28)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच इदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे। ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।9.1।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: To you, who are free from envy, I shall now impart this most confidential knowledge, together with its realization, by knowing which you will be freed from the miseries of material existence.
meaning: Lord Krishna begins by promising to reveal the most confidential knowledge to Arjuna. This sacred wisdom is imparted only to those who are free from envy and possess sincere faith. It encompasses both theoretical understanding (jnana) and practical realization (vijnana) of the truth. By comprehending this profound knowledge, one becomes liberated from all inauspicious material entanglements. This liberation leads the soul to recognize its true nature and its eternal relationship with the Supreme Being.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.1)

shloka_text: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्। प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम्।।9.2।।
translation: This knowledge is the king of sciences, the most profound secret, supremely pure, directly perceivable, righteous, very pleasant to practice, and everlasting.
meaning: This knowledge is extolled as the sovereign science and the most profound of all secrets. It is supremely pure and excellent, capable of purifying the soul from all impurities. The wisdom it imparts is directly perceivable, meaning its truths can be experienced firsthand. It aligns perfectly with the principles of righteousness and is remarkably easy and joyful to practice. The benefits derived from this knowledge are everlasting, leading to eternal peace and liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.2)

shloka_text: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप। अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि।।9.3।।
translation: O conqueror of enemies, those who have no faith in this dharma (path of devotion) fail to attain Me and return to the path of repeated birth and death in this material world.
meaning: Lord Krishna emphasizes the critical role of faith as the foundation of spiritual progress. Individuals who lack conviction in this divine knowledge and the path of devotion cannot embrace it. Without such faith, they remain incapable of attaining the Supreme Lord. Consequently, these persons are compelled to return to the cycle of repeated birth and death in the material world. Therefore, unwavering faith in this sacred dharma is absolutely essential for achieving liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.3)

shloka_text: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना। मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः।।9.4।।
translation: This entire cosmic manifestation is pervaded by Me in My unmanifested form. All beings reside in Me, but I do not reside in them.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes His omnipresence, stating that He pervades the entire universe in His unmanifested form. This implies that His power and presence are everywhere, even though He Himself is not directly visible. All living beings and material elements are situated within Him, as He is the ultimate support and shelter for everything. Nevertheless, the Lord remains distinct from them and is not affected by their qualities or defects. This illustrates His inconceivable power and yogamaya, which enable Him to be simultaneously all-pervading and detached.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.4)

shloka_text: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्। भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः।।9.5।।
translation: And yet, all beings do not actually reside in Me. Behold My divine mystic power! Although I am the maintainer and creator of all beings, I am not situated in them.
meaning: Lord Krishna reveals another aspect of His inconceivable power, which transcends ordinary understanding. He states that although all beings appear to be situated in Him, they are not actually within Him. This is a wondrous manifestation of His 'yogam aishvaram,' or divine mystic power. He is the maintainer and creator of all living entities, yet He remains completely detached from them. This paradox highlights His supreme transcendence and His absolute distinction from material nature.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.5)

shloka_text: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान्। तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय।।9.6।।
translation: Understand that just as the mighty wind, blowing everywhere, always rests in the sky, so too all beings rest in Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna provides a beautiful analogy to explain His omnipresence and detachment. Just as the mighty wind, though constantly moving everywhere, always rests within the sky yet remains unaffected by it. Similarly, all living beings and the entire cosmos are situated within the Lord, yet He remains distinct and unattached to them. This example clarifies His inconceivable power, demonstrating how He sustains everything without being bound by anything. Comprehending this profound mystery is the initial step towards acquiring divine knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.6)

shloka_text: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम्। कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम्।।9.7।।
translation: O son of Kunti, at the end of a kalpa (a cosmic cycle), all beings merge into My material nature, and at the beginning of the next kalpa, I manifest them again.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes His role in the cyclical process of creation and dissolution. He explains that at the end of a cosmic cycle, known as a kalpa, all living beings merge back into His primordial material nature. This nature is His own energy, through which He governs the entire creation. Subsequently, at the dawn of the next kalpa, He manifests these very same beings once again. This continuous process illustrates the Lord's eternal power of creation and annihilation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.7)

shloka_text: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः। भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात्।।9.8।।
translation: Presiding over My own material nature, I repeatedly create this entire multitude of beings, who are helpless under the influence of nature.
meaning: The Lord performs the act of creation by presiding over and controlling His own material nature. He repeatedly brings forth the multitude of living beings into various species. These beings take birth under the sway of material nature, according to their past karma. They appear not by their own will, but by the compelling force of nature's laws. This elucidates the Lord's supreme controlling power and the process of reincarnation for souls based on their actions.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.8)

shloka_text: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय। उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु।।9.9।।
translation: O Dhananjaya, these actions do not bind Me, for I remain unattached to them, situated as if neutral.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains His principle of detachment from all actions. He states that all acts of creation, no matter how vast, do not bind Him. The reason for this is His unwavering detachment from those actions. He acts like a neutral observer, without any desire for the fruits of those actions. This demonstrates His supreme divinity, as He remains unaffected by the outcomes of all activities, even while being their ultimate source.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.9)

shloka_text: मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम्। हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते।।9.10।।
translation: O son of Kunti, under My supervision, material nature brings forth all moving and non-moving beings, and by this means, the cosmic manifestation is created and dissolved.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies that material nature operates solely under His supervision. Under His watchful guidance, nature brings forth both animate and inanimate beings. He does not directly interfere but inspires nature through His inherent power. It is for this reason that the entire cosmic manifestation is continuously created and undergoes transformations. This illustrates the Lord's supreme controlling power, without which nature would remain inert.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.10)

shloka_text: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम्। परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम्।।9.11।।
translation: Foolish people disregard Me when I descend in a human form, not knowing My supreme divine nature as the great Lord of all beings.
meaning: Lord Krishna here addresses those ignorant individuals who fail to recognize Him. When He descends in a human form, foolish people disrespect Him, considering Him an ordinary human being. Such individuals are unaware of His supreme divine nature and His position as the great Lord of all beings. Deluded by His illusory energy, they remain incapable of comprehending His true opulence. This verse reveals the profound mystery of the Lord's avatar pastimes and describes the plight of the ignorant.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.11)

shloka_text: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः। राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः।।9.12।।
translation: Such deluded persons are of vain hopes, vain actions, vain knowledge, and bewildered intelligence. They take shelter of the demoniac, atheistic, and deluding nature.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the characteristics of those ignorant individuals who fail to recognize Him. Such people live with vain hopes, and all their actions ultimately prove fruitless. Their knowledge also becomes futile, as it does not guide them towards the ultimate truth. They possess bewildered minds, remaining under the influence of demoniac, atheistic, and deluding natures. This nature keeps them far from the truth and maintains them in a state of illusion, preventing spiritual advancement.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.12)

shloka_text: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः। भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम्।।9.13।।
translation: But O son of Pritha, the great souls, who are under the protection of the divine nature, worship Me with an unswerving mind, knowing Me as the imperishable origin of all beings.
meaning: Lord Krishna now describes the characteristics of great souls, distinguishing them from the ignorant. Great souls take refuge in the divine nature, which assists them in comprehending the truth. They worship the Lord with exclusive devotion, knowing Him as the imperishable origin of all beings and the ultimate truth. Their minds remain fixed solely on the Lord, and they do not worship anyone else. This exclusive devotion enables them to truly know the Lord's real nature and attain Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.13)

shloka_text: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः। नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।।9.14।।
translation: Always glorifying Me, striving with great determination, humbly bowing down to Me, and constantly united with Me through loving devotion, they worship Me.
meaning: Great souls constantly glorify the Lord's glories, which is a primary aspect of their devotion. They strive tirelessly with firm determination for their spiritual advancement. They humbly bow down to the Lord, expressing their reverence and devotion. Their minds and souls remain perpetually connected to the Lord, keeping them constantly united. Thus, through exclusive devotion, they continuously worship the Lord and attain supreme bliss.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.14)

shloka_text: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते। एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम्।।9.15।।
translation: Others, by cultivating knowledge, also worship Me. Some worship Me as the undifferentiated oneness, some as distinct individuals, and others as the cosmic form with various manifestations.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains that He is worshipped not only through the path of devotion but also through the path of knowledge. Some enlightened individuals worship Him through the sacrifice of knowledge, perceiving Him as the undifferentiated Brahman. Others worship Him as distinct deities, considering Him the Supreme Lord in various forms. Some devotees worship Him in His cosmic form, seeing Him pervading the entire universe in manifold ways. This verse illustrates the Lord's omnipresence and the possibility of worshipping Him through diverse spiritual paths.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.15)

shloka_text: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम्। मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम्।।9.16।।
translation: I am the Vedic ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the oblation, I am the medicinal herb. I am the mantra, I am the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains His omnipresence through the various components of a sacrifice. He declares that He is the Vedic ritual (kratu) and the general sacrifice (yajna). He is also the oblation offered to ancestors (svadha) and the medicinal herbs. The mantras, clarified butter, fire, and the very act of offering in a sacrifice are all Him. This illustrates that the Lord is the origin, means, and fruit of all actions, and nothing exists beyond Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.16)

shloka_text: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः। वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च।।9.17।।
translation: I am the Father of this universe, the Mother, the Sustainer, and the Grandsire. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig Veda, Sama Veda, and Yajur Veda.
meaning: Lord Krishna reveals His supreme existence through various relationships and elements. He declares Himself to be the Father, Mother, Sustainer, and Grandsire of this entire universe. He is the ultimate object of knowledge and the purifier among all sacred things. The primordial sound Om, which is the root of the Vedas, and the three main Vedas—Rig, Sama, and Yajur—are also His manifestations. This verse establishes the Lord's supremacy and His role as the fundamental cause of all creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.17)

shloka_text: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत्। प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम्।।9.18।।
translation: I am the supreme goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the abode, the refuge, and the most loving friend. I am the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the imperishable seed, and the resting place.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes various aspects of His supreme existence, stating that He is the ultimate goal. He is the maintainer of all beings, the master, and the witness who observes every action. He is the abode for all, the ultimate refuge, and the true friend who desires welfare without any self-interest. He is the fundamental cause of creation, dissolution, and sustenance of the universe; everything rests in Him. He is the imperishable seed of all creation and the ultimate resting place, from which everything originates and into which everything dissolves.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.18)

shloka_text: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च। अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन।।9.19।।
translation: O Arjuna, I radiate heat, I withhold and send forth the rain. I am immortality and also death. I am the eternal spirit (sat) and the temporary matter (asat).
meaning: Lord Krishna demonstrates His omnipotence, stating that He is the controller of all natural phenomena. He radiates heat as the sun and regulates the rain, both withholding and sending it forth. He is the ultimate cause of life and death; both immortality and mortality are His manifestations. He is also the 'sat,' the eternal spirit, and the 'asat,' the temporary material existence. This verse establishes the Lord's supreme reality, who is the foundation of all dualities and manifestations.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.19)

shloka_text: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते। ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान्।।9.20।।
translation: Those who study the three Vedas, drink the Soma juice, and are purified of sins, worship Me through sacrifices and pray for passage to heaven. They attain the pious abode of Indra and enjoy the celestial pleasures of the gods in heaven.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes individuals who engage in Vedic ritualistic activities. Such persons study the three Vedas, partake in Soma juice, and purify themselves of sins through sacrifices. They worship the Lord through these sacrifices, but their ultimate goal is to attain heavenly planets. Due to their accumulated piety, they reach higher abodes like Indraloka and enjoy celestial pleasures there.
