This illustrates that the fruits of fruitive actions are temporary and do not lead to ultimate liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.20)

shloka_text: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति। एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते।।9.21।।
translation: Having enjoyed the vast pleasures of the heavenly planets, when their stock of pious merits is exhausted, they return to the mortal world. Thus, those who follow the rituals of the three Vedas, desiring sense enjoyments, repeatedly come and go.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies the transient nature of heavenly enjoyments. After experiencing vast pleasures in the celestial realms, when their accumulated pious merits are exhausted. These souls return to the mortal world, the earthly plane, from where they began their journey. Thus, those who follow the ritualistic portions of the three Vedas, solely desiring material enjoyments. They remain trapped in the cycle of birth and death, repeatedly coming and going, never attaining ultimate peace.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.21)

shloka_text: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते। तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्।।9.22।।
translation: Those who worship Me with exclusive devotion, always thinking of Me, I personally take care of their spiritual and material needs (yoga-kshemam).
meaning: Lord Krishna here reveals His special promise to His exclusive devotees. Those devotees who constantly think of Him alone and worship no one else. For such constantly absorbed devotees, He personally takes responsibility for their yoga (acquiring what they lack) and kshemam (preserving what they have). This means the Lord takes care of all His devotees' needs, whether material or spiritual. This verse demonstrates the Lord's immense compassion and love for His devotees, providing them complete security.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.22)

shloka_text: येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः। तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम्।।9.23।।
translation: O son of Kunti, even those devotees who worship other deities with faith, they also worship Me, but in an improper way.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies that all worship directed towards other deities ultimately reaches Him. Devotees who faithfully worship other gods are, in essence, unknowingly worshipping Him. However, this worship is performed improperly because they do not understand the Lord's supreme nature. They consider the deities as independent gods, whereas the deities are actually manifestations of the Lord's own powers. This verse highlights the Lord's supremacy, indicating that He is the ultimate recipient of all worship, even if the method is incorrect.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.23)

shloka_text: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च। न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते।।9.24।।
translation: For I am indeed the enjoyer and the Lord of all sacrifices. But they do not know Me in My true divine nature, and therefore, they fall down (wander in the cycle of birth and death).
meaning: Lord Krishna re-establishes His position as the supreme enjoyer and master. He states that He is the ultimate recipient and controller of all sacrifices and austerities. However, those who do not understand Him in this true essence remain bound by the fruits of their actions. Such ignorant individuals continue to wander in the cycle of birth and death and fail to attain the supreme destination. This verse emphasizes the importance of knowing the Lord's true nature, which is the path to liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.24)

shloka_text: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः। भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम्।।9.25।।
translation: Those who worship the celestial gods go to the gods; those who worship the ancestors go to the ancestors; those who worship ghosts go to ghosts; and those who worship Me come to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies the distinct outcomes of various types of worship. Those who worship celestial gods attain the abodes of those gods. Worshippers of ancestors go to the ancestral realms, and those who worship ghosts go to the ghostly species. However, those who worship the Lord with exclusive devotion directly attain Him. This verse illustrates that individuals achieve the destination they worship, and devotion to the Lord alone grants the supreme destination.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.25)

shloka_text: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति। तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः।।9.26।।
translation: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water, I accept that offering from the pure-hearted devotee.
meaning: Lord Krishna here emphasizes the simplicity and profound significance of devotion. He states that He accepts anything, no matter how humble, if it is offered to Him with love and devotion. Even a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a little water, if given with a pure heart, is accepted by the Lord. The value lies not in the object itself, but in the sentiment and love of the one offering it. This verse illustrates that the Lord is hungry only for love, and true devotion alone pleases Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.26)

shloka_text: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत्। यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम्।।9.27।।
translation: O son of Kunti, whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer as oblation, whatever you give as charity, and whatever austerities you perform, do that as an offering to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna here explains the principle of Karma Yoga, integrating it with devotion. He instructs Arjuna to offer all his actions, whether mundane or religious, to Him. This includes all activities such as eating, performing sacrifices, giving charity, and observing austerities. When all actions are dedicated to the Lord, they become free from the bondage of karmic reactions. This verse shows the path to spiritualizing every aspect of life and establishing a continuous connection with the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.27)

shloka_text: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः। संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि।।9.28।।
translation: Thus, you will be freed from the bondage of actions, which bear good and bad results. With your mind fixed on Me through renunciation (sanyasa-yoga), you will become liberated and come to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the outcome of dedicating all actions to Him. When all actions are offered to Him, an individual becomes liberated from the bondage of both good and bad karmic reactions. This leads to freedom from the entanglement of karma, which is the cause of the cycle of birth and death. Through sanyasa-yoga, meaning renouncing the desire for results and fixing the mind on the Lord, the soul becomes liberated. Thus, being completely liberated, the devotee ultimately attains the Lord and resides in His supreme abode.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.28)

shloka_text: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः। ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्।।9.29।।
translation: I am equally disposed to all living beings; no one is hateful to Me, nor is anyone especially dear. But those who worship Me with love and devotion, they reside in Me, and I also reside in them.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes His impartiality and equanimity towards all beings. He states that He regards all living entities equally; no one is His enemy, nor is anyone His special friend. In His view, no one is hateful or particularly dear; He offers equal opportunities to all. However, for those devotees who worship Him with love and devotion, a special relationship is established with the Lord. Such devotees reside in the Lord, and the Lord also resides in their hearts, which is the unique mystery of devotion.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.29)

shloka_text: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक्। साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः।।9.30।।
translation: Even if a person of extremely bad conduct worships Me with exclusive devotion, he should be considered righteous, for he has made the proper resolve.
meaning: Lord Krishna emphasizes the power of devotion and its transformative effect. He states that even if a person, regardless of how sinful their past conduct may have been. If they begin to worship the Lord with exclusive devotion, they should be considered righteous. The reason for this is that they have made a firm resolve to turn their life in the right direction. This verse illustrates that devotion to the Lord can eradicate anyone's past sins and purify them completely.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.30)

shloka_text: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति। कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति।।9.31।।
translation: He quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly that My devotee never perishes.
meaning: Lord Krishna guarantees the future of His devotee, regardless of their past. A person engaged in exclusive devotion quickly becomes righteous, and all their faults are eradicated. They attain lasting peace in this very life, a peace that transcends material happiness. The Lord instructs Arjuna to boldly declare that His devotee never perishes. This promise is a testament to the Lord's boundless love and protection for His devotees, safeguarding them from all adversities.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.31)

shloka_text: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः। स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम्।।9.32।।
translation: O son of Pritha, even those who may be of lower birth—women, Vaishyas (merchants), as well as Shudras (laborers)—if they take refuge in Me, they also attain the supreme destination.
meaning: Lord Krishna here emphasizes the universality and inclusivity of devotion. He states that anyone who takes refuge in Him, regardless of their social status or birth. Women, Vaishyas (merchants), Shudras (laborers), or even those born in lower species, if they take shelter of the Lord. All of them attain the supreme destination, which is the highest goal of liberation. This verse illustrates that birth or social class is no impediment to spiritual advancement; only sincere devotion is paramount.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.32)

shloka_text: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा। अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम्।।9.33।।
translation: What then to speak of the pious Brahmins and saintly royal sages who are My devotees! Therefore, having obtained this transient and joyless world, engage in devotion to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna extends the logic from the previous verse, stating that if even those of lower birth can attain Him. Then, what to say of pious Brahmins and saintly royal sages who are naturally virtuous and knowledgeable. For them, attaining the Lord is even more certain and straightforward due to their inherent qualities. The Lord advises Arjuna to engage in devotion to Him, having taken birth in this transient and sorrowful world. This verse inspires one to recognize the ephemeral nature of life and engage in devotion to achieve ultimate happiness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.33)

shloka_text: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु। मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः।।9.34।।
translation: Always think of Me, be My devotee, worship Me, and offer obeisances to Me. By thus dedicating your mind and body to Me, you will certainly come to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna presents the essence of this chapter in four simple instructions, forming the foundation of Bhakti Yoga. He commands Arjuna to always fix his mind on Him, become His devotee, and worship Him. Additionally, He instructs Arjuna to humbly offer obeisances to Him, which symbolizes complete surrender. By following these directives, an individual's mind and soul become fully united with the Lord. Thus, by dedicating oneself to the Lord, the devotee is assured of attaining Him and reaching the supreme abode.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (9.34)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच भूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः। यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया।।10.1।।
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O mighty-armed one, hear again My supreme word, which I shall speak to you, who are My beloved, for your welfare.
meaning: Lord Krishna addresses Arjuna, stating that He will again impart His supreme words. This verse highlights the profound love of the Lord for Arjuna and His desire for Arjuna's welfare. The Supreme Lord is exceedingly compassionate towards His devotees and is always ready to bestow knowledge upon them. This verse also underscores the significance of the guru-disciple tradition, where the disciple's faith and the guru's love form the basis of knowledge acquisition. The Lord's words are not mere instructions but divine guidance for the ultimate good of the living entity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.1)

shloka_text: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः। अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः।।10.2।।
translation: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know My origin; for I am, in every respect, the source of the gods and the great sages.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna declares His supreme existence. He states that neither the gods nor the great sages know His origin or true nature. The reason for this is that the Lord Himself is the prime cause of all gods and great sages. He is the original source of all creation, from whom everything emanates. This illustrates His inconceivable power and paramount position, which transcends all mundane or divine entities.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.2)

shloka_text: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम्। असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते।।10.3।।
translation: He who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the Supreme Lord of all worlds, he, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes the glory of one who truly understands His nature. A person who knows the Lord as unborn, beginningless, and the great Lord of all worlds is truly wise. Such an individual becomes free from the entanglement of worldly illusion and remains undeluded. By the influence of this knowledge, one is liberated from all sins and attains supreme peace. This knowledge alone is the path to liberation and grants freedom from all bondage.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.3)

shloka_text: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः। सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च।।10.4।।
translation: Intellect, knowledge, freedom from delusion, forgiveness, truthfulness, control over the senses, control of the mind, joy, sorrow, birth, death, fear, and fearlessness—
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes various qualities and emotions that originate from Him. Virtues like intellect, knowledge, and freedom from delusion are essential for human spiritual development. Forgiveness, truthfulness, sense-control, and mind-control are symbols of self-mastery and ethical conduct. Dualities such as joy-sorrow, birth-death, and fear-fearlessness also manifest through His power. All these emotions and qualities are indeed His opulences, existing in diverse forms throughout the world. This illustrates that the entire creation and all experiences within it are extensions of the Lord's divine play.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.4)

shloka_text: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः। भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः।।10.5।।
translation: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and infamy—these various dispositions of living beings arise from Me alone.
meaning: Continuing to describe His opulences, Lord Krishna states that qualities like non-violence, equanimity, and contentment also originate from Him. Actions such as austerity and charity are also inspired by Him, which are crucial for the welfare of living beings. Worldly outcomes like fame and infamy are also determined by His will. All these various dispositions and tendencies manifest in living entities solely from Me. This indicates that all virtues and vices, good and bad, present in every living being, are different aspects of the Lord's power.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.5)

shloka_text: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा। मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः।।10.6।।
translation: The seven great sages, and before them the four great sages (Sanaka and others), and the fourteen Manus—all these were born from My mind, and from them all these living beings in the world have originated.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His process of creation, states that the seven great sages and, even before them, the four Sanaka sages, were born from His mind. Additionally, the fourteen Manus, who govern during different cosmic periods, also manifested from His being. From all these great souls, all the living entities in the world have originated and expanded. This demonstrates that the Lord is the ultimate source of all creation, and all primary creators are parts of His power. Thus, the supreme authority of the Lord and His creative power are clearly explained.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.6)

shloka_text: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः। सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः।।10.7।।
translation: He who truly knows My opulence and mystic power becomes united with Me through unwavering devotional service—there is no doubt about this.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes the fruit of knowledge gained by understanding His opulences and mystic power. A person who truly comprehends the Lord's divine glory and His inconceivable powers becomes firmly established in unwavering devotional service. The mind of such a devotee becomes fixed on the Lord and never wavers. This knowledge connects him in an unbreakable bond with the Lord, leading to the attainment of supreme peace and liberation. There is no doubt that this knowledge is the foundation of ultimate devotion.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.7)

shloka_text: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते। इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः।।10.8।।
translation: I am the origin of all creation, and everything proceeds from Me. Knowing this, the wise worship Me with great faith and devotion.
meaning: Lord Krishna presents the essence of His supreme existence in this verse. He states that He is the original source of all creation, and everything originates from Him and is sustained by Him. Knowing this truth, wise and knowledgeable individuals worship the Lord with complete faith and devotion. Such devotees consider the Lord as their everything and remain absorbed in Him. This verse clarifies the fundamental principle of Bhakti Yoga, where the Lord is worshipped as the cause of all causes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.8)

shloka_text: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम्। कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च।।10.9।।
translation: Those whose minds are fixed on Me, whose lives are surrendered to Me, enlightening one another with divine knowledge of God and constantly speaking about Me, remain satisfied and delight in Me.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes the characteristics of His exclusive devotees. Such devotees, whose minds and lives are completely surrendered to the Lord, share knowledge of the Lord's divine qualities and pastimes with each other. They constantly speak about the Lord and enlighten one another with spiritual wisdom. In this way, they remain satisfied and delight in the Lord's love. This is a beautiful form of devotion where devotees, in community, glorify the Lord's greatness and experience supreme joy.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.9)

shloka_text: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम्। ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते।।10.10।।
translation: To those who are ever steadfast and worship Me with love, I grant that divine knowledge (buddhi-yoga) by which they come to Me.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes His grace towards His devotees. To those devotees who are constantly engaged in Me and worship Me with love, I grant that special buddhi-yoga. This buddhi-yoga is the divine knowledge that shows them the right path and helps them reach Me. This indicates that the Lord not only bestows love upon His devotees but also provides them with the necessary intelligence and guidance for spiritual progress. Thus, the Lord guides His devotees on the path to liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.10)

shloka_text: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः। नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता।।10.11।।
translation: Out of compassion for them, I, dwelling within their hearts, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the luminous lamp of knowledge.
meaning: Lord Krishna demonstrates His boundless compassion towards His devotees. He states that out of compassion for His devotees, He Himself resides within their hearts. Dwelling there, He destroys the darkness born of ignorance with the luminous lamp of knowledge. This indicates that the Lord guides His devotees internally and leads them out of spiritual darkness. It is the Lord's supreme kindness that He Himself ignites the light of knowledge within the hearts of His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.11)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान्। पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम्।।10.12।।
translation: Arjuna said: You are the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Abode, the Supreme Purifier. You are the eternal, divine Person, the primal God, unborn, and all-pervading.
meaning: Arjuna, upon hearing Lord Krishna's words, accepts His divinity. He declares the Lord to be the Supreme Brahman, the Supreme Abode, and the Supreme Purifier, who is the foundation of all creation. Arjuna recognizes Him as the eternal, divine Person, the primal God, unborn, and all-pervading. This demonstrates Arjuna's deep faith and knowledge, as he has understood the true nature of the Lord. This verse is a beautiful hymn of praise to the Lord's glory and His supreme form.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.12)

shloka_text: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा। असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे।।10.13।।
translation: All the sages, as well as the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, declare You to be so, and You Yourself are also telling me this.
meaning: Arjuna, affirming his statement, says that not only he, but all great sages also consider the Lord to be the Supreme Truth. Revered saints like the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa also describe the Lord in this very form. Arjuna emphasizes that the Lord Himself is declaring this truth, which confirms his faith. This verse highlights the tradition of ancient sages and the authenticity of their knowledge, who accept the Lord's divine nature.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.13)

shloka_text: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव। न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः।।10.14।।
translation: O Keshav! All that You tell me, I accept as truth. O Lord! Neither the gods nor the demons understand Your manifestation.
meaning: Arjuna accepts Lord Krishna's words as absolute truth. He states that whatever the Lord is telling him is factual and beyond doubt. Arjuna also acknowledges that neither the gods nor the demons can comprehend the Lord's true pastimes or form. This is due to the Lord's inconceivable power and the influence of His Maya, which prevents anyone from knowing His complete nature. This verse demonstrates Arjuna's complete faith and his surrender to the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.14)

shloka_text: स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम। भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते।।10.15।।
translation: O Purushottama! O Creator of all beings! O Lord of all beings! O God of gods! O Lord of the universe! You alone know Yourself by Yourself.
meaning: Arjuna acknowledges Lord Krishna's uniqueness, stating that He is the only one who knows Himself by Himself. He addresses the Lord as Purushottama, the Creator of all beings (Bhutabhavana), the Lord of all creatures (Bhutesha), the God of gods (Devadeva), and the Lord of the entire universe (Jagatpate). This indicates that the Lord's knowledge does not depend on any external source, but He Himself is the knower of His own nature. This is proof of His supreme independence and omniscience, which is not found in any other entity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.15)

shloka_text: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः। याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि।।10.16।।
translation: You alone are capable of fully describing Your own divine opulences, by which You pervade and reside in all these worlds.
meaning: Arjuna requests the Lord to describe His divine opulences in detail. He states that only the Lord Himself can fully explain His boundless powers and glories, by which He pervades all worlds. This indicates Arjuna's eagerness to know the Lord's universal form, so that he may understand His greatness more deeply. This prayer reveals the devotee's curiosity and his faith in the Lord, which leads him towards supreme knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.16)

shloka_text: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन्। केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया।।10.17।।
translation: O Yogin! How shall I, constantly meditating, know You? O Lord! In what various forms are You to be contemplated by me?
meaning: Arjuna asks the Lord how he can continuously meditate upon Him and know Him. He wishes to know in what specific forms or aspects the Lord is to be contemplated by him. This question reflects the devotee's practical curiosity about how he can experience the Lord in his daily life. Arjuna seeks to understand how to comprehend the Lord's omnipresence and in what objects His presence can be experienced. This knowledge will help the devotee establish a deeper connection with the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.17)

shloka_text: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन। भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम्।।10.18।।
translation: O Janardana! Please describe Your mystic power and opulence again in detail; for I am never satiated by hearing Your nectar-like words.
meaning: Arjuna requests Lord Krishna to describe His mystic power and opulences again in detail. He states that he is never satiated by hearing the Lord's nectar-like words; rather, his desire to hear only increases. This demonstrates the devotee's boundless faith and love for the Lord, where the thirst for divine knowledge is never quenched. Arjuna's prayer is an inspiration for all seekers to always remain eager to know the Lord's glory.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.18)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः। प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे।।10.19।।
translation: The Blessed Lord said: Yes, O best of the Kurus, I shall certainly describe to you My divine opulences, primarily; for there is no end to My extensive glories.
meaning: Lord Krishna accepts Arjuna's request and agrees to describe His divine opulences. He states that He will tell Arjuna about His principal opulences, as there is no end to His glories. This indicates that the Lord's powers and splendors are infinite, and a complete description of them is impossible. Therefore, He will only mention the main forms through which Arjuna can recognize Him in the world. This reveals the Lord's boundlessness and His grace in bestowing knowledge upon His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.19)

shloka_text: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः। अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च।।10.20।।
translation: O Gudakesha! I am the Self, seated in the hearts of all living entities. I am also the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings.
meaning: Lord Krishna reveals the most important aspect of His supreme existence. He addresses Arjuna as 'Gudakesha' (conqueror of sleep) and states that He resides as the Self in the hearts of all living entities. This means that He is present within every being as the witness and controller. Furthermore, He is the fundamental cause of the origin, sustenance, and dissolution of all beings. This verse clarifies the Lord's omnipresence and His supreme lordship, who is the foundation of all creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.20)

shloka_text: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान्। मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी।।10.21।।
translation: Among the Adityas, I am Vishnu; among luminous objects, I am the radiant sun. Among the Maruts, I am Marichi, and among the stars, I am the moon.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that He manifests Himself in various supreme entities. Among the Adityas, He is Vishnu, known as the maintainer. Among all luminous objects, He is the radiant sun, the source of light and energy. Among the Maruts, He is Marichi, the powerful deity of the winds. Among the stars, He is the moon, which provides coolness and peace. This indicates that wherever there is excellence, power, or beauty, it is a part of the Lord's opulence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.21)

shloka_text: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः। इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना।।10.22।।
translation: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the celestial gods, I am Indra. Among the senses, I am the mind, and among living beings, I am consciousness.
meaning: Continuing to describe His opulences, Lord Krishna states that among the Vedas, He is the Sama Veda, renowned for its sweetness and musicality. Among the celestial gods, He is Indra, the king of heaven and a powerful ruler. Among the senses, He is the mind, which is the center of will and deliberation, controlling all other senses. Among all living beings, He is consciousness, the essence of life and the basis of all experience. This indicates that the Lord exists as the supreme power not only in the external world but also in the internal realm.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.22)

shloka_text: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम्। वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम्।।10.23।।
translation: Among the Rudras, I am Shankara (Lord Shiva); among Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera (the god of wealth). Among the Vasus, I am Agni (fire), and among mountains, I am Mount Meru.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among the Rudras, He is Shankara (Lord Shiva), the deity of destruction. Among Yakshas and Rakshasas, He is Kubera, the god of wealth and treasurer. Among the Vasus, He is Agni (the fire god), a symbol of purity and energy. Among mountains, He is Mount Meru, considered the abode of the gods. This indicates that the Lord manifests His presence in all powerful and significant entities, and His glory is omnipresent.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.23)

shloka_text: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम्। सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः।।10.24।।
translation: O Partha! Among priests, know Me as the chief Brihaspati. Among commanders, I am Skanda (Kartikeya), and among reservoirs of water, I am the ocean.
meaning: Lord Krishna continues to describe His opulences, addressing Arjuna. He states that among priests, He is Brihaspati, the guru of the gods and a symbol of knowledge. Among commanders, He is Skanda (Kartikeya), the commander-in-chief of the gods and a symbol of martial prowess. Among all reservoirs of water, He is the ocean, a symbol of boundless depth and vastness. This indicates that the Lord is present in the supreme and most influential form in every sphere where leadership, power, or vastness is demonstrated.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.24)

shloka_text: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम्। यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः।।10.25।।
translation: Among the great seers, I am Bhrigu; among utterances, I am the single syllable (Om). Among sacrifices, I am the sacrifice of chanting (japa-yajna), and among immovable things, I am the Himalayas.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among the great seers, He is Bhrigu, who was a great ascetic and wise man. Among utterances, He is the single syllable 'Om', which is the essence of all Vedas and a symbol of the Supreme Brahman. Among sacrifices, He is japa-yajna, considered the highest sacrifice because it is simple and highly fruitful. Among immovable things, He is the Himalayas, renowned for its vastness and stability. This indicates that the Lord manifests Himself in the supreme expressions of knowledge, sound, devotion, and nature.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.25)

shloka_text: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः। गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः।।10.26।।
translation: Among all trees, I am the Banyan tree; among the celestial sages, I am Narada. Among the Gandharvas, I am Chitraratha, and among the perfected beings, I am Sage Kapila.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among trees, He is the Banyan tree, considered sacred and long-lived. Among the celestial sages, He is Narada, who is a supreme devotee of the Lord and travels through all three worlds. Among the Gandharvas, He is Chitraratha, renowned for his musical art. Among the perfected beings, He is Sage Kapila, who expounded the Sankhya philosophy. This indicates that the Lord is present in the supreme and ideal forms in the realms of nature, devotion, art, and knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.26)

shloka_text: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम्। ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम्।।10.27।।
translation: Among horses, know Me as Uchchaihshrava, born from the churning of nectar. Among lordly elephants, I am Airavata, and among humans, I am the king.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among horses, He is Uchchaihshrava, which was born from the churning of the ocean of nectar and is considered supremely excellent. Among lordly elephants, He is Airavata, the vehicle of Indra and the best of all elephants. Among humans, He is the king, who is a symbol of justice and order and protects the subjects. This indicates that the Lord is present in the supreme and influential forms even in the animal kingdom and human society, representing power, beauty, and governance.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.27)

shloka_text: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक्। प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः।।10.28।।
translation: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt (Vajra); among cows, I am Kamadhenu. Among the causes of procreation, I am Kamadeva (the god of love), and among serpents, I am Vasuki.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among weapons, He is the thunderbolt (Vajra), the powerful weapon of Indra. Among cows, He is Kamadhenu, the divine cow that fulfills all desires. Among the causes of procreation, He is Kamadeva, who symbolizes love and attraction for the continuity of creation. Among serpents, He is Vasuki, the king of serpents who assisted in the churning of the ocean. This indicates that the Lord is present in supreme forms even in power, prosperity, creation, and among mysterious beings.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.28)

shloka_text: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम्। पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम्।।10.29।।
translation: Among snakes, I am Ananta (Sheshnaga); among aquatics, I am Varuna. Among the departed ancestors, I am Aryama, and among dispensers of law, I am Yama.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among snakes, He is Ananta (Sheshnaga), who serves as Lord Vishnu's couch. Among aquatics, He is Varuna, the deity of water and lord of the ocean. Among the departed ancestors, He is Aryama, the chief deity of Pitriloka. Among dispensers of law, He is Yama, the god of righteousness and death. This indicates that the Lord is present as the supreme regulator and maintainer in various realms and systems of creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.29)

shloka_text: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम्। मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्।।10.30।।
translation: Among the demons, I am Prahlada; among all that controls, I am Time. Among animals, I am the lion, and among birds, I am Garuda.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among the demons, He is Prahlada, renowned for his unwavering devotion. Among all that controls, He is Time, which governs everything and spares no one. Among animals, He is the lion, known for its strength and prowess. Among birds, He is Garuda, the vehicle of Lord Vishnu and the best of all birds. This indicates that the Lord manifests Himself in the supreme forms of devotion, control, power, and speed.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.30)

shloka_text: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम्। झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी।।10.31।।
translation: Among purifiers, I am the wind; among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among aquatic creatures, I am the crocodile, and among flowing rivers, I am the Ganges.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among purifiers, He is the wind, which purifies everything. Among wielders of weapons, He is Rama, who symbolizes righteousness and moral conduct. Among aquatic creatures, He is the crocodile, known for its strength and fear. Among flowing rivers, He is the Ganges, considered supremely sacred and bestower of liberation. This indicates that the Lord manifests Himself in the supreme forms of purity, righteousness, power, and sanctity, which are essential for the welfare of creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.31)

shloka_text: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन। अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम्।।10.32।।
translation: O Arjuna! Of all creations, I am the beginning, the end, and also the middle. Among sciences, I am the science of spirituality, and among debaters, I am the conclusive truth.
meaning: Lord Krishna reiterates the essence of His supreme existence in this verse. He tells Arjuna that He is the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creations, which demonstrates His omnipresence and controlling power. Among sciences, He is the science of spirituality, considered supreme among all knowledge as it reveals the truth of the Self and the Supreme Self. Among debaters, He is the conclusive truth, representing the ultimate reality and logical conclusion. This indicates that the Lord is at the root of all knowledge and existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.32)

shloka_text: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च। अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः।।10.33।।
translation: Among letters, I am the letter 'A'; among grammatical compounds, I am the dual compound. I am indeed endless Time, and among creators, I am Brahma, the one with faces everywhere.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among letters, He is the letter 'A', which is the root of all sounds. Among grammatical compounds, He is the dual compound, which joins two equally important terms. He is indeed endless Time, which is continuous and indestructible. Among creators, He is Brahma, the one with faces everywhere, who is the creator of the universe. This indicates that the Lord is supremely present in the fundamental principles of language, grammar, time, and creation, proving His omnipresence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.33)

shloka_text: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम्। कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा।।10.34।।
translation: I am all-devouring Death, and I am also the origin of all things yet to be. Among feminine qualities, I am fame, prosperity, fine speech, memory, intelligence, courage, and forgiveness.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that He is all-devouring Death, symbolizing the end of life. He is also the origin of all things yet to be, indicating continuous creation. Among feminine qualities, He is fame, prosperity (beauty), fine speech, memory, intelligence, courage, and forgiveness. This indicates that the Lord is equally present in life and death, creation and destruction, and all excellent human qualities. His glory pervades every aspect of existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.34)

shloka_text: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम्। मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः।।10.35।।
translation: Among the hymns of the Sama Veda, I am the Brihatsama; among poetic meters, I am the Gayatri. Among the months, I am Margashirsha, and among seasons, I am spring.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among the hymns of the Sama Veda, He is the Brihatsama, which is extremely important and powerful. Among poetic meters, He is the Gayatri mantra, considered the essence of the Vedas and supremely sacred. Among the months, He is Margashirsha (November-December), which is considered auspicious and holy. Among seasons, He is spring, which symbolizes beauty, new life, and joy. This indicates that the Lord manifests Himself in the supreme aspects of Vedic knowledge, the cycle of time, and the most beautiful and auspicious aspects of nature.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.35)

shloka_text: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्। जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम्।।10.36।।
translation: Among cheats, I am gambling; among the splendid, I am splendor. I am victory, I am firm resolve, and I am also the virtue of the virtuous.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among cheats, He is gambling, which symbolizes illusory power. Among the splendid, He is splendor, the source of brilliance and influence. He is victory, symbolizing success and superiority. He is firm resolve, representing determination and unwavering willpower. Among virtuous persons, He is virtue, the foundation of purity and good qualities. This indicates that the Lord manifests His power and influence in every aspect of life, whether positive or negative.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.36)

shloka_text: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः। मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः।।10.37।।
translation: Among the Vrishnis, I am Vasudeva (Krishna); among the Pandavas, I am Dhananjaya (Arjuna). Among the sages, I am Vyasa, and among great thinkers, I am Ushana (Shukracharya).
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among the Vrishnis, He is Vasudeva (Krishna) Himself, which is His supreme identity. Among the Pandavas, He is Dhananjaya (Arjuna), who symbolizes His power and devotion. Among the sages, He is Vyasa, who compiled the Vedas and composed the Mahabharata. Among poets (wise thinkers), He is Ushana (Shukracharya), the guru of the demons and a great scholar. This indicates that the Lord manifests His special presence among His devotees, the wise, and great personalities.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.37)

shloka_text: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम्। मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम्।।10.38।।
translation: Among means of suppression, I am punishment; among those who seek victory, I am statesmanship. Among secrets, I am silence, and among the wise, I am knowledge.
meaning: Lord Krishna, describing His opulences, states that among means of suppression, He is punishment, which is necessary for maintaining justice and order. Among those who seek victory, He is statesmanship, which is the right path to achieve success. Among secrets, He is silence, symbolizing profound knowledge and inner peace. Among the wise, He is knowledge, representing the understanding of ultimate truth and discernment. This indicates that the Lord is present at the core of justice, success, confidentiality, and knowledge, which are essential for the functioning of creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.38)

shloka_text: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन। न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्।।10.39।।
translation: O Arjuna! Whatever is the generating seed of all living beings, that also am I. There is no moving or non-moving creature that can exist without Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna presents the ultimate and comprehensive essence of His supreme existence. He tells Arjuna that He is the generating seed of all living beings, from which everything originates. He clarifies that there is no moving or non-moving creature in this world that can exist without Him or be devoid of Him. This confirms His omnipresence and His being the fundamental cause of all creation. The Lord is the very foundation and life-force of all existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.39)

shloka_text: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप। एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया।।10.40।।
translation: O Parantapa! There is no end to My divine opulences. This extensive description of My glories has been declared by Me only in brief.
meaning: Lord Krishna addresses Arjuna, stating that there is no end to His divine opulences. Whatever He has described is merely a brief account of His glories. This indicates that the Lord's powers and splendors are infinite, and a complete description of them is impossible for anyone. This verse re-establishes the Lord's boundlessness and His infinite glory, allowing the devotee to experience His vastness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.40)

shloka_text: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा। तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम्।।10.41।।
translation: Whatever being is endowed with opulence, beauty, and power, know that to have sprung from a mere spark of My splendor.
meaning: Lord Krishna reveals an important principle to Arjuna. He states that whatever in this world is endowed with opulence, beauty, and power, know that to have originated from a mere spark of His splendor. This means that the ultimate source of all excellence, beauty, and power is the Lord Himself. No object or being is independent in its glory; rather, it is just a small fraction of the Lord's power. This verse clarifies the Lord's supremacy and His pervasiveness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.41)

shloka_text: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन। विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत्।।10.42।।
translation: Or, what is the need for you to know all these details, O Arjuna? I sustain this entire universe by merely a fraction of My being.
meaning: In conclusion to His Vibhuti Yoga, Lord Krishna tells Arjuna that there is no great need for him to know all these detailed descriptions. He clarifies that He sustains this entire universe by merely a small fraction of His power. This indicates that the Lord's true power and glory are so infinite that a complete description of them is impossible. This verse is the ultimate proof of the Lord's inconceivable power and His supreme existence, which is the foundation of all creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (10.42)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम्। यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम।।11.1।।
translation: Arjun said: Out of compassion for me, You have spoken these supremely confidential words concerning the spiritual self, by which my illusion has been dispelled.
meaning: Arjun expresses his gratitude to Shree Krishna, stating that his illusion has been dispelled by the Lord's teachings. This verse indicates Arjun's readiness to delve deeper into spiritual knowledge. Shree Krishna had previously imparted knowledge about the immortality of the soul and the path of Karma Yoga. Through this profound wisdom, Arjun's attachment and doubts regarding the war have vanished. He now desires to behold the Universal Form of God, marking the next stage in his spiritual evolution.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.1)

shloka_text: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया। त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम्।।11.2।।
translation: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the appearance and disappearance of all living beings, and also about Your inexhaustible glory.
meaning: Arjun recalls Shree Krishna's previous discourses where the Lord described the creation and dissolution of the universe. He acknowledges having heard in detail about the origin and end of all beings directly from the Lord. Furthermore, Arjun has assimilated the knowledge of Shree Krishna's eternal and imperishable glory. This indicates that Arjun has grasped the theoretical knowledge and now yearns for a direct, experiential realization. This verse highlights Arjun's profound curiosity and spiritual advancement.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.2)

shloka_text: एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर। द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम।।11.3।।
translation: O Supreme Lord, whatever You have spoken about Yourself is indeed true. O Purushottam, I desire to see Your divine, majestic form.
meaning: In this verse, Arjun affirms the truthfulness of Shree Krishna's words, acknowledging that everything the Lord has revealed about Himself is absolutely true. Arjun's desire is no longer limited to theoretical understanding; he now yearns for a direct vision of the Lord's divine, majestic form. This profound desire signifies his deep faith and complete surrender to the Supreme Being. Arjun's request marks a crucial turning point in his spiritual journey, as he eagerly anticipates experiencing the Universal Form of God. This vision will provide him with direct proof of the Lord's omnipresence and omnipotence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.3)

shloka_text: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो। योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम्।।11.4।।
translation: O Lord, if You think that I am capable of beholding that form, then, O Lord of all mystic powers, please reveal Your imperishable Self to me.
meaning: Arjun humbly requests Shree Krishna to reveal His Universal Form only if He deems Arjun worthy of beholding it. This demonstrates Arjun's humility and his complete submission to the Lord's will. He addresses the Lord as 'Yogeshwara,' signifying the master of all mystic powers. Arjun understands that only through the Lord's grace can such a transcendental vision be granted. This verse reveals Arjun's profound faith and his absolute trust in the Lord's omnipotence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.4)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः। नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च।।11.5।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: O Pārtha, behold My hundreds and thousands of various divine forms, of different colors and shapes.
meaning: Shree Krishna accepts Arjun's request and prepares to reveal His Universal Form. He instructs Arjun to behold His numerous, diverse, and divine forms. These forms are not just one, but hundreds and thousands, encompassing various colors and shapes. The Lord's statement indicates that His Universal Form is limitless and beyond human comprehension. This vision will provide Arjun with a direct experience of God's omnipresence and boundless power. This verse is a testament to the Lord's grace and His infinite glory.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.5)

shloka_text: पश्यादित्यान्वसून्रुद्रानश्िवनौ मरुतस्तथा। बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याऽश्चर्याणि भारत।।11.6।।
translation: O Bhārata, behold the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvinī Kumārs, and Maruts. See many wonders never revealed before.
meaning: Shree Krishna instructs Arjun to behold various deities and powers within His Universal Form. He mentions the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvinī Kumārs, and Maruts, who are prominent deities in the Vedic tradition. The Lord also states that Arjun will witness many astonishing forms never seen by anyone before. This indicates that the Universal Form of God is not merely a collection of deities but is far more expansive and wondrous. This vision will allow Arjun to experience the Lord's supremacy as the source of all cosmic powers.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.6)

shloka_text: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम्। मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि।।11.7।।
translation: O Guḍākeśha, behold now in My body the entire universe, with all its moving and non-moving beings, assembled together, and whatever else you desire to see.
meaning: Shree Krishna invites Arjun to behold the entire universe within His Universal Form. He declares that the whole cosmos, including all moving and non-moving beings, is situated in one place within His body. This signifies that the Lord is the foundation and support of all creation. Furthermore, the Lord assures Arjun that he can see anything else he desires within this form. This verse presents direct evidence of God's omnipresence and infinite power, where the entire universe is contained within a single part of Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.7)

shloka_text: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा। दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्।।11.8।।
translation: But you cannot see Me with these ordinary physical eyes. I give you divine vision; behold My majestic opulence.
meaning: Shree Krishna clarifies that His Universal Form cannot be perceived by ordinary human eyes. This form is so vast and transcendental that it requires a special spiritual capacity to behold. Therefore, the Lord bestows divine vision upon Arjun, enabling him to witness His majestic opulence. This divine vision is not merely an enhancement of physical eyes but a spiritual faculty granted by the Lord's grace. This verse indicates that the true vision of God's form is possible only through His causeless mercy, not solely through human endeavor.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.8)

shloka_text: सञ्जय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः। दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम्।।11.9।।
translation: Sañjaya said: O King, having spoken thus, the Supreme Lord of Yog, Hari, then displayed His supreme, majestic form to Pārtha.
meaning: Sañjaya informs Dhritarashtra that Shree Krishna, after granting divine vision to Arjun, revealed His Universal Form. He refers to Shree Krishna as 'Mahayogeshwara,' symbolizing His boundless yogic powers. This form was supremely majestic, visible only through the Lord's grace. Sañjaya's description indicates that he was able to witness the events on the battlefield through his divine vision. This verse highlights the Lord's omnipotence and the wondrous nature of His divine pastimes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.9)

shloka_text: अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम्। अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम्।।11.10।।
translation: (Arjun saw) a form with many mouths and eyes, displaying many wondrous sights, adorned with many divine ornaments, and holding many uplifted divine weapons.
meaning: Sañjaya now begins to describe the Universal Form as seen by Arjun. He states that the Lord's form possessed countless mouths and eyes, signifying its vastness and omnipresence. This form was filled with many wondrous sights, transcending ordinary imagination. The Lord was adorned with numerous divine ornaments and held many divine weapons, symbolizing His power and majesty. This description illustrates the limitless and awe-inspiring nature of the Lord's Universal Form, which fills Arjun with both fear and wonder.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.10)

shloka_text: दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम्। सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम्।।11.11।।
translation: (Arjun saw) the Lord wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, full of all wonders, unlimited, and with faces everywhere.
meaning: Sañjaya continues to describe the divine beauty and grandeur of the Universal Form. He states that the Lord was adorned with divine garlands and garments, and anointed with divine fragrances. This form was replete with all kinds of wonders, signifying its transcendental nature. The Lord was infinite, with faces in all directions, symbolizing His omnipresence and omniscience. This description represents an unforgettable and awe-inspiring experience for Arjun, providing him with a direct realization of the Lord's boundless glory.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.11)

shloka_text: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता। यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः।।11.12।।
translation: If the splendor of a thousand suns were to blaze forth simultaneously in the sky, that might perhaps resemble the effulgence of that great being.
meaning: Sañjaya describes the astonishing radiance and brilliance of the Universal Form. He states that if a thousand suns were to rise simultaneously in the sky, their combined light would still barely compare to the effulgence of that great being. This simile illustrates the inconceivable luminosity and grandeur of the Lord's Universal Form. This radiance was so intense that it could be unbearable for ordinary human senses. This verse powerfully conveys the boundless power of the Lord and the glory of His divine presence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.12)

shloka_text: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा। अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा।।11.13।।
translation: At that time, Arjun, the son of Pāṇḍu, saw the entire universe, with its many divisions, all situated in one place within the body of the God of gods.
meaning: Sañjaya describes what Arjun witnessed within the Universal Form. Arjun saw the entire universe, with all its diverse divisions, situated in one place within the body of the God of gods. This universe encompassed all realms, beings, and events. This vision provided Arjun with a direct experience of the Lord's omnipresence and His inseparable connection with creation. This verse illustrates the boundless power of the Lord and the grandeur of His cosmic presence, where everything is contained within Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.13)

shloka_text: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः। प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत।।11.14।।
translation: Then, Dhananjaya (Arjun), filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the Lord, and with folded hands, he spoke.
meaning: Sañjaya describes Arjun's reaction upon witnessing the Universal Form of the Lord. Arjun was filled with wonder and fear by this astonishing vision, and his hair stood on end. Following this awe-inspiring experience, he immediately bowed his head to the Lord and, with folded hands, addressed Him. This reaction signifies Arjun's profound reverence and awe towards the Lord's boundless power and grandeur. This verse indicates that the Universal Form of God was so impactful that it completely overwhelmed Arjun.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.14)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान्। ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थ मृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान्।।11.15।।
translation: Arjun said: O Lord, I behold all the gods within Your body, as well as hosts of various beings. I see Brahmā seated on the lotus, Lord Shiva, all the sages, and the divine serpents.
meaning: Arjun begins to describe the Universal Form he has witnessed. He states that he saw all the gods and hosts of various beings within the Lord's body. Specifically, he beheld Brahmā seated on the lotus, Lord Shiva, all the great sages, and the divine serpents. This description is direct evidence of the Lord's omnipresence and the containment of all creation within Him. Arjun's statement indicates that the Lord is the ultimate source and refuge of the entire universe. This vision further deepens Arjun's boundless reverence and awe towards the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.15)

shloka_text: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम्। नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप।।11.16।।
translation: O Lord of the universe, O Universal Form, I behold You with infinite arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes, with infinite forms on all sides. I see neither Your end, nor Your middle, nor Your beginning.
meaning: Arjun describes the infinitude and omnipresence of the Lord's Universal Form. He states that the Lord possesses countless arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes, signifying His boundless nature. Arjun perceives neither the beginning, middle, nor end of the Lord, making it clear that this form transcends the limitations of time and space. He addresses the Lord as 'Vishveshwara' and 'Vishwarupa,' denoting His cosmic sovereignty. This description evokes deep awe in Arjun's mind regarding the Lord's inconceivable vastness and His supreme transcendence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.16)

shloka_text: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च तेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम्। पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम्।।11.17।।
translation: I behold You crowned, bearing a mace and a disc, a mass of splendor, shining brilliantly on all sides. I see You difficult to look upon, like blazing fire and the sun, immeasurable in Your effulgence.
meaning: Arjun describes the radiance and grandeur of the Lord's Universal Form. He sees the Lord adorned with a crown, mace, and disc, symbolizing His regal power and sovereignty. This form of the Lord is a mass of splendor, shining brilliantly from all directions, making it exceedingly difficult to behold. His effulgence is like blazing fire and thousands of suns, indicating His inconceivable power. This form is immeasurable, meaning its glory cannot be estimated. This description highlights the boundless power of the Lord and the awe-inspiring nature of His divine presence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.17)

shloka_text: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्। त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे।।11.18।।
translation: You are the imperishable, the supreme object of knowledge. You are the supreme support of this universe. You are the eternal protector of the everlasting dharma, and You are the primeval Divine Person—this is my conviction.
meaning: Arjun, upon witnessing the Universal Form, acknowledges the Lord's true identity. He declares that the Lord is the imperishable, the supreme knowable truth. He is the ultimate support and foundation of this entire universe. Arjun recognizes the Lord as the imperishable, the protector of eternal dharma, and the primeval Divine Person. This statement reflects Arjun's profound spiritual insight and his complete faith in the Lord. This verse establishes the Lord's supremacy, His eternal nature, and His role as the guardian of righteousness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.18)

shloka_text: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य मनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम्। पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम् स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम्।।11.19।।
translation: I behold You without beginning, middle, or end, possessing infinite power, with countless arms, the moon and sun as Your eyes. I see You with a mouth like blazing fire, scorching this entire universe with Your own effulgence.
meaning: Arjun continues to describe the boundless nature and power of the Lord's Universal Form. He states that the Lord has no beginning, middle, or end, signifying His eternal existence. He possesses infinite valor and countless arms, with the moon and sun serving as His eyes. The Lord's mouth resembles blazing fire, and He is scorching the entire universe with His own effulgence. This description illustrates the Lord's omnipotence, His cosmic presence, and His fierce radiance, which fills Arjun with both fear and awe.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.19)

shloka_text: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः। दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन्।।11.20।।
translation: O Great One, this entire space between heaven and earth, and all directions, are pervaded by You alone. Seeing this wondrous and terrible form of Yours, the three worlds are trembling with fear.
meaning: Arjun describes the Lord's omnipresence and the impact of His Universal Form. He states that the entire space between heaven and earth, along with all directions, is pervaded by the Lord alone. This signifies His boundless presence. Upon witnessing this wondrous and terrible form of the Lord, the three worlds are trembling with fear. This reaction indicates the awe and terror inspired by the Lord's immense power and cosmic form. Arjun's statement establishes the Lord's supremacy and His inconceivable might.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.20)

shloka_text: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घाः विशन्ति केचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति। स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाः स्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः।।11.21।।
translation: Indeed, these hosts of gods are entering You, and some, struck with fear, are praising You with folded hands. The assemblies of great sages and perfected beings, uttering 'Svasti' (all hail), are extolling You with abundant hymns.
meaning: Arjun describes the reactions of various beings within the Universal Form. He observes hosts of gods entering the Lord, while some, struck with fear, are praising Him with folded hands. Assemblies of great sages and perfected beings, uttering 'Svasti' (all hail), are extolling the Lord with abundant hymns. This scene illustrates that the Lord is the center of all creation, sustenance, and dissolution. This verse reveals the Lord's supremacy and the natural reverence and awe that all beings in all realms feel towards Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.21)

shloka_text: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या विश्वेऽश्िवनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च। गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घा वीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे।।11.22।।
translation: The Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Vishvadevas, Ashvinī Kumārs, Maruts, and the ancestors, as well as the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas—all are beholding You in wonder.
meaning: Arjun provides a detailed description of the various divine entities present within the Lord's Universal Form. He mentions the Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Vishvadevas, Ashvinī Kumārs, Maruts, and the ancestors. Additionally, hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas are also beholding the Lord in wonder. This indicates that the Lord's Universal Form encompasses the entire cosmic order and its inhabitants. All beings, whether gods, sages, or others, are filled with awe upon witnessing this magnificent manifestation of the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.22)

shloka_text: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम्। बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम्।।11.23।।
translation: O mighty-armed Lord, seeing Your magnificent form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many stomachs, and terrifying with many teeth, all the worlds are trembling with fear, and so am I.
meaning: Arjun describes the terrifying aspect of the Lord's Universal Form. He states that this magnificent form of the Lord possesses countless mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, feet, and stomachs. Particularly, it appears exceedingly terrifying due to its numerous teeth. Witnessing this formidable form, all the worlds are trembling with fear, and Arjun himself is greatly terrified. This description illustrates the Lord's destructive power and His aspect as Time, symbolizing the end of creation. Arjun's fear is a natural human reaction to the Lord's boundless might.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.23)

shloka_text: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम्। दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो।।11.24।।
translation: O Vishnu, seeing You touching the sky, effulgent, with many colors, with open mouths and blazing, enormous eyes, my inner self is trembling with fear. I find neither firmness nor mental peace.
meaning: Arjun describes the formidable and terrifying aspect of the Lord's Universal Form. He states that the Lord's form touches the sky, is effulgent, and possesses many colors. His mouths are open, and His eyes are blazing and enormous, appearing exceedingly dreadful. Witnessing this form, Arjun's inner self is trembling with fear, and he has lost both firmness and mental peace. This indicates that the Lord's form is so overwhelming that it is disturbing Arjun's mind. Arjun's reaction highlights his human vulnerability in the face of the Lord's boundless power and cosmic manifestation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.24)

shloka_text: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि दृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि। दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास।।11.25।।
translation: Seeing Your mouths, terrifying with teeth and resembling the fire of annihilation, I lose my sense of direction and find no peace. O Lord of lords, O refuge of the universe, be merciful to me.
meaning: Arjun describes the most terrifying aspects of the Lord's Universal Form. He states that the Lord's mouths, with their teeth, appear exceedingly dreadful and resemble the fire of annihilation. Witnessing this sight, Arjun has lost his sense of direction and finds no peace whatsoever. Addressing the Lord as 'Devesha' and 'Jagannivasa,' he implores Him to be pleased and show mercy. This verse highlights Arjun's extreme fear and his intense desire for the Lord to return to His gentle, familiar form.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.25)

shloka_text: अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राः सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः। भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौ सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः।।11.26।।
translation: All the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of kings, Bhishma, Drona, and that son of Suta (Karna), as well as the chief warriors from our side, are all entering You.
meaning: Arjun witnesses a terrifying vision of the war's future within the Universal Form. He sees all the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with their allied kings, entering the Lord's mouths. Great warriors like Bhishma, Drona, and Karna are similarly being absorbed into the Lord. He even observes some chief warriors from his own side meeting the same fate. This vision clarifies to Arjun that the outcome of the war is already predetermined, and all warriors will meet their end within the Lord. This verse confirms the Lord's aspect as Time, the destroyer of all.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.26)

shloka_text: वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि। केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु संदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः।।11.27।।
translation: All of them are swiftly entering Your mouths, which are terrifying with teeth and exceedingly fearsome. Some are seen stuck between Your teeth, with their heads crushed.
meaning: Arjun provides a more terrifying description of the destructive aspect of the Universal Form. He observes warriors swiftly entering the Lord's dreadful, tooth-filled mouths. Some warriors are seen stuck between the teeth, with their heads crushed. This scene vividly portrays the ferocity of war and the destruction it entails. It highlights the ruthlessness and inevitability of the Lord's aspect as Time, where no one can escape death. This experience makes Arjun realize the true outcome of the war and the supreme power of the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.27)

shloka_text: यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाः समुद्रमेवाभिमुखाः द्रवन्ति। तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति।।11.28।।
translation: As the many currents of rivers naturally flow towards the ocean, so too are these heroes of the human world entering Your blazing mouths.
meaning: Arjun uses a powerful simile to describe the inevitable outcome of the war. He states that just as the many currents of rivers naturally flow towards and merge into the ocean, so too are all these heroes of the human world entering the Lord's blazing mouths. This analogy illustrates that death is an undeniable truth, and no one can escape it. The Lord's Universal Form symbolizes Time, which absorbs all beings into itself. This verse expresses the inevitability of war and the Lord's destructive power with great clarity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.28)

shloka_text: यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः। तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः।।11.29।।
translation: As moths swiftly enter a blazing fire to perish, so too are these people rapidly entering Your mouths for their destruction.
meaning: Arjun uses another poignant simile to illustrate the inevitability of destruction. He states that just as moths swiftly plunge into a blazing fire for their annihilation, so too are all these warriors rapidly entering the Lord's mouths. This analogy signifies that all beings involved in the war, regardless of their power, are moving towards their predetermined end. It highlights the irresistible power of the Lord's aspect as Time, against which no resistance is possible. Arjun's observation makes him realize the futility of war and the supreme authority of the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.29)

shloka_text: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ता ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः। तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं भासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो।।11.30।।
translation: O Vishnu, You are licking up, devouring all the worlds on all sides with Your blazing mouths. Your fierce rays are scorching the entire universe, filling it with Your effulgence.
meaning: Arjun describes the destructive action of the Lord's Universal Form. He states that the Lord is licking up and devouring all the worlds on all sides with His blazing mouths. This scene illustrates the ferocity of the Lord's aspect as Time, which consumes everything. The entire universe is filled and scorched by the Lord's fierce effulgence, creating an atmosphere of fear and destruction. This verse very clearly expresses the boundless power of the Lord and the terrifying nature of His cosmic destructive form. Arjun's experience provides him with a direct realization of the Lord's supreme authority.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.30)

shloka_text: आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद। विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम्।।11.31।।
translation: Tell me who You are, with this fierce form. Salutations to You, O best of gods, be merciful. I wish to know You, the primeval one, for I do not comprehend Your workings.
meaning: Arjun, overwhelmed by fear and awe, asks the Lord about His true identity. Terrified by the Lord's fierce form, he implores Him for mercy. Arjun wishes to know who this primeval being is, as he cannot comprehend the Lord's actions and workings. This question reflects Arjun's spiritual curiosity and the profound doubt that has arisen in his mind. This verse highlights the inconceivable power of the Lord and the limitations of human understanding in grasping His mysteries.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.31)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः। ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः।।11.32।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, and I have come forth to annihilate all people here. Even without you, all the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist.
meaning: Shree Krishna answers Arjun's question by revealing His true identity. He declares that He is Time, the great destroyer of worlds, who has manifested to annihilate all. The Lord clarifies that the outcome of the war is already predetermined, and even without Arjun's participation, all opposing warriors will be destroyed. This statement illustrates the Lord's supreme authority and His cosmic plan. Arjun must understand that he is merely an instrument, and the Lord's will is paramount.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.32)

shloka_text: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व जित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम्। मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेव निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन्।।11.33।।
translation: Therefore, arise, gain glory, conquer your enemies, and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. Indeed, all these have already been slain by Me. O Savyasāchin (Arjun, the ambidextrous archer), be merely an instrument.
meaning: The Lord encourages Arjun to fight, as the outcome is already predetermined. He instructs Arjun to arise, gain glory, conquer his enemies, and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. Shree Krishna clarifies that all the warriors have already been slain by Him, and Arjun is merely to be an instrument. This statement reinforces the principle of Karma Yoga, where one must perform their duty without attachment to the results. Arjun needs to understand that he is a part of the Lord's plan and must fulfill his designated role.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.33)

shloka_text: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च कर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान्। मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान्।।11.34।।
translation: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and other brave warriors, who have already been slain by Me, you should kill. Do not be disturbed; fight, and you shall certainly conquer your enemies in battle.
meaning: Shree Krishna names the prominent warriors whom He has already slain. He mentions Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna, who were among the most powerful figures in the war. The Lord instructs Arjun to kill these already vanquished warriors and not to be disturbed. He assures Arjun that he will fight and certainly conquer his enemies. This statement is intended to remove doubt and fear from Arjun's mind, enabling him to perform his duty without hesitation. This verse demonstrates the Lord's omnipotence and His unwavering support for His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.34)

shloka_text: सञ्जय उवाच एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी। नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं सगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य।।11.35।।
translation: Sañjaya said: Having heard these words of Keshava, Kirīṭī (Arjun), with folded hands, trembling, overwhelmed with fear, bowed down and again spoke to Krishna in a faltering voice.
meaning: Sañjaya describes Arjun's reaction upon hearing the Lord's words about His aspect as Time. Arjun, the crowned one (Kirīṭī), trembled with fear upon hearing Keshava's words. With folded hands, overwhelmed by terror, he bowed down to the Lord and then spoke to Him in a faltering voice. This indicates that the Lord's Universal Form and His words had a profound impact on Arjun. Arjun's fear is a natural human reaction to the Lord's boundless power and His cosmic destructive form.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.35)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या जगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च। रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः।।11.36।।
translation: Arjun said: O Hrishikesha, it is indeed fitting that the world rejoices and is enamored by Your glory. The demons, struck with fear, are fleeing in all directions, and all the hosts of perfected beings are bowing down to You.
meaning: Arjun glorifies the Lord, stating that it is indeed fitting that the entire world rejoices and is enamored by His glory. He observes that demons, struck with fear, are fleeing in all directions, while all hosts of perfected beings are bowing down to the Lord. This indicates that virtuous beings rejoice in the Lord's presence, while evil forces flee in terror. This verse establishes the Lord's supremacy and His righteous rule, where dharma is protected and adharma is vanquished.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.36)

shloka_text: कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन् गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे। अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास त्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत्।।11.37।।
translation: O Great One, why should they not bow down to You, who are the original creator even of Brahmā, and greater than him? O Infinite One, O Lord of the devatās, O refuge of the universe, You are the imperishable, that which is beyond both manifest and unmanifest.
meaning: Arjun acknowledges the Lord's supremacy and His unique position. He questions why anyone would not bow down to Him, who is the original creator even of Brahmā and greater than him. He addresses the Lord as Infinite, Lord of the devatās, and refuge of the universe, signifying His omnipresence and omnipotence. Arjun also states that the Lord is the imperishable, the ultimate truth beyond both the manifest and unmanifest. This verse establishes the Lord's identity as the Supreme Brahman, the cause of all causes, and beyond all existences.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.37)

shloka_text: त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराण स्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम्। वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप।।11.38।।
translation: You are the original Divine God, the primeval Person. You are the supreme resting place of this universe. You are the knower, the object of knowledge, and the supreme abode. O infinite-formed one, this entire universe is pervaded by You.
meaning: Arjun further describes the Lord's supreme existence. He refers to the Lord as the original Divine God and the primeval Person, signifying His eternality and supremacy. The Lord is the ultimate refuge and foundation of this entire universe. Arjun also states that the Lord is the knower, the object of knowledge, and the supreme abode (goal).
