O infinite-formed one, this entire universe is pervaded by Him, proving His omnipresence. This verse further confirms the Lord's identity as the Supreme Brahman, the cause of all knowledge and existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.38)

shloka_text: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कः प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च। नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वः पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते।।11.39।।
translation: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the Moon, Prajāpati, and the great-grandfather. Salutations, salutations to You a thousand times, and again and again, salutations to You!
meaning: Arjun further clarifies the Lord's omnipresence by stating that He is Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the Moon, Prajāpati, and even the great-grandfather of Brahmā. This indicates that all deities and cosmic powers are merely different forms or manifestations of the Lord. Arjun offers salutations to the Lord a thousand times and repeatedly expresses his reverence. This demonstrates his complete surrender and boundless devotion to the Lord. This verse establishes the Lord's supremacy and the containment of all cosmic powers within Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.39)

shloka_text: नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व। अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः।।11.40।।
translation: Salutations to You from the front, and then from behind. Salutations to You from all sides, O All-pervading One. You possess infinite power and immeasurable valor. You pervade everything, and therefore, You are everything.
meaning: Arjun offers salutations to the Lord from all directions, signifying His omnipresence. He states that the Lord pervades from the front, from behind, and from all sides, hence salutations are offered to Him from every direction. The Lord possesses infinite power and immeasurable valor, which indicates His boundless might. Arjun concludes that the Lord pervades everything, and therefore, He is everything. This verse establishes the Lord's identity as the Supreme Brahman, the origin and essence of all existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.40)

shloka_text: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति। अजानता महिमानं तवेदं मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि।।11.41।।
translation: Thinking You to be a friend, whatever I have presumptuously said, addressing You as 'O Krishna,' 'O Yadava,' 'O my dear friend,' not knowing this Your majesty, either out of negligence or out of affection.
meaning: Arjun apologizes to the Lord for his past ignorance and informality. He admits that, considering the Lord merely a friend and unaware of His true majesty, he presumptuously addressed Him as 'O Krishna,' 'O Yadava,' or 'O my dear friend,' either out of negligence or affection. This indicates that after witnessing the Universal Form, Arjun has gained a complete realization of the Lord's supremacy. This verse expresses Arjun's deep reverence for the Lord and his repentance, as he acknowledges his past errors.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.41)

shloka_text: यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु। एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम्।।11.42।।
translation: And whatever disrespect I have shown You, for the sake of humor, while at play, resting, sitting, or eating, either alone or in the presence of others, O Infallible One, I beg forgiveness from You, the Immeasurable One, for all that.
meaning: Arjun offers a detailed apology for his past informality and disrespect. He admits that he has shown disrespect to the Lord, even humorously, while playing, resting, sitting, or eating, whether alone or in the presence of others. Addressing the Lord as 'Achyuta' and 'Aprameya,' he begs forgiveness for all those transgressions. This verse demonstrates Arjun's humility, repentance, and his complete surrender to the Lord. It also highlights his newfound understanding of the Lord's majesty.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.42)

shloka_text: पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान्। न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्यो लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव।।11.43।।
translation: You are the father of this moving and non-moving world, and You are its worshipable Guru, greater than all gurus. O You of incomparable power, there is none equal to You in the three worlds, so how can there be anyone greater?
meaning: Arjun acknowledges the Lord's unparalleled supremacy. He declares that the Lord is the father of this moving and non-moving world, its worshipable Guru, and greater than all gurus. Arjun firmly states that there is none equal to the Lord in the three worlds, and therefore, no one can be greater than Him. This statement establishes the Lord's identity as the Supreme Brahman, the origin of all relationships and the source of all powers. This verse highlights the Lord's boundless power, knowledge, and glory, which are beyond comparison.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.43)

shloka_text: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम्। पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युः प्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम्।।11.44।।
translation: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I implore Your grace, O adorable Lord. O Lord, You should forgive my offenses, just as a father forgives his son, a friend his friend, and a lover his beloved.
meaning: Arjun begs forgiveness from the Lord for his transgressions and implores His grace. He prostrates his body, bowing down, and seeks mercy from the adorable Lord. Arjun requests the Lord to forgive his offenses, just as a father forgives his son, a friend his friend, and a lover his beloved. This verse demonstrates Arjun's complete surrender, humility, and profound love for the Lord. It also highlights the Lord's compassion and His affectionate disposition towards His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.44)

shloka_text: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे। तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपं प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास।।11.45।।
translation: Having seen that which was never seen before, I am indeed joyful, yet my mind is trembling with fear. O Lord, please show me that very (four-armed) form. O God of gods, O abode of the universe, be pleased.
meaning: Arjun describes the conflicting emotions within his mind. He states that he is joyful to have seen the Universal Form, which he had never witnessed before, yet his mind is trembling with fear. Due to this fear and awe, he requests the Lord to return to His gentle, four-armed form. Addressing the Lord as 'Devesha' and 'Jagannivasa,' he implores Him to be pleased. This verse indicates that although the Universal Form was astonishing, Arjun prefers the Lord's calm and familiar form.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.45)

shloka_text: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव। तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते।।11.46।।
translation: I wish to see You in Your crowned, mace-bearing, and disc-in-hand form. O thousand-armed one, O Universal Form, please appear in that same four-armed form.
meaning: Arjun explicitly requests the Lord to return to His familiar four-armed form. He wishes to see the Lord adorned with a crown, mace, and disc, which are the distinguishing features of His Vishnu form. Even while addressing the Lord as 'Sahasrabāho' and 'Vishvamūrte,' Arjun prays for Him to assume His gentle form. This indicates that a devotee prefers the personal, loving form of the Lord, even if they understand the glory of His Universal Form. This verse highlights the sweet relationship between the Lord and His devotee.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.46)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात्। तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम्।।11.47।।
translation: The Blessed Lord said: O Arjun, being pleased with you, I have shown you, by My Yogmaya power, this supreme, effulgent, cosmic, unlimited, and primeval form, which no one other than you has ever seen before.
meaning: Shree Krishna assures Arjun that He has revealed this wondrous Universal Form to him out of His pleasure and through His Yogmaya power. He explains that this form is supreme, effulgent, cosmic, unlimited, and primeval. The Lord also clarifies that no one other than Arjun has ever seen this form before. This indicates that this vision was a result of the Lord's special grace, which can only be attained by His dear devotee. This verse highlights the Lord's boundless power and His special love for His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.47)

shloka_text: न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः। एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोके द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर।।11.48।।
translation: O best of the Kuru warriors, in this human world, I cannot be seen in this form by anyone other than you, neither through Vedic study, nor sacrifices, nor charity, nor pious deeds, nor severe austerities.
meaning: Shree Krishna emphasizes the rarity of beholding the Universal Form. He states that in this human world, this form cannot be seen by anyone other than Arjun, neither through Vedic study, nor sacrifices, nor charity, nor pious deeds, nor severe austerities. This indicates that the Lord's form is attained only through His causeless mercy and pure devotion. This verse highlights the limitations of rituals, knowledge, and austerities, establishing the supremacy of devotion. The Lord's grace is the sole path to true vision.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.48)

shloka_text: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम्। व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वं तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य।।11.49।।
translation: Let neither distress nor bewilderment be yours upon seeing this terrible form of Mine. Free from fear and with a cheerful mind, behold again that very (gentle) form of Mine.
meaning: Shree Krishna instructs Arjun to free himself from fear and bewilderment. He assures Arjun that he should neither be distressed nor bewildered by seeing His terrible form. The Lord directs Arjun to behold His gentle form again, free from fear and with a cheerful mind. This indicates that the Lord is extremely compassionate towards His devotees and respects their feelings. This verse highlights the Lord's affectionate nature, where He desires to make His devotee feel calm and at ease.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.49)

shloka_text: सञ्जय उवाच इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः। आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं भूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा।।11.50।।
translation: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjun, Vāsudeva again displayed His personal (four-armed) form. And then, the compassionate Mahātmā (Shree Krishna), assuming His gentle (two-armed) form, consoled the frightened Arjun.
meaning: Sañjaya informs Dhritarashtra about Shree Krishna's actions to console Arjun. Having spoken thus to Arjun, Vāsudeva first displayed His four-armed form, and then the compassionate Mahātmā (Shree Krishna) assumed His gentle, two-armed human form. In this way, He consoled the frightened Arjun and made him feel at ease. This demonstrates how much the Lord cares for the feelings of His devotees and fulfills their desires. This verse highlights the Lord's compassion and His love for His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.50)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन। इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः।।11.51।।
translation: Arjun said: O Janārdana, seeing this gentle human form of Yours, I am now composed in mind and have returned to my natural state.
meaning: Arjun expresses his relief upon seeing the Lord's gentle human form. He states that upon witnessing this form, his mind has become composed, and he has returned to his natural state. This indicates that the Lord's gentle form provides peace and comfort to devotees, whereas the Universal Form evokes fear and awe. Arjun's statement highlights his deep intimacy and love for the Lord's personal form. This verse demonstrates the Lord's grace and His affectionate disposition towards His devotees.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.51)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम। देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः।।11.52।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: This form of Mine, which you have seen, is exceedingly difficult to behold. Even the gods constantly long to see this form.
meaning: Shree Krishna informs Arjun about the rarity of the Universal Form he has witnessed. He states that this form is exceedingly difficult to behold, and even the gods constantly long to see it. This indicates that Arjun has received an experience, through the Lord's special grace, that is rare even for the deities. This verse highlights the Lord's glory and the uniqueness of His Universal Form. It also signifies Arjun's spiritual importance and his special relationship with the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.52)

shloka_text: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया। शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा।।11.53।।
translation: As you have seen Me, in this form I cannot be seen by Vedic study, nor by severe penances, nor by charity, nor by worship.
meaning: Shree Krishna reiterates that His Universal Form cannot be attained merely through material or ritualistic endeavors. He states that the vision Arjun has received cannot be achieved through Vedic study, nor severe penances, nor charity, nor sacrifices. This verse clarifies the limitations of knowledge, action, and austerity, indicating that the true vision of the Lord's form is possible only through His causeless mercy. It points towards the supremacy of devotion as the sole path to please the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.53)

shloka_text: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन। ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप।।11.54।।
translation: O scorcher of foes, Arjun, in this form I can be truly known, seen, and entered into (union with Me) only through unalloyed devotion.
meaning: Shree Krishna clarifies how true knowledge and experience of His Universal Form can be attained. He states that such a vision and union with Him are possible only through unalloyed devotion. 'Unalloyed devotion' means being solely dedicated to the Lord without any other desires or motives. This verse establishes the supremacy of Bhakti Yoga, where pure love and surrender are the only means to know, see, and enter into the Lord. It explains the importance of devotion to Arjun, which is superior to all other spiritual practices.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.54)

shloka_text: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः। निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव।।11.55।।
translation: O Pāṇḍava, one who performs actions for My sake, considers Me the Supreme Goal, is devoted to Me, is free from attachment, and bears no malice towards any being—such a person comes to Me.
meaning: Shree Krishna summarizes the path of devotion, explaining who can attain Him. He states that a person who performs actions for His sake, considers Him the Supreme Goal, is devoted to Him, is free from attachment, and bears no malice towards any being, such a person attains Him. This verse highlights the importance of selfless action, unalloyed devotion, detachment, and benevolence towards all beings. It presents a complete and balanced spiritual path for attaining the Lord. This is one of the central messages of the Bhagavad Gita, outlining the path to liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (11.55)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते।येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः।।12.1।।
translation: Arjuna said: Of those devotees who are ever steadfastly engaged in Your worship, and of those who worship the imperishable, unmanifested Brahman, who are the more perfect yogis?
meaning: Arjuna posed this question to Lord Krishna, seeking to understand which path, devotion to the personal God or meditation on the impersonal Brahman, is superior. He wished to know who among those who worship the manifest form and those who contemplate the unmanifest Brahman are considered more perfect yogis. This inquiry is crucial for clarifying the distinction between Bhakti Yoga and Jnana Yoga. Arjuna's curiosity reflects the natural human tendency to seek clarity in spiritual pursuits. Lord Krishna will address this question in the subsequent verses, illuminating the significance of both paths.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.1)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः।।12.2।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me and always engage in My worship with supreme faith, them I consider to be the most perfect in Yoga.
meaning: Lord Krishna clearly states here that the path of Saguna Bhakti, or devotion to the personal God, is supremely excellent. He declares that those devotees who fix their minds on Him and constantly worship Him are the most perfect yogis. Such devotion requires dedicating one's mind and intellect entirely to the Lord. This path is characterized by supreme faith and love, which brings the practitioner closer to God. The Lord Himself considers such devotees to be the best, as they directly connect with Him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.2)

shloka_text: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते।सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम्।।12.3।।
translation: But those who worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, the unthinkable, the unchanging, the immovable, and the eternal Brahman—
meaning: This verse describes the practitioners who worship the unmanifest Brahman. They meditate upon the indefinable, unmanifest, and all-pervading Brahman, which cannot be grasped by the senses. Such practitioners keep their senses completely under control and maintain equanimity towards all beings. They strive to merge into the unchanging, eternal, and immovable Brahman. This path is extremely difficult and subtle, requiring the mind to focus on the formless. It is the path of Jnana Yoga, leading to self-realization.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.3)

shloka_text: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः।ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः।।12.4।।
translation: (Those who) restraining all their senses, being even-minded everywhere, and engaged in the welfare of all beings, they too attain Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna clarifies here that even the worshipers of the unmanifest Brahman ultimately attain Him. Such practitioners keep their senses completely controlled and maintain equanimity in all situations. They remain engaged in the welfare of all beings, which demonstrates their sense of universal love. Although their path is that of impersonal worship, the fruit of their spiritual practice is indeed the attainment of God. This indicates that different spiritual paths ultimately lead to the same Supreme Truth.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.4)

shloka_text: क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम्। अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते।।12.5।।
translation: The struggle of those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest is much greater, for the path to the unmanifest is very difficult for embodied beings to achieve.
meaning: Lord Krishna here clarifies the difficulty of the path of impersonal worship. He states that those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest Brahman face greater tribulations. It is exceedingly difficult for embodied beings to meditate on the formless Brahman. The mind naturally seeks to focus on a form or shape, making concentration on the formless challenging. This verse highlights the practical difficulties of the path of impersonal devotion compared to personal devotion.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.5)

shloka_text: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः।अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते।।12.6।।
translation: But those who dedicate all their actions to Me, regarding Me as the supreme goal, and worship Me, meditating on Me with exclusive devotion—
meaning: This verse describes the simplicity and effectiveness of the path of personal devotion. Lord Krishna states that those devotees who dedicate all their actions to Him are extremely dear to Him. Such devotees consider God as their supreme goal and worship Him with exclusive devotion. They constantly meditate on the Lord and dedicate their lives to His service. This path is more accessible and joyful for embodied beings, as it involves a sense of love and relationship.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.6)

shloka_text: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात्।भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम्।।12.7।।
translation: O son of Pritha, for those whose minds are fixed on Me, I swiftly become their deliverer from the ocean of birth and death.
meaning: Lord Krishna assures His devotees here that He will swiftly deliver them. He states that for those devotees who fix their minds on Him, He Himself becomes their deliverer from the ocean of birth and death. This demonstrates the Lord's boundless compassion and love for His devotees. This verse contains the Lord's promise to free His surrendered devotees from all miseries. It reveals the supreme glory of the path of devotion, where God Himself becomes the deliverer.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.7)

shloka_text: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय।निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः।।12.8।।
translation: Fix your mind on Me alone, and surrender your intellect to Me. Thereafter, you will reside in Me alone; there is no doubt about this.
meaning: Lord Krishna here explains the essence of Bhakti Yoga. He instructs Arjuna to completely surrender his mind and intellect to Him. Fixing the mind on the Lord's personal form and engaging the intellect in His divine knowledge is true devotion. Through such complete surrender, the practitioner begins to reside in God alone. This is the Lord's unwavering promise that such a devotee will never be separated from Him. This verse highlights the importance of complete surrender.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.8)

shloka_text: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय।।12.9।।
translation: O Dhananjaya, if you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me, then seek to attain Me through the yoga of repeated practice.
meaning: Lord Krishna here suggests an alternative path for those practitioners who cannot immediately fix their minds on Him. He states that if it is difficult to concentrate the mind, one should resort to Abhyasa Yoga, or the yoga of practice. Abhyasa Yoga means engaging the mind in God through continuous effort and repetition. This gradually trains the mind and leads it towards concentration. This verse indicates that perseverance and patience are essential for spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.9)

shloka_text: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव।मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि।।12.10।।
translation: If you are unable even to practice, then be intent on performing actions for My sake. By performing actions for My sake, you shall attain perfection.
meaning: Lord Krishna here describes another simpler path, if even the yoga of practice seems difficult. He states that in such a case, one should become intent on performing actions for His sake. This means performing all actions as service to God, without any desire for personal results. When actions are dedicated to God, they become purified and lead the practitioner towards perfection. This is the principle of Karma Yoga, where liberation can be achieved by connecting actions with devotion.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.10)

shloka_text: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः।सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान्।।12.11।।
translation: If you are unable to even do this, then taking refuge in My Yoga, control your mind and renounce the fruits of all actions.
meaning: Lord Krishna presents yet another option here, for those who cannot follow the preceding paths. He states that if it is not possible to even perform actions for God, then one should practice renunciation of the fruits of all actions. This means performing actions but abandoning attachment to their results. This is the path of self-control and non-attachment, which calms the mind. By renouncing the fruits of actions, one gradually becomes free from ego and desires, thereby attaining inner peace.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.11)

shloka_text: श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते।ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम्।।12.12।।
translation: Better indeed is knowledge than mechanical practice; better than knowledge is meditation; better than meditation is renunciation of the fruits of actions, for immediately after renunciation, peace is attained.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna outlines the hierarchy of different levels of spiritual progress. He states that knowledge is superior to mere mechanical practice, as knowledge provides the right direction. Meditation is superior to knowledge, because meditation concentrates the mind and provides inner experience. Renunciation of the fruits of actions is superior to meditation, as it eliminates attachment. Immediately after the renunciation of action's fruits, supreme peace is attained, which is the end of all suffering.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.12)

shloka_text: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी।।12.13।।
translation: One who bears no malice towards any being, who is friendly and compassionate to all, free from attachment to possessions and egoism, equipoised in happiness and distress, and forgiving—
meaning: This verse begins to describe the qualities of a devotee dear to the Lord. Such a devotee is free from malice towards all beings and is a friend and compassionate to everyone. He has no attachment to any possession and is free from egoism, understanding himself as distinct from the body. He remains equipoised in both happiness and distress, undisturbed by either. Furthermore, he is always forgiving, pardoning the mistakes of others.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.13)

shloka_text: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः।मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः।।12.14।।
translation: One who is always contented, a yogi, self-controlled, firm in conviction, and who has dedicated his mind and intellect to Me—such a devotee is very dear to Me.
meaning: The Lord here describes other qualities of His dear devotee. Such a devotee is always contented, regardless of circumstances. He is self-controlled and firm in conviction, thus not deviating from his spiritual path. Most importantly, he has completely dedicated his mind and intellect to the Lord. Such a devotee is exceedingly dear to the Lord, because his devotion is complete and exclusive.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.14)

shloka_text: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः।हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः।।12.15।।
translation: He by whom no one is agitated, and who is not agitated by anyone, who is free from joy, envy, fear, and anxiety—such a devotee is very dear to Me.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes another important quality found in His dear devotee. Such a devotee acts in a way that no being is agitated or troubled by him. Simultaneously, he himself is not disturbed by any other being or external circumstance. He is free from dualities like joy, envy (or anger), fear, and anxiety. This is a symbol of equanimity and inner peace, which makes him exceedingly dear to the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.15)

shloka_text: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः।।12.16।।
translation: One who is indifferent to worldly gain, pure, skillful, unconcerned, untroubled, and who has renounced all undertakings—such a devotee is very dear to Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna here describes further qualities of His dear devotee. Such a devotee is indifferent to any worldly gain and is pure, both internally and externally. He is skillful in his duties but unconcerned about the results, thus remaining unperturbed. He is free from all kinds of distress and anxieties, having renounced the initiation of all undertakings. This renunciation does not mean abandoning actions, but rather abandoning attachment to their fruits.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.16)

shloka_text: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः।।12.17।।
translation: One who neither rejoices nor despairs, neither laments nor hankers for gain, and who has renounced both good and evil deeds—such a devotee, full of devotion, is very dear to Me.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes the mental stability of His dear devotee. Such a devotee neither rejoices excessively at any gain nor despairs or laments over any loss. He does not hanker for anything, as all his desires are absorbed in God. He renounces attachment to the fruits of both good and evil deeds, knowing that all actions are subject to Maya. Such a devoted person is exceedingly dear to the Lord, because he transcends all dualities.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.17)

shloka_text: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः।।12.18।।
translation: One who is alike to foe and friend, as well as in honor and dishonor, who is equipoised in cold and heat, joy and sorrow, and is free from all unfavorable association—
meaning: Lord Krishna here describes the equanimity and non-attachment of His dear devotee. Such a devotee maintains an equal attitude towards both foe and friend, harboring no special attachment or aversion towards anyone. He remains undisturbed by both honor and dishonor, as his self-respect does not depend on external circumstances. He maintains equanimity even in dualities like cold and heat, joy and sorrow. He is free from all kinds of attachments, so no external object can affect him.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.18)

shloka_text: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित्।अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः।।12.19।।
translation: One who is alike in reproach and praise, who is silent (in contemplation), contented with anything, without attachment to a fixed residence, whose intellect is firm—such a devotee, full of devotion, is very dear to Me.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes the final qualities of His dear devotee. Such a devotee remains alike in both reproach and praise, knowing that these are all transient. He remains silent, which means not speaking unnecessarily and maintaining inner peace. He is contented with whatever he receives, without any complaint. He has no fixed residence, meaning he is not attached to any particular place. His intellect is firmly fixed in God, and such a devoted person is exceedingly dear to the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.19)

shloka_text: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते।श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः।।12.20।।
translation: But those devotees who, with faith, consider Me as the supreme goal and partake of this nectar of righteousness as declared, they are exceedingly dear to Me.
meaning: In this concluding verse, Lord Krishna summarizes the glory of the path of devotion He has described. He states that those devotees who faithfully consider Him as the supreme goal are exceedingly dear to Him. Such devotees partake of this 'nectar of righteousness,' which means following the principles of Bhakti Yoga as declared by the Lord. This nectar liberates them from the cycle of birth and death and grants supreme peace. This verse re-establishes the supremacy of the path of devotion and the importance of complete surrender to God.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (12.20)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च। एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव।।13.1।।
translation: Arjuna said: O Keshav! I wish to know about Prakriti (material nature), Purusha (the enjoyer), Kshetra (the field), Kshetrajna (the knower of the field), knowledge, and the object of knowledge.
meaning: In this verse, Arjuna expresses his profound desire to understand the intricate concepts of Prakriti, Purusha, Kshetra, and Kshetrajna from Lord Krishna. This inquiry marks the initial step towards spiritual enlightenment, where a seeker yearns to differentiate between material and spiritual realities. Kshetra refers to the physical body, while Kshetrajna is the soul or consciousness that perceives and knows the body. Knowledge is the process through which these truths are comprehended, and the object of knowledge is the ultimate truth to be realized. Arjuna's earnest request serves as a guiding light for all sincere aspirants on the path of self-realization.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.1)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते।एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः।।13.2।।
translation: The Supreme Divine Lord said: O son of Kunti! This body is called the 'field' (Kshetra), and one who knows it is called the 'knower of the field' (Kshetrajna) by those who discern the truth.
meaning: Lord Krishna responds to Arjuna's inquiry by defining the body as the 'Kshetra' or the field of activities. This body serves as the arena where the soul experiences life and reaps the consequences of its actions. The one who is aware of this body and all its internal workings is termed the 'Kshetrajna', the knower of the field. Those who are enlightened, the knowers of truth, clearly understand this distinction between the perishable body and the imperishable soul. This verse establishes the fundamental difference between the soul and the body, which forms the bedrock of spiritual wisdom.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.2)

shloka_text: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत। क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम।।13.3।।
translation: O scion of Bharat! Know Me to be the Knower of the field in all fields. The understanding of the field and the knower of the field—that alone is considered by Me to be true knowledge.
meaning: Lord Krishna reveals a profound truth here, stating that He Himself is the Knower of the field (Kshetrajna) in all bodies. This implies that the ultimate source of the individual soul within every living being is the Supreme Lord Himself, who is omnipresent as the Supersoul. True knowledge lies in understanding this distinction between the Kshetra (body) and the Kshetrajna (soul). This understanding liberates us from material attachments and guides us towards spiritual advancement. The Lord emphasizes that discerning this duality is the recognition of the ultimate truth, paving the way for liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.3)

shloka_text: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्।स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु।।13.4।।
translation: What that field of activities is, what its nature is, how changes take place in it, from what it is produced, and who that knower of the field is, and what his powers are—listen to all this from Me in summary.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna prepares Arjuna for a detailed exposition on the Kshetra and Kshetrajna. He promises to clarify the nature of the field, its transformations, its origin, and the causes behind it. Concurrently, He proposes to briefly explain the identity of the knower of the field and its divine influences. This description offers a systematic approach to comprehending the profound depths of spiritual knowledge. The Lord's assurance instills eagerness in seekers for the revelation of the ultimate truth.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.4)

shloka_text: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक्।ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्िचतैः।।13.5।।
translation: This knowledge of the field and the knower of the field has been sung in manifold ways by great sages, described variously in different Vedic hymns, and also conclusively established with logic by the aphorisms of the Brahma Sutra.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna emphasizes the authenticity and ancient origin of the knowledge concerning the Kshetra and Kshetrajna. He explains that this wisdom is not merely His personal view but has been expounded in various ways by great sages. Diverse Vedic hymns and Upanishads also contain distinct descriptions of this profound truth. Furthermore, this knowledge is firmly established with logical and conclusive evidence through the aphorisms of the Brahma Sutra. This highlights that the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita are an integral part of the eternal Vedic tradition and are founded on irrefutable proofs.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.5)

shloka_text: महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च।इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः।।13.6।।
translation: The five great elements (earth, water, fire, air, ether), ego, intellect, the unmanifested primordial matter, the ten senses (five knowledge-acquiring senses and five working senses), the one mind, and the five objects of the senses (form, taste, smell, touch, sound).
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna begins to describe the detailed components of the Kshetra, the field of activities. He identifies the five great elements—earth, water, fire, air, and ether—as the fundamental material basis of the Kshetra. Ego, intellect, and the unmanifested primordial matter are also crucial parts of the Kshetra, operating at a subtle level. The ten senses (five knowledge-acquiring and five working senses) along with the mind, which is the eleventh sense, are also integral to the Kshetra. Furthermore, the five objects of the senses—form, taste, smell, touch, and sound—are included within the Kshetra, forming the basis of material experiences.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.6)

shloka_text: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः।एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम्।।13.7।।
translation: Desire, aversion, happiness, misery, the aggregate (of the body), consciousness, and will (fortitude)—all these, along with their modifications, are said to comprise the field of activities in summary.
meaning: Lord Krishna continues the description of the Kshetra, now including its mental and emotional aspects. Emotions such as desire and aversion, happiness and misery, are also modifications of the Kshetra, forming part of the living entity's experiences. The aggregate of the body, meaning the combination of various elements, along with consciousness and fortitude (will), are also encompassed within the Kshetra. All these elements, including their modifications, collectively constitute the Kshetra, which serves as the foundation for the soul's actions. Thus, the Kshetra is not merely the physical body but a complex amalgamation of mind, intellect, ego, and emotions.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.7)

shloka_text: अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम्।आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः।।13.8।।
translation: Humbleness, freedom from hypocrisy, non-violence, forgiveness, simplicity, service of the Guru, cleanliness of body and mind, steadfastness, and self-control.
meaning: From this verse, Lord Krishna begins to describe the qualities that constitute true knowledge. Humbleness (amanitvam) and freedom from hypocrisy (adambhitvam) signify the essential humility required for spiritual progress. Non-violence (ahimsa) and forgiveness (kshanti) establish a compassionate and tolerant attitude towards others. Simplicity, service to the Guru, cleanliness, steadfastness, and self-control indicate internal and external purity and discipline. These virtues elevate an individual beyond material attachments, guiding them towards self-realization.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.8)

shloka_text: इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च।जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्।।13.9।।
translation: Dispassion towards the objects of the senses, absence of egotism, and constant perception of the evils and miseries of birth, death, old age, and disease.
meaning: Continuing the series of qualities of knowledge, Lord Krishna highlights dispassion towards sense objects as crucial. The absence of egotism is also essential for self-knowledge, as ego obstructs the perception of truth. Constant contemplation on the miseries of birth, death, old age, and disease reveals the ephemeral nature of material life. This reflection makes an individual aware of the futility of worldly existence and strengthens their resolve on the spiritual path. By perceiving these faults, one understands the transient nature of material pleasures and becomes detached from them.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.9)

shloka_text: असक्ितरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु।नित्यं च समचित्तत्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु।।13.10।।
translation: Non-attachment and absence of craving for children, spouse, home, etc., and constant even-mindedness in the attainment of the desirable and undesirable.
meaning: To advance on the path of knowledge, Lord Krishna emphasizes non-attachment to material possessions and relationships like children, spouse, and home. The absence of craving for these connections and properties grants an individual inner freedom. Maintaining constant even-mindedness in the face of desirable and undesirable occurrences in life is also a significant characteristic of knowledge. This equanimity helps an individual rise above dualities such as pleasure and pain, gain and loss. Such non-attachment and even-mindedness truly pave the way for genuine spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.10)

shloka_text: मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्ितरव्यभिचारिणी।विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि।।13.11।।
translation: Unwavering devotion to Me through exclusive union, inclination for solitary and sacred places, and aversion for mundane society.
meaning: Lord Krishna here reveals a supremely important aspect of knowledge: unwavering devotion exclusively to Him. This unswerving devotion, which has no other objective, is the essence of the spiritual path. An inclination for solitary and sacred places keeps an individual away from external distractions and aids in internal contemplation. Aversion to mundane society and its activities also helps in concentrating the mind and keeping it focused on the spiritual goal. All these qualities together lead a seeker towards the ultimate truth and help them establish a deep connection with the Lord.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.11)

shloka_text: अध्यात्मज्ञाननित्यत्वं तत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनम्।एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतोन्यथा।।13.12।।
translation: Constancy in spiritual knowledge, and philosophical understanding of the goal of knowledge—all this is declared as knowledge, and whatever is contrary to this is ignorance.
meaning: Lord Krishna concludes the description of the qualities of knowledge by emphasizing constancy in spiritual understanding. The philosophical understanding of the goal of knowledge, meaning the endeavor to comprehend the ultimate truth, is an integral part of true wisdom. The aggregate of all these qualities is termed real knowledge, which leads an individual towards liberation. Anything contrary to these qualities, such as ego, attachment, and indulgence in material pleasures, is declared as ignorance. This verse clearly establishes the distinction between knowledge and ignorance, enabling the seeker to choose the correct path.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.12)

shloka_text: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते।अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते।।13.13।।
translation: I shall now reveal to you that which ought to be known, by knowing which one achieves immortality. That beginningless, supreme Brahman, subordinate to Me, is said to be neither existent nor non-existent.
meaning: Lord Krishna now begins to describe the Jneyam, the ultimate truth that ought to be known. He states that by knowing this Jneyam, one attains immortality, which is the ultimate goal of liberation. This Jneyam is beginningless and is the Supreme Brahman, subordinate to the Lord Himself, the origin of all existence. It cannot be called 'sat' (existent) nor 'asat' (non-existent), as it transcends material dualities. This Supreme Brahman is beyond material attributes and is inaccessible to our limited senses and mind.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.13)

shloka_text: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति।।13.14।।
translation: That Supreme Brahman has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere. It has ears everywhere and exists pervading everything in the universe.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the omnipresent nature of the Supreme Brahman, which extends in all directions. He states that the Supreme Brahman has hands, feet, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, signifying its omnipotence. This symbolic description indicates that it is not confined to any single location or form but is present everywhere. It exists pervading the entire universe, meaning nothing is outside of it. This verse clearly expresses the infinitude of the Supreme Brahman and its all-pervading presence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.14)

shloka_text: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम्।असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च।।13.15।।
translation: It perceives all sense objects, yet is devoid of all senses. It is unattached, yet the sustainer of all. It is beyond the three modes of material nature, yet the enjoyer of the three modes of material nature.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the paradoxical attributes of the Supreme Brahman, which highlight its transcendental nature. It perceives all sense objects, yet is devoid of material senses itself, indicating its divine consciousness. It is unattached to anything, yet sustains all beings, proving its supreme authority. The Supreme Brahman is beyond the three modes of material nature (sattva, rajas, tamas), yet it is the enjoyer of these modes. This description illustrates that the Supreme Brahman is not bound by the laws of the material world but is their controller and witness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.15)

shloka_text: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च। सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत्।।13.16।।
translation: It is outside and inside all living beings; it is both moving and non-moving. Due to its subtlety, it is incomprehensible; it is very far away and also very near.
meaning: Lord Krishna continues to describe the omnipresence and subtlety of the Supreme Brahman. It exists both outside and inside all living beings, as the Supersoul and the individual soul, respectively. It manifests in both moving (charam) and non-moving (acharam) forms, indicating its infinite expressions. Due to its extremely subtle nature, it is incomprehensible to ordinary senses and the mind. It is very far for the ignorant, yet extremely near for the wise and devoted, illustrating the duality of its accessibility.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.16)

shloka_text: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्।भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च।।13.17।।
translation: Although indivisible, it appears to be divided among living beings. That which is to be known is the sustainer of all beings, and it is also the annihilator and the creator.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes both the unity and diversity of the Supreme Brahman. It exists indivisibly within all beings, yet appears divided due to its illusory energy (Maya). This knowable Supreme Brahman is the sustainer of all living entities, indicating its role as a protector. It is also the creator and annihilator of the universe, establishing its nature as the ultimate controller. This verse clarifies the inconceivable power of the Supreme Brahman and its paramount authority.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.17)

shloka_text: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्।।13.18।।
translation: It is the source of light in all luminaries; it is said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the goal of knowledge, and it dwells within the heart of all living beings.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the Supreme Brahman as the source of all light, even of the sun, moon, and fire. It is said to be beyond material darkness, indicating its pure spiritual nature. It is knowledge itself, the object to be known, and attainable only through knowledge. This Supreme Brahman resides as the Supersoul within the heart of all living beings, signifying its inner presence. This verse establishes the ultimate divinity of the Supreme Brahman, its nature as knowledge, and its omnipresent internality.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.18)

shloka_text: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते।।13.19।।
translation: Thus, the nature of the field, the meaning of knowledge, and the object of knowledge have been revealed in summary. My devotee, having understood this, attains My divine nature.
meaning: Lord Krishna concludes His concise description of the Kshetra, knowledge, and the object of knowledge in this verse. He clarifies that a devotee who comprehends this profound wisdom becomes capable of attaining His divine nature. This knowledge is not merely intellectual understanding but leads to self-realization and unity with the Lord. Attaining the divine nature of the Lord is the state of liberation and ultimate bliss. This verse underscores the fruit of knowledge and the importance of devotion, which is the ultimate goal of the spiritual journey.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.19)

shloka_text: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि।विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान्।।13.20।।
translation: Know both material nature and the individual souls to be beginningless. And also know all transformations (of the body) and the three modes of nature to be produced by material energy.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna declares both Prakriti (material nature) and Purusha (the individual soul) to be beginningless. This means that both have existed since time immemorial and have no known origin. All transformations of the body and the three modes of material nature (sattva, rajas, tamas) originate from Prakriti itself. It is crucial to understand that the soul (Purusha) is distinct from Prakriti and imperishable, while Prakriti and its modifications are subject to change. This knowledge guides the living entity towards liberation from material bondage.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.20)

shloka_text: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते।पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते।।13.21।।
translation: Material energy is said to be the medium for the creation of the effect (body) and the cause (senses). The individual soul is said to be responsible for experiencing happiness and distress.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna clarifies the distinct roles of Prakriti and Purusha. Prakriti is stated to be the cause for the creation of the body (effect) and the senses (cause). This means that the development of the physical body and senses occurs due to the qualities of material nature. Purusha, the individual soul, is the experiencer of happiness and distress. This verse illustrates that Prakriti creates the material world, while the soul experiences the objects thus created.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.21)

shloka_text: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान्।कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु।।13.22।।
translation: The individual soul, seated in material energy, indeed desires to enjoy the three modes of nature produced by material energy. Its attachment to these modes is the cause of its birth in superior and inferior wombs.
meaning: Lord Krishna explains that the individual soul, situated in material nature, experiences the qualities produced by Prakriti. This experience arises from desire and attachment, which keep the soul bound in the material world. The soul's association with these qualities is the primary cause of its birth in various species. Birth in superior or inferior wombs depends on the soul's actions and its attachment to the modes of nature. This verse clarifies the law of karma and the cycle of reincarnation, which forms the basis of material existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.22)

shloka_text: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः।परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः।।13.23।।
translation: The Supreme Lord, who is also called the Supersoul, is present in this body as the witness, the permitter, the supporter, the transcendental enjoyer, and the ultimate controller.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the divine nature of the Supersoul residing within the body. The Supersoul is the witness of all the living entity's actions, acting as the observer. It permits the desires of the living entity, allowing them to fulfill their actions, thus being the permitter. The Supersoul sustains and supports all beings, hence it is the maintainer. It is the ultimate controller (Maheshvara) and the transcendental enjoyer, who, though beyond material qualities, is the ultimate source of all experiences.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.23)

shloka_text: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह। सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते।।13.24।।
translation: One who thus understands the Purusha (the individual soul and the Supreme Lord) and material nature along with its modes, even while acting in every way, does not take birth again.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the fruit of understanding the Kshetra and Kshetrajna. One who correctly comprehends this distinction between Purusha (the individual soul and the Supreme Lord) and Prakriti along with its modes becomes liberated. Such a knowledgeable person, even while living and acting in the material world, is freed from the cycle of rebirth. This knowledge elevates them above material attachments and establishes them in the state of self-realization. This verse demonstrates that true knowledge is the path to liberation, freeing one from the bondage of birth and death.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.24)

shloka_text: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे।।13.25।।
translation: Some perceive the Supreme Soul within their heart by the mind through meditation. Others perceive it through the cultivation of knowledge (Sankhya Yoga), and still others through the path of action (Karma Yoga).
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes various paths to self-realization. Some yogis perceive the Supersoul residing within their heart through their mind, by means of meditation (Dhyana Yoga). Others understand the soul through Sankhya Yoga, which involves the path of analytical knowledge and discrimination. Still others attain the Supreme Soul through Karma Yoga, by performing actions without attachment to their results. This illustrates that there are multiple valid paths to attain the ultimate truth, suitable for individuals with different inclinations.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.25)

shloka_text: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते।तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः।।13.26।।
translation: Still others, who are unaware of these spiritual paths, begin to worship by hearing from others. They also, being devoted to hearing (from saints), certainly cross over death.
meaning: Lord Krishna here offers hope for those who are not directly capable of Dhyana or Jnana Yoga. He states that individuals who do not know these spiritual paths themselves can still worship by hearing from others. Such devotees, who are devoted to hearing with faith from saints and scriptures, also certainly transcend the bondage of death. This verse highlights the importance of satsang (association with devotees) and the Guru-disciple tradition, where liberation is possible even through mere hearing. It reveals the boundless mercy of the Lord, who provides an opportunity for liberation to everyone, regardless of their specific path.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.26)

shloka_text: यावत्सञ्जायते किञ्चित्सत्त्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम्।क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञसंयोगात्तद्विद्धि भरतर्षभ।।13.27।।
translation: O best of the Bharatas! Whatever being, moving or unmoving, manifests, know that it is produced from the combination of the field of activities and the knower of the field.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna clarifies the fundamental principle of creation. He states that whatever manifests in this world, whether stationary or moving, arises only from the combination of the Kshetra and the Kshetrajna. Kshetra represents material nature, and Kshetrajna represents the soul or the Supersoul. This combination is the basis of all forms of life and existence; without it, no creation is possible. This verse illustrates the coexistence and interrelationship of material and spiritual elements.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.27)

shloka_text: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम्।विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति।।13.28।।
translation: One who sees the Supreme Soul equally present in all beings, imperishable amidst the perishable, truly perceives.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna defines true vision or knowledge. One who sees the Supreme Lord equally present in all beings, regardless of their species, is truly wise. Such a person also perceives that while physical bodies are perishable, the soul and Supersoul residing within them are imperishable. This equanimous vision liberates an individual from discrimination and teaches respect for all living entities. Such a vision alone leads to the realization of the ultimate truth and guides an individual towards spiritual advancement.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.28)

shloka_text: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम्।न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्।।13.29।।
translation: Indeed, one who sees God as the Supreme Soul equally present everywhere does not degrade oneself by one's mind, and thereby attains the supreme destination.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the spiritual benefits of equanimous vision. One who sees the Supersoul equally present everywhere never degrades oneself. Such a person does not harm the self by their mind, knowing that the same Supersoul resides in all. As a result of such equanimity and self-control, that individual attains the supreme destination, which is liberation. This verse demonstrates that self-knowledge and equanimous vision are the path to ultimate well-being.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.29)

shloka_text: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः।यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति।।13.30।।
translation: One who sees that all actions are truly performed in every way by material nature, and also sees the embodied soul as actionless, truly perceives.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna clarifies the true nature of action. One who perceives that all actions are indeed performed in every way by the modes of material nature is truly wise. Such a person also understands that the soul itself is actionless, meaning it is not the doer of actions but merely a witness. This knowledge helps an individual become detached from the fruits of actions and liberates them from bondage. This verse demonstrates that understanding the passivity of the soul and the activity of nature is true spiritual insight.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.30)

shloka_text: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।।13.31।।
translation: When one sees the diverse variety of living entities situated in the same place, and thereafter sees that they are born from that very source, then they attain Brahman.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the state of Brahman realization. When an individual perceives the diverse variety of all living entities as situated in one supreme reality, they attain true knowledge. They also see that all beings have expanded from that very same ultimate source. This experience of oneness elevates an individual above material distinctions and grants them the realization of identity with Brahman. Upon gaining such insight, the individual attains Brahman and reaches the state of liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.31)

shloka_text: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः।शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते।।13.32।।
translation: O Arjun, the son of Kunti! This Supreme Soul is imperishable due to being without beginning and being devoid of any material qualities. Although dwelling in the body, it neither acts nor is tainted.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna reiterates the divine and transcendental nature of the Supersoul. The Supersoul is beginningless, meaning it has no origin, and is devoid of material qualities (nirguna). For this reason, it is imperishable (avyaya), meaning indestructible and unchangeable. Although it resides in all bodies, it neither performs any actions nor is it tainted by their results. This verse illustrates the Supersoul's neutrality, purity, and its distinctness from the material world.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.32)

shloka_text: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते।सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते।।13.33।।
translation: As the all-pervading space is not contaminated due to its subtlety, similarly, the soul, though situated everywhere in the body, is not contaminated.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna explains the non-attachment of the soul with a beautiful analogy. Just as the all-pervading space, due to its subtlety, is not tainted by any material object. Similarly, the soul, though present everywhere within the body, is not contaminated by the body's modifications or actions. This subtlety and non-attachment of the soul are proof of its pure spiritual nature. This verse clarifies the imperishable and untainted state of the soul, which keeps it free from material bondage.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.33)

shloka_text: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः।क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत।।13.34।।
translation: O Arjun, the son of Bharat! As one sun illumines this entire solar system, so does the knower of the field (the soul) illumine the entire field (the body).
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna explains the illuminating power of the soul's consciousness with another analogy. Just as a single sun, with its rays, illumines the entire solar system and makes it visible. Similarly, the Kshetri (the soul) illumines the entire Kshetra (the body) with its consciousness. This consciousness of the soul makes the body alive and grants it the ability to experience. This verse illustrates the central role of the soul and its luminous nature, which is the basis of the body's existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.34)

shloka_text: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा।भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्।।13.35।।
translation: Those who, with the eyes of knowledge, thus know the difference between the body and the knower of the body, and also the release of the living entity from material nature, approach the Supreme.
meaning: Lord Krishna concludes this chapter by describing the ultimate fruit of knowledge. One who clearly perceives the difference between the Kshetra (body) and the Kshetrajna (soul) with the eyes of knowledge is truly wise. Such a person also understands how the liberation of the living entity from material nature is possible. These knowledgeable individuals attain the Supreme destination, which is liberation and reaching the abode of the Lord. This verse demonstrates that the path of self-knowledge and liberation from material nature leads to the ultimate truth.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (13.35)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम्।यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः।।14.1।।
translation: The Supreme Lord said: I shall again declare unto you this supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledge, by knowing which all the sages have attained the highest perfection from this world.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna resolves to impart the supreme knowledge to Arjuna. This knowledge is considered the best among all forms of wisdom and leads to liberation. Many sages, by understanding this profound truth, have transcended worldly attachments and achieved the highest perfection. This wisdom reveals the true nature of the soul and the path to rise above the modes of material nature. The Lord reiterates this knowledge to ensure Arjuna's complete comprehension and spiritual upliftment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.1)

shloka_text: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः।सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च।।14.2।।
translation: Those who take refuge in this knowledge attain a nature similar to Mine; they are not born at the time of creation, nor are they disturbed at the time of dissolution.
meaning: Those who attain this supreme knowledge achieve a divine nature akin to the Lord's own. Such enlightened souls are not born again into new bodies at the beginning of creation. They also remain undisturbed and free from anxiety during the time of universal dissolution. This state signifies complete liberation from the cycle of birth and death. They transcend the modes of material nature and attain eternal peace. This knowledge paves the way for the soul's union with the Supreme Being.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.2)

shloka_text: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम्।संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत।।14.3।।
translation: O son of Bharata, My great material nature (Mahat-Brahma) is the womb; in that, I place the germ. From that, all living beings are born.
meaning: Here, the Lord explains the mystery of creation. He states that His great material nature, Mahat-Brahma, serves as the womb or mother of all living beings. Into this nature, the Lord Himself places the seed, which represents the individual souls. From this union, all animate and inanimate beings come into existence. This illustrates that both nature and the soul are under the Lord's supreme power. The Lord is thus the ultimate cause and sustainer of the entire creation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.3)

shloka_text: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः।तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता।।14.4।।
translation: O son of Kunti, whatever forms are produced in all species of life, the great material nature is their womb, and I am the seed-giving father.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna clarifies His role as the father and mother of creation. He states that for all the various species of life that manifest in the universe, the great material nature (Mahat-Brahma) serves as the mother. The Lord Himself is the seed-giving father, implanting the individual souls into these bodies. This principle illustrates the creation of the universe through the union of nature and the spirit. The Lord is thus the ultimate progenitor and controller of all living beings. This establishes His omnipresence and His role as the supreme creator.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.4)

shloka_text: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः।निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम्।।14.5।।
translation: O mighty-armed one, Sattva (goodness), Rajas (passion), and Tamas (ignorance) – these modes, born of material nature, bind the eternal embodied soul to the body.
meaning: Here, the Lord introduces the three modes of material nature: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. These three qualities originate from material nature and bind the eternal soul to the physical body. Although the soul is imperishable and eternal, it feels bound by the influence of these modes. These modes determine the soul's actions and experiences within the material world. Due to these qualities, the soul remains entangled in the cycle of happiness and sorrow, knowledge and ignorance, action and inaction. Understanding these modes is the first step towards liberation from their binding influence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.5)

shloka_text: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम्।सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ।।14.6।।
translation: O sinless one, among these, the mode of goodness (Sattva), being pure, is illuminating and free from all maladies. It binds the embodied soul through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge.
meaning: The mode of goodness (Sattva) is the purest and most untainted among the three modes, making it illuminating and free from ailments. This quality generates feelings of knowledge and happiness within an individual. However, it still binds the embodied soul because the person becomes attached to happiness and knowledge. An individual situated in Sattva feels knowledgeable and joyful, and this very attachment prevents liberation. This binding is subtle, yet it hinders the soul from achieving complete freedom. Therefore, transcending even the mode of goodness is essential for ultimate liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.6)

shloka_text: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम्।तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम्।।14.7।।
translation: O son of Kunti, know the mode of passion (Rajas) to be of the nature of intense desire, arising from craving and attachment. It binds the embodied soul through attachment to fruitive actions.
meaning: The mode of passion (Rajas) is understood as the root cause of attachment and desire. It arises from craving and longing, which constantly impel an individual to engage in activities. A person under the influence of Rajas performs actions with an expectation of their results. This mode binds the embodied soul through attachment to the fruits of actions. Due to this attachment, the soul repeatedly takes birth and experiences the consequences of its deeds. Therefore, the mode of passion also presents a significant obstacle on the path to liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.7)

shloka_text: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम्।प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत।।14.8।।
translation: O son of Bharata, know the mode of ignorance (Tamas) to be born of darkness, deluding all embodied souls. It binds the embodied soul through negligence, laziness, and sleep.
meaning: The mode of ignorance (Tamas) originates from nescience and deludes all embodied souls. This quality induces negligence, laziness, and excessive sleep in an individual. Under the influence of Tamas, a person deviates from their duties and loses the discernment between right and wrong. It plunges the soul into darkness and inactivity, causing it to forget its true nature. The bondage of Tamas is the deepest and the greatest impediment on the path to liberation. It is therefore extremely essential to become free from it.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.8)

shloka_text: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत।ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत।।14.9।।
translation: O son of Bharata, the mode of goodness binds one to happiness, passion binds one to action, but the mode of ignorance, covering knowledge, binds one to delusion.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord summarizes the distinct effects of the three modes. The mode of goodness inclines an individual towards happiness and knowledge, leading them to perceive themselves as joyful and wise. The mode of passion engages a person in actions, causing them to remain constantly active with a desire for results. The mode of ignorance, by obscuring knowledge, traps an individual in negligence, laziness, and delusion. Thus, all three modes bind the embodied soul to the material world in different ways. Only by understanding the influences of these modes can one transcend them.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.9)

shloka_text: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत।रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा।।14.10।।
translation: O son of Bharata, sometimes the mode of goodness predominates by overcoming passion and ignorance. Sometimes passion predominates by overcoming goodness and ignorance, and sometimes ignorance predominates by overcoming goodness and passion.
meaning: The Lord explains here that these three modes are never static; rather, they constantly vie for dominance over each other. When the mode of goodness increases, it suppresses passion and ignorance, leading to an increase in peace and knowledge within the individual. Similarly, when the mode of passion becomes strong, it suppresses goodness and ignorance, engaging the person in action and attachment. And when the mode of ignorance predominates, it suppresses goodness and passion, plunging the individual into nescience and delusion. This cycle continues perpetually, causing the living entity's states to fluctuate.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.10)

shloka_text: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते।ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत।।14.11।।
translation: When illumination and knowledge manifest through all the gates of the body, then one should know that the mode of goodness has predominated.
meaning: The Lord describes the symptoms of an increase in the mode of goodness here. When the light of knowledge manifests through all the gates of the body, meaning the senses, one should understand that the mode of goodness is predominant. This implies that a person's eyes, ears, mind, and intellect become capable of grasping pure knowledge. During such times, feelings of discernment, peace, and contentment increase within the individual. This state is conducive to spiritual progress. The predominance of Sattva enables a person to make correct decisions.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.11)

shloka_text: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा।रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ।।14.12।।
translation: O best of the Bharatas, when the mode of passion predominates, greed, activity, undertaking of actions, restlessness, and craving – these all arise.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord describes the symptoms of an increase in the mode of passion. When Rajas predominates, greed, excessive activity, and the desire to undertake various actions increase in an individual. Restlessness and intense craving for different objects are also indicators of an increase in Rajas. Such a person's mind remains agitated, and they constantly pursue material achievements. This state keeps an individual perpetually active but deprives them of inner peace. The influence of Rajas further entangles a person in worldly attachments.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.12)

shloka_text: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च।तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन।।14.13।।
translation: O joy of the Kurus, when the mode of ignorance predominates, darkness, inactivity, negligence, and delusion – these all manifest.
meaning: The Lord describes the symptoms of an increase in the mode of ignorance here. When Tamas predominates, darkness, inactivity, negligence, and delusion arise in an individual. Such a person's intellect becomes dull, and they are unable to discern right from wrong. They turn away from their duties, indulging in laziness and excessive sleep. This state leads an individual towards degradation, both spiritually and materially. The influence of Tamas plunges the living entity into profound darkness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.13)

shloka_text: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्।तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते।।14.14।।
translation: When an embodied being meets death while the mode of goodness predominates, then he attains the pure worlds of those who know the Supreme.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord explains how the predominance of a particular mode at the time of death determines one's next birth. If an embodied being dies when the mode of goodness is predominant, they attain the pure worlds of those who are highly learned. These worlds are akin to higher celestial realms, where happiness and knowledge prevail. Dying in the mode of goodness signifies that the individual lived a life adhering to righteousness, knowledge, and purity. This state leads the soul towards higher spiritual experiences.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.14)

shloka_text: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते।तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते।।14.15।।
translation: Dying in the mode of passion, one is born among those attached to fruitive actions. Likewise, dying in the mode of ignorance, one takes birth in the animal kingdom.
meaning: The Lord describes the consequences of dying in the modes of passion and ignorance here. If a person dies with the predominance of the mode of passion, they are born among human beings who are attached to fruitive actions. Such individuals are constantly driven by the desire for material pleasures and the fruits of their labor. Conversely, if someone dies absorbed in the mode of ignorance, they take birth in lower species, such as animals or other unintelligent life forms. This illustrates that the influence of the modes determines not only the present life but also future births.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.15)

shloka_text: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम्।रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्।।14.16।।
translation: The fruit of righteous action is said to be pure and in the mode of goodness. The fruit of the mode of passion is misery, and the fruit of the mode of ignorance is nescience.
meaning: In this verse, the Lord clarifies the fruits of actions according to the three modes. The result of actions performed in the mode of goodness is pure and untainted, leading to happiness, knowledge, and peace for the individual. The fruit of actions motivated by the mode of passion is misery, as they are filled with attachment and desires. The outcome of actions arising from the mode of ignorance is nescience, which keeps a person in delusion and confusion. This principle explains the law of karma in the context of the modes. Therefore, understanding the modes is essential to comprehend the results of one's actions.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.16)

shloka_text: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च।प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च।।14.17।।
translation: From the mode of goodness, knowledge arises; from the mode of passion, greed certainly arises; and from the mode of ignorance, negligence, delusion, and indeed ignorance itself arise.
meaning: Here, the Lord describes the primary mental and intellectual outcomes arising from each mode. From the predominance of the mode of goodness, pure knowledge emerges in an individual, making them discerning. From the mode of passion, greed and intense desires arise, pushing a person towards material accumulation. From the mode of ignorance, negligence, delusion, and nescience are born, corrupting an individual's intellect. This verse clarifies the subtle influences of the modes. By understanding these effects, one can recognize their own nature.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.17)

shloka_text: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः।जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः।।14.18।।
translation: Those situated in the mode of goodness rise upwards. Those in the mode of passion remain in the middle. And those situated in the abominable mode of ignorance go downwards.
meaning: This verse clarifies the destiny and movement of the soul according to the modes. Individuals situated in the mode of goodness ascend to higher realms after death, where knowledge and happiness prevail. Those in the mode of passion remain in the middle realms, meaning they are reborn in the human world, where they remain entangled in the cycle of action and its results. Individuals situated in the abominable mode of ignorance descend to lower species or hellish realms, where ignorance and suffering predominate. This demonstrates that our current actions and dominant modes determine our future.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.18)

shloka_text: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति।गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति।।14.19।।
translation: When the seer perceives no doer other than the modes of nature, and knows that which is transcendental to these modes, he attains My divine nature.
meaning: This verse points towards the state of transcending the modes. When an enlightened individual realizes that all actions are performed solely by the modes of material nature, and that the soul is not truly the doer, they transcend these modes. They also come to know that beyond these modes exists a Supreme Being, the Lord Himself. By attaining this knowledge, they achieve the divine nature of the Lord. This state liberates the soul from the cycle of birth and death. This is the highest level of self-realization.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.19)
