shloka_text: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान्।जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते।।14.20।।
translation: The embodied soul, by transcending these three modes, which are the cause of the body's origin, becomes liberated from birth, death, old age, and misery, and attains immortality.
meaning: This verse describes the ultimate fruit of transcending the modes. When the embodied soul surpasses these three modes, which originate from material nature, it becomes liberated from birth, death, old age, and all forms of misery. Upon transcending the modes, the soul recognizes its true, imperishable nature. In this state, it attains immortality, which is another name for liberation. This is a state of supreme peace and eternal bliss. This represents the ultimate goal of the Bhagavad Gita's teachings.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.20)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो।किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते।।14.21।।
translation: Arjuna inquired: O Lord, by what symptoms is one known who has transcended these three modes? What is his conduct, and how does he transcend these three modes?
meaning: Arjuna asks the Lord three significant questions regarding a person who has transcended the modes. Firstly, what are the symptoms by which such a person can be identified as having transcended the modes? Secondly, what is their conduct like, meaning how do they behave in the world? Thirdly, how does one transcend these three modes, meaning what is the process to become गुणातीत? These questions reflect Arjuna's curiosity and his desire for spiritual advancement. The answers to these questions can help even ordinary seekers understand the state of transcending the modes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.21)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति।।14.22।।
translation: The Supreme Divine Personality said: O son of Pandu, he who does not hate illumination (the effect of Sattva), activity (the effect of Rajas), and delusion (the effect of Tamas) when they are present, nor longs for them when they are absent.
meaning: The Lord describes the first symptom of a person who has transcended the modes. Such an individual does not hate illumination (the effect of Sattva), activity (the effect of Rajas), or delusion (the effect of Tamas) when they manifest. They observe the natural effects of these modes with a detached attitude. When these modes subside, they do not long for them, meaning they are neither pleased by their presence nor saddened by their absence. They witness the play of the modes with a sense of detachment. This equanimity is the primary indication of having transcended the modes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.22)

shloka_text: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते।।14.23।।
translation: He who remains like a neutral observer, undisturbed by the modes, and who, knowing that "the modes are acting upon the modes," remains steadfast and does not waver.
meaning: A person who has transcended the modes remains in a state of neutrality, meaning they are unaffected by the influences of the modes. They know that all actions are being performed solely by the modes of material nature, and that they themselves are not the doer of these actions. Due to this knowledge, they remain undisturbed by the play of the modes and stay steadfast in their spiritual state. They rise above dualities like happiness and sorrow, gain and loss. This inner stability and the attitude of a witness are crucial characteristics of the state of transcending the modes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.23)

shloka_text: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः।।14.24।।
translation: He who is alike in happiness and distress, who is established in the Self, to whom a clod of earth, a stone, and gold are of equal value. He who is equal to the pleasant and the unpleasant, who is steady, and who is equal in censure and praise.
meaning: The equanimity of a person who has transcended the modes is described here. They remain equal in both happiness and distress, knowing that these are all plays of the modes. They are established in their true Self and see no distinction between external objects like a clod of earth, a stone, or gold. They remain equal in pleasant and unpleasant situations and are patient. They are undisturbed by censure or praise, as their identity transcends the modes. This equanimity signifies their inner liberation and stability.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.24)

shloka_text: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते।।14.25।।
translation: He who is equal in honor and dishonor, equal to friends and foes. He who has renounced all undertakings, such a person is said to have transcended the modes.
meaning: A person who has transcended the modes remains equal in both honor and dishonor, as their spiritual vision rises above these dualities. They treat both friends and foes with equanimity, seeing the same Self in everyone. The most significant symptom is that they renounce the initiation of all worldly actions. This does not mean they become inactive, but rather they perform actions without attachment to their results. Such an individual is truly said to have transcended the three modes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.25)

shloka_text: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते।स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते।।14.26।।
translation: And he who serves Me with unswerving devotion (Bhakti-yoga), he, transcending these modes, becomes fit for the state of Brahman.
meaning: Here, the Lord reveals the most direct and effective path to transcend the modes. An individual who serves the Lord with unswerving devotion (Bhakti-yoga) easily surpasses these three modes. Unswerving devotion means pure love and service to the Lord without any desire or self-interest. Through such devotion, the mind becomes purified, and the individual becomes free from the influence of the modes. Rising above the modes, they become fit to attain the state of Brahman, which is self-realization. This path of devotion is indeed the means to ultimate liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.26)

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च।शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च।।14.27।।
translation: For I am the basis of the impersonal Brahman, of the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss.
meaning: In this concluding verse, the Lord declares His supreme position. He states that He is the basis of the imperishable Brahman, of immortality, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss. This implies that the impersonal Brahman is also an aspect of Lord Krishna's own power. Those who attain Brahman actually attain an aspect of the Lord Himself. The Lord is the ultimate source and final destination of all spiritual perfections. This verse establishes the Lord's supremacy and His position as the ultimate cause of all causes.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (14.27)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्।छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्।।15.1।।
translation: The Supreme Divine Personality said: They speak of an imperishable Ashvattha tree with its roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; one who knows this tree is the knower of the Vedas.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the material world as an inverted Ashvattha tree. Its roots are above, in the highest spiritual realms, and its branches extend downwards into the human world. This world-tree is called imperishable because it perpetually revolves in the cycle of birth and death. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns, which describe rituals and enjoyments, further entangling the soul. One who truly comprehends the nature of this world-tree is considered a true knower of the Vedas' profound wisdom. This understanding reveals the transient nature of the world and guides one towards the path of detachment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.1)

shloka_text: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा     गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः।अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि     कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके।।15.2।।
translation: Its branches extend both downwards and upwards, nourished by the modes of material nature, with sense objects as its buds. And its roots also spread downwards in the human world, binding one to actions.
meaning: This verse elaborates on the world-tree, explaining its intricate structure. Its branches, representing various species and planetary systems, are nourished by the modes of material nature: goodness, passion, and ignorance. The buds on these branches are the objects of the senses, which further entangle living beings in worldly affairs. In the human world, its secondary roots also spread downwards, binding the soul through the consequences of actions. These roots lead to new births as a result of both good and bad deeds. Thus, this tree continuously revolves the soul in the cycle of birth and death.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.2)

shloka_text: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते    नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा।अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल    मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा।।15.3।।
translation: Its true form is not perceived in this world, nor its beginning, nor its end, nor its firm foundation. Having cut down this deeply rooted Ashvattha tree with the strong axe of detachment.
meaning: This verse reveals the illusory nature of the material world. The true form, beginning, end, or foundation of this world-tree is impossible to grasp with ordinary intellect. It is so complex and bewildering that no one can fully perceive it. Its roots are so deeply entrenched that uprooting it is extremely difficult. The only way to cut down this tree of worldly existence is with the strong axe of detachment. Dispassion towards sense objects and the fruits of actions is the sole means to liberation from this bondage. This detachment alone leads us towards the ultimate truth.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.3)

shloka_text: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः।तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी।।15.4।।
translation: Thereafter, one must search for that supreme abode, from which having gone, one never returns again. I surrender to that original Supreme Lord, from whom this ancient stream of activity has flowed forth.
meaning: After severing the world-tree with the axe of detachment, the seeker must then search for that supreme abode. This is the eternal dwelling from which, having reached it, a soul never returns to the cycle of birth and death. To attain this supreme state, one must surrender to that original Supreme Lord, Lord Krishna. He is the fundamental cause of all creation, and from Him, this ancient stream of worldly activity has flowed forth. By taking refuge in Him, the soul attains true peace and liberation. This surrender is indeed the path to achieving the ultimate goal.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.4)

shloka_text: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः।द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत्।।15.5।।
translation: Those who are free from pride and delusion, who have conquered the evils of attachment, who are constantly devoted to the Self and God, whose desires have completely subsided, and who are liberated from the dualities of pleasure and pain, such unbewildered souls attain that imperishable supreme abode.
meaning: This verse describes the essential qualities required for attaining the supreme abode. Freedom from pride and delusion, victory over the evils of attachment, and constant devotion to the Self and God are extremely important. Only those whose desires for sense gratification have completely subsided can progress on this path. Liberation from dualities like pleasure and pain, gain and loss, is also crucial. Such wise and unbewildered individuals alone attain that imperishable supreme abode, from which there is no return. This state represents the pinnacle of self-realization and God-realization.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.5)

shloka_text: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः।यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।।15.6।।
translation: Neither the sun illumines that supreme abode, nor the moon, nor fire. Having gone there, living beings never return; that is My supreme abode.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the transcendental nature of His supreme abode. This dwelling does not depend on material sources of light such as the sun, moon, or fire. It possesses its own divine effulgence, which is beyond the material realm. This is the place where, having reached it, a soul becomes completely liberated from the cycle of birth and death. It is the eternal residence of the Lord, where pure souls reside in an eternal relationship with Him. Attaining this abode is the ultimate goal of the living being, where one finds supreme peace and bliss.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.6)

shloka_text: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः।मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति।।15.7।।
translation: In this world of living beings, the eternal individual soul is indeed My fragmental part, and it struggles with the six senses, including the mind, which are situated in material nature.
meaning: Here, Lord Krishna reveals the true nature of the living entity. Every soul is an eternal fragmental part of the Supreme Soul, which is never destroyed. Upon entering the material world, this fragment assumes a body and finds itself bound by the modes of material nature. The six senses, including the mind (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin), are under the sway of material nature and are attracted to sense objects. Due to this attraction, the soul becomes entangled in the cycle of birth and death, constantly struggling. This verse clarifies the divine origin of the soul and its current material predicament.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.7)

shloka_text: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः।गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात्।।15.8।।
translation: When the embodied soul, the master of the body, leaves one body and obtains another, it carries these senses and the mind with it, just as the wind carries fragrances from their sources.
meaning: This verse explains the process of the soul's transmigration. The living entity, who is truly the master of the body, abandons one body at the time of death. It then enters another body, carrying with it the subtle body (mind, intelligence, ego, and senses). This process is exactly like the wind carrying fragrances from flowers or other sources. The soul obtains a new body according to its past actions, which corresponds to its desires and inclinations. This continuous cycle persists until the soul achieves liberation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.8)

shloka_text: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च।अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते।।15.9।।
translation: The embodied soul, taking shelter of the ear, the eye, the sense of touch, the tongue, and the nose, along with the mind, enjoys the objects of the senses.
meaning: This verse describes the method by which the living entity experiences enjoyment in the material world. The soul, residing in the body, in conjunction with the mind, experiences sense objects through its five knowledge-acquiring senses (ears, eyes, skin, tongue, nose). Through these senses, the soul enjoys sound, form, touch, taste, and smell. The mind acts as the central processing unit for these sensory experiences. Thus, the living entity remains engaged in various enjoyments in the material world according to its desires and inclinations. These enjoyments are what bind it to the cycle of worldly existence.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.9)

shloka_text: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम्।विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः।।15.10।।
translation: The deluded do not perceive the soul when it departs from the body, nor when it resides in the body, nor when it enjoys sense objects under the spell of the modes of material nature. Only those who possess the eyes of knowledge can truly see it.
meaning: This verse highlights the subtlety of the soul and the capacity to comprehend it. Ignorant and deluded individuals cannot perceive the soul as distinct from the body. They identify the soul with the body, whether it is departing, residing within, or enjoying sense objects under the influence of material modes. Their vision is purely material, and they fail to grasp the divine nature of the soul. In contrast, only those wise individuals who possess the eyes of knowledge can truly perceive the soul's actual form. They understand that the soul is distinct from the body, imperishable, and eternal.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.10)

shloka_text: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम्।यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः।।15.11।।
translation: Striving yogis also perceive this soul enshrined within themselves. However, those whose minds are not purified, even though they strive, do not perceive this soul, for they are unaware.
meaning: This verse emphasizes the importance of purifying the mind for self-realization. Yogis who are constantly striving and have purified their minds are able to perceive the soul enshrined within themselves. This self-perception is the result of internal discipline and concentration. Conversely, those whose minds are not purified, even if they strive, cannot perceive the soul. Their minds remain entangled in sense objects, rendering them unable to comprehend the subtle nature of the soul. Therefore, purity of mind and concentration are extremely essential for self-knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.11)

shloka_text: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम्।यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्।।15.12।।
translation: Know that the brilliance which resides in the sun and illuminates the entire world, and that which is in the moon, and that which is in fire, all that splendor is Mine.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes His omnipresence and supreme divinity. He states that the brilliance residing in the sun, which illuminates the entire world, is His own effulgence. The coolness and radiance of the moon also originate from Him. The burning power and light present in fire are also a part of His divine energy. Thus, the Lord clarifies that all sources of light and energy in the material world are manifestations of His divine power. This verse helps us understand that the Lord is the fundamental basis and controller of all creation. Nothing is possible without His power.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.12)

shloka_text: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा।पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः।।15.13।।
translation: Permeating the earth, I sustain all living beings with My energy. And becoming the moon, which supplies the juice of life, I nourish all plants.
meaning: Lord Krishna elaborates on His sustaining power. He states that by permeating the earth with His inconceivable energy, He sustains all living beings. It is His power that keeps the earth stable and makes life possible. Furthermore, He manifests as the moon, providing sap and nourishment to all plants. The moon's coolness and life-giving essence help plants grow and flourish. Thus, the Lord not only creates but also maintains and nourishes creation, ensuring the continuous cycle of life.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.13)

shloka_text: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः।प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्।।15.14।।
translation: Becoming the digestive fire (Vaishvanara) situated in the bodies of all living beings, I, united with the incoming and outgoing breaths, digest the four kinds of food.
meaning: Lord Krishna reveals another crucial aspect of His internal power. He states that He Himself resides as the Vaishvanara fire within the bodies of all living beings. This Vaishvanara fire is responsible for digesting food, thereby providing energy to the body. In conjunction with the balance of the incoming and outgoing breaths (prana and apana), this fire digests the four kinds of food (eaten by chewing, drinking, licking, and sucking). This demonstrates that the Lord not only sustains the external world but also resides within every living being, making its life possible. This is proof of His omnipresence and His compassion towards all beings.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.14)

shloka_text: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च।वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्।।15.15।।
translation: I am seated in the hearts of all living beings. From Me come memory, knowledge, and also forgetfulness. By all the Vedas, I alone am to be known. Indeed, I am the compiler of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
meaning: This verse illustrates the Supreme Lord's ultimate authority and His profound connection with all living beings. Lord Krishna resides as the Supersoul in the hearts of every living entity. From Him alone come memory, knowledge, and also forgetfulness, all according to the beings' actions and desires. The ultimate goal of all Vedas is to know the Lord, as He is the source of all knowledge. He Himself is the compiler of the Vedas and the true knower of their meanings. Thus, the Lord is the ultimate truth, the ultimate knowledge, and the ultimate controller.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.15)

shloka_text: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते।।15.16।।
translation: In this world, there are two types of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All living entities are perishable, and the liberated soul, which is unchanging, is called imperishable.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes two main categories of living entities here. The first category is called 'Kshara' (perishable), which includes all embodied beings subject to the cycle of birth and death. The second category is called 'Akshara' (imperishable), comprising those souls who have become liberated from material bondage and are thus stable and indestructible. These Akshara beings are 'Kutastha,' meaning they remain fixed in their original spiritual state, unaffected by the changes of material nature. This distinction clarifies the material and spiritual states of the living entity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.16)

shloka_text: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः।यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः।।15.17।।
translation: But there is another, the Supreme Divine Personality, distinct from these two (perishable and imperishable), who is called the Supersoul. He is the indestructible controller who, by entering the three worlds, sustains them.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna asserts His supreme preeminence. He describes a third, superior being, distinct from both the perishable (Kshara) and the imperishable (Akshara). This superior being is the Supersoul, who resides in the hearts of all living entities. He is the indestructible controller who, by His power, enters and sustains all three worlds (heaven, earth, and the lower realms). This clarifies that the Lord is not only distinct from individual souls but is also the supreme controller and maintainer of all creation. His existence is unique and supreme.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.17)

shloka_text: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः।।15.18।।
translation: Because I am transcendental to the perishable and even superior to the imperishable, therefore, I am celebrated in the world and in the Vedas as the Supreme Divine Personality (Purushottama).
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna explicitly declares His supreme position. He states that He is not only beyond the perishable material bodies but also superior to the imperishable liberated souls. This unique position makes Him 'Purushottama,' meaning 'the Supreme Person' or 'the Best of Persons.' This name makes Him renowned both in the world (among common people) and in the Vedas (in scriptures). This verse serves as irrefutable proof of the Lord's supreme divinity and His unparalleled existence, establishing Him above all.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.18)

shloka_text: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्।स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत।।15.19।।
translation: O Bharata (Arjuna), one who, without delusion, knows Me as the Supreme Divine Personality (Purushottama) in this way, he is the knower of everything and worships Me with his whole being.
meaning: This verse describes the significance and fruit of knowing the Purushottama. Lord Krishna states that one who knows Him as Purushottama without any doubt is truly omniscient. Such a wise person alone recognizes the Lord in His true form. He then worships the Lord with his entire being, encompassing mind, speech, and action. This devotion is the essence of supreme knowledge and the path to liberation. Such a devotee requires no further knowledge, for he has realized the ultimate truth.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.19)

shloka_text: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ।एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत।।15.20।।
translation: O sinless Arjuna, thus this most confidential scripture has been spoken by Me to you. By understanding this, a person becomes enlightened and accomplishes all that needs to be done.
meaning: In this concluding verse, Lord Krishna reiterates the profound significance of the knowledge presented in the fifteenth chapter. He refers to it as 'guhyatamam shastram,' meaning the most confidential knowledge, which is imparted only to deserving devotees. A person who assimilates this knowledge becomes enlightened, as they comprehend the true nature of the world and their relationship with the Supreme Soul. For such an individual, all duties in life are fulfilled, as they have achieved the ultimate goal. This knowledge paves the way for liberation and grants the soul supreme peace.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (15.20)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः। दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्।।16.1।।
translation: The Supreme Divine Personality said: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadfastness in knowledge and spiritual discipline, charity, control of the senses, performance of sacrifice, study of sacred books, austerity, and straightforwardness.
meaning: This verse begins the enumeration of divine qualities that lead to liberation. Lord Krishna is providing a detailed description of the divine virtues, by cultivating which a person achieves spiritual progress. Fearlessness and purity of mind are fundamental for inner peace and spiritual growth. Steadfastness in knowledge and spiritual discipline paves the way for self-realization. Actions like charity, sense control, and sacrifice make an individual selfless and virtuous. Study of sacred texts, austerity, and straightforwardness bring purity and discipline into one's life. All these qualities collectively contribute to the formation of a divine personality.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.1)

shloka_text: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम्।दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्।।16.2।।
translation: Non-violence, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, restraint from fault-finding, compassion towards all living beings, absence of covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and lack of fickleness.
meaning: This verse highlights other significant qualities of divine nature. Non-violence and truthfulness are the foundational pillars of an ethical life, leading an individual towards pure conduct. Absence of anger and renunciation promote inner peace and detachment, stabilizing the mind. Restraint from fault-finding and compassion towards all beings demonstrate social harmony and empathy. Absence of covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and lack of fickleness strengthen and purify one's character. These virtues collectively pave the way for a balanced and spiritual life.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.2)

shloka_text: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता। भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत।।16.3।।
translation: Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, bearing enmity towards none, and absence of vanity—these are the qualities of those endowed with divine nature, O scion of Bharat (Arjuna).
meaning: This verse describes the concluding qualities of divine nature, which define a divine person. Vigor and fortitude provide an individual with inner strength and stability, enabling them to face life's challenges. Forgiveness and cleanliness purify the mind and soul, removing malice and impure thoughts. Bearing enmity towards none and absence of vanity promote social harmony and humility. All these qualities together create a personality that is spiritually advanced and an ideal for society. Lord Krishna explains these virtues to Arjuna as the divine endowment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.3)

shloka_text: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च।अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्।।16.4।।
translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness, and ignorance—these are the qualities of those endowed with demoniac nature, O Pārtha (Arjuna).
meaning: This verse describes the qualities of demoniac nature, which lead a person towards bondage and degradation. Hypocrisy, arrogance, and conceit fill an individual with ego, causing them to look down upon others. Anger and harshness make their behavior violent and unpleasant, deteriorating social relationships. Ignorance is the root cause of all these vices, preventing an individual from distinguishing between right and wrong. These demoniac qualities hinder spiritual progress and ultimately lead to suffering. Lord Krishna warns Arjuna to avoid these negative tendencies.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.4)

shloka_text: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता।मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव।।16.5।।
translation: Divine qualities are considered to be for liberation, and demoniac qualities for bondage. O Pāṇḍava (Arjuna), do not grieve, for you are born with divine qualities.
meaning: This verse clearly states the consequences of divine and demoniac natures. Divine qualities lead a person towards spiritual liberation and ultimate bliss, whereas demoniac qualities entangle them in worldly bondage. Lord Krishna assures Arjuna that he is endowed with divine qualities, and therefore, he should not grieve in any way. This assurance inspires Arjuna to remain firm on his path of duty and to stay away from demoniac tendencies. This verse conveys the message to evaluate our inner qualities and to move towards positivity.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.5)

shloka_text: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च।दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु।।16.6।।
translation: In this world, there are only two types of created beings—the divine and the demoniac. The divine qualities have been described at length; now, O Pārtha (Arjuna), hear from Me about the demoniac qualities.
meaning: This verse introduces the two fundamental human tendencies existing in the world. Lord Krishna clarifies that humans are either endowed with divine qualities or demoniac qualities. The divine qualities, which lead to liberation and spiritual progress, have already been described in detail. Now, the Lord prepares to describe the demoniac qualities, which cause bondage and degradation. This distinction helps individuals understand their tendencies and choose the right path. Arjuna is asked to listen carefully to the demoniac qualities so that he can avoid them.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.6)

shloka_text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः।न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते।।16.7।।
translation: Persons of demoniac nature do not comprehend what is proper action and what is improper action. Neither purity, nor good conduct, nor truthfulness exists in them.
meaning: This verse describes the fundamental characteristics of individuals with demoniac tendencies. Such people fail to understand the distinction between righteous and unrighteous actions, leading them to act arbitrarily. They lack internal and external purity, which is reflected in their thoughts and deeds. Good conduct and moral values are absent in their lives, causing them to spread unrest in society. They have no allegiance to truth, often resorting to lies and deceit. All these characteristics reveal a demoniac nature and lead them towards spiritual degradation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.7)

shloka_text: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम्।अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम्।।16.8।।
translation: They (demoniac people) say that this world is without absolute truth, without any basis, and without a God. It is born of mutual union, prompted by lust, and has no other cause.
meaning: This verse illustrates the atheistic and materialistic ideology of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They consider the world to be unreal and baseless, refusing to acknowledge any divine power or moral order. According to them, this world originated without any God, merely due to chance and lustful desires. Denying the deeper meaning and purpose of life, they consider only sensual pleasure as the ultimate goal. This perspective alienates them from spiritual values and motivates them to indulge solely in material enjoyments. Such thinking pushes an individual towards moral degradation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.8)

shloka_text: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः।प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः।।16.9।।
translation: Holding such views, these misguided souls of small intellect, engaging in cruel actions, arise as enemies for the destruction of the world.
meaning: This verse clarifies the destructive consequences of demoniac ideology. Those who adopt such atheistic and materialistic views have their souls misguided and their intellect becomes narrow. They indulge in cruel and violent actions solely for their self-interest, spreading unrest and destruction in society. Such individuals are detrimental to themselves and others, becoming enemies of the world. Their activities are focused only on material enjoyment and accumulation of power, causing them to completely abandon moral and spiritual values. This verse illustrates the negative impact of individuals with demoniac tendencies.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.9)

shloka_text: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः।मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः।।16.10।।
translation: Harboring insatiable lust, full of hypocrisy, arrogance, and conceit, deluded, they cling to impermanent things and act with impure resolve.
meaning: This verse describes the internal state and actions of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They are subject to insatiable lustful desires, which keep them constantly restless. Hypocrisy, arrogance, and conceit fill them with ego, leading them to falsely display their superiority. Due to delusion, they consider unreal and transient things as truth, keeping their intellect confused. Such people act with impure resolves and contaminated thoughts, making their actions also impure. This state leads them towards spiritual degradation and suffering.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.10)

shloka_text: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः।कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः।।16.11।।
translation: Taking refuge in endless anxieties that last until death, they consider gratification of desires as the supreme purpose of life and are convinced that this is all there is.
meaning: This verse illustrates the mental state and life perspective of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They remain immersed in countless anxieties that persist until death, as their lives are solely focused on material pleasures. For them, gratification of desires is the supreme purpose of life, and they do not accept any other objective beyond it. They become convinced that the meaning of life is merely to enjoy sensual pleasures and that there is nothing beyond this. This narrow thinking deprives them of spiritual growth and keeps them in constant restlessness and dissatisfaction. Such people can never attain true peace and joy.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.11)

shloka_text: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः।ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्।।16.12।।
translation: Bound by hundreds of ties of desire, dedicated to lust and anger, they strive to accumulate wealth by unjust means for the gratification of their desires.
meaning: This verse describes the covetousness and unethical actions of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They are entangled in hundreds of nets of hopes and desires, which keep them perpetually unsatisfied. Lust and anger are the primary driving forces in their lives, keeping them constantly restless. For the gratification of their senses, they strive to accumulate wealth through unjust and unethical means. They do not hesitate to exploit or deceive others. This tendency leads them towards moral degradation and spreads unrest in society.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.12)

shloka_text: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम्।इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम्।।16.13।।
translation: "This I have gained today, and this desire I shall obtain. This is mine, and this wealth also will be mine again in the future."
meaning: This verse illustrates the selfish and greedy mindset of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They constantly dwell on their achievements and future desires, with only material gain being paramount. "This I have gained today" signifies their present satisfaction, while "this desire I shall obtain" expresses their limitless future aspirations. They consider wealth and possessions as their own and harbor a strong desire to accumulate even more. This thinking never allows them to be satisfied and keeps them trapped in a continuous race for material acquisition.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.13)

shloka_text: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि।ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी।।16.14।।
translation: "That enemy has been destroyed by me, and I shall destroy others also. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, I am powerful, and I am happy."
meaning: This verse illustrates the ego, violence, and self-praise of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They consider themselves omnipotent and do not hesitate to destroy their enemies. "I am the lord" reveals their extreme egoistic thinking, where they consider themselves above any higher power. They remain self-absorbed, believing themselves to be the enjoyer, perfect, powerful, and happy, while in reality, they are restless and dissatisfied. This mindset makes them cruel and merciless towards others, causing them to be solely engaged in fulfilling their self-interest.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.14)

shloka_text: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया।यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः।।16.15।।
translation: "I am wealthy and born in a noble family. Who else is equal to me? I shall perform sacrifices, I shall give alms, and I shall rejoice." Thus, they are deluded by ignorance.
meaning: This verse illustrates the arrogance and ignorance of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They consider themselves superior due to their wealth and noble birth, and they do not see anyone as equal to themselves. They believe they can enhance their prestige in society by performing actions like sacrifices and charity, but their sole purpose is ostentation and self-praise. This thinking arises from ignorance, which keeps them away from true spiritual values. They indulge in external show-offs and neglect inner purity. This ignorance deprives them of true joy.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.15)

shloka_text: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः।प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ।।16.16।।
translation: Perplexed by numerous anxieties, enveloped by a network of illusions, excessively attached to sense gratification, they fall into an unclean hell.
meaning: This verse describes the tragic end of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They are surrounded by countless anxieties, which prevent their minds from ever finding peace. Trapped in a web of delusion and illusion, they cannot perceive the truth and continue on the wrong path. Their excessive attachment to sense gratification compels them to chase material pleasures, thereby depriving them of spiritual progress. Ultimately, such people fall into an impure and sorrowful hell where they suffer intense torment due to their actions. This verse warns of the dreadful consequences of a demoniac lifestyle.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.16)

shloka_text: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः।यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम्।।16.17।।
translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, full of wealth, pride, and arrogance, they perform sacrifices merely in name, ostentatiously and without regard for scriptural injunctions.
meaning: This verse exposes the hypocrisy and ignorance of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They consider themselves highly superior and are stubborn by nature, refusing to listen to anyone. Wealth, pride, and arrogance fill them with ego, leading them to try and maintain their false prestige. They perform sacrifices merely for show, which are in name only and do not adhere to scriptural injunctions. Their sole purpose is to establish their dominance in society and impress others, not to gain genuine spiritual benefit. This ostentatious behavior keeps them away from true devotion and knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.17)

shloka_text: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः।।16.18।।
translation: Taking refuge in egotism, strength, arrogance, lust, and anger, these envious demoniac individuals hate Me (the Supreme Self) residing in their own and others' bodies.
meaning: This verse illustrates the extreme ignorance and God-hatred of individuals with demoniac tendencies. They are enveloped by vices such as egotism, strength, arrogance, lust, and anger, which blind them. They fail to understand that the Supreme Self resides in the hearts of all beings, whether in their own body or in others'. Due to their envy and hatred, they even despise that Supreme Self who is present both within and without them. This ignorance completely alienates them from spiritual truth and pushes them towards grave sins.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.18)

shloka_text: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान्।क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु।।16.19।।
translation: Those hateful, cruel, and vile persons among humankind in this material world, I repeatedly cast them into inauspicious demoniac wombs.
meaning: This verse describes the punishment ordained by Lord Krishna for individuals with demoniac tendencies. Those who indulge in hateful, cruel, and vile actions are repeatedly born by the Lord into inauspicious demoniac wombs. This is the natural consequence of their actions, where they further strengthen their demoniac tendencies. This punishment deprives them of spiritual progress and keeps them entangled in the cycle of material existence. This statement by the Lord demonstrates His justice and His resolve to establish righteousness. It inspires us to be mindful of our actions.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.19)

shloka_text: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि।मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम्।।16.20।।
translation: O son of Kunti (Arjuna), those ignorant persons, having obtained demoniac wombs birth after birth, fail to reach Me and thereafter descend to an even more abominable destination.
meaning: This verse clarifies the unfortunate future of individuals with demoniac tendencies. Those ignorant persons who are born into demoniac wombs remain deprived of spiritual knowledge and the attainment of God, birth after birth. Due to their demoniac tendencies, they continuously descend towards degradation and ultimately reach an even more abominable destination. This state completely diverts them from the path of liberation and pushes them into the deep darkness of material existence. This statement by Lord Krishna warns of the severe consequences of a demoniac lifestyle.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.20)

shloka_text: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः।कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्।।16.21।।
translation: These are the three types of gates to hell, which destroy the self—lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
meaning: This verse clearly states the three main causes of spiritual degradation. Lust, anger, and greed are considered the three gates to hell because they contaminate the soul and lead it towards destruction. Lust entangles an individual in material pleasures, anger makes them violent and restless, and greed motivates them to commit unethical actions. It is extremely essential to abandon these three vices, as they deprive a person of true happiness and peace. Only by conquering these can an individual achieve spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.21)

shloka_text: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः।आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम्।।16.22।।
translation: O son of Kunti (Arjuna), a person freed from these three gates to darkness acts for the welfare of their soul, and thereby attains the supreme goal.
meaning: This verse describes the positive consequences of abandoning lust, anger, and greed. A person who frees themselves from these three gates to darkness begins to act for the true welfare of their soul. Their tendencies change, and they progress towards spiritual advancement. The actions of such an individual are selfless and righteous, leading them to attain inner peace and contentment. Ultimately, through such conduct, they achieve the supreme goal, which is liberation. This verse explains the importance of self-control and spiritual practice.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.22)

shloka_text: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः।न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्।।16.23।।
translation: One who discards scriptural injunctions and acts under the impulse of desire attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.
meaning: This verse clarifies the importance of scriptures and the consequences of disregarding them. An individual who neglects the injunctions prescribed by the scriptures and acts solely according to their desires can never attain true perfection. Such a person neither achieves worldly happiness nor attains the supreme spiritual goal. Scriptures guide us on the path of right and wrong, and adhering to them is essential for spiritual progress. Acting arbitrarily leads to confusion and ultimately results in suffering.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.23)

shloka_text: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ।ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि।।16.24।।
translation: Therefore, in determining what is duty and what is forbidden action, the scriptures are your authority. Having understood the actions revealed in the scriptural injunctions, you should perform them in this world.
meaning: This verse emphasizes the supreme authoritative importance of scriptures. Lord Krishna instructs Arjuna that scriptures are the only reliable guide for determining what is duty and what is forbidden action. One should perform actions in this world only after understanding the injunctions revealed in the scriptures, as they provide the foundation for righteousness and morality. By adhering to scriptural conduct rather than one's arbitrary desires, an individual can achieve true welfare. This teaching inspires us to live a discerning life and follow the scriptures for spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (16.24)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाचये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः।तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः।।17.1।।
translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, what is the state of those who worship with faith but disregard the injunctions of the scriptures? Is their devotion in the mode of goodness, passion, or ignorance?
meaning: Arjuna's question here seeks to understand the nature of faith itself. He inquires about the spiritual state of those who, despite neglecting scriptural injunctions, still engage in worship with sincere faith. This query is crucial for comprehending the inner disposition of an individual and the motivation behind their actions. Lord Krishna will elaborate on the different types of faith based on the three modes of material nature in response to this question. This inquiry helps us recognize that not just external rituals, but the underlying sentiment of an action, holds profound significance.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.1)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु।।17.2।।
translation: The Supreme Personality said: The faith of embodied beings, born of their innate nature, is of three kinds—in the mode of goodness, passion, and ignorance. Hear about them from Me.
meaning: Lord Krishna, responding to Arjuna's query, explains that the faith of embodied beings is inherently threefold. This faith originates from the three modes of material nature—goodness, passion, and ignorance—residing within an individual's consciousness. A person's faith aligns with the mode that predominantly influences them. This classification helps us understand that not everyone's spiritual journey or method of worship is identical. The Lord will further elaborate on these three types of faith to ensure Arjuna's clear comprehension.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.2)

shloka_text: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत।श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः।।17.3।।
translation: O Bharata, the faith of all human beings conforms to the nature of their inner being. A person is made of his faith; whatever his faith is, so he is.
meaning: Lord Krishna here elucidates the profound influence of faith. He states that every individual's faith is shaped by the inherent qualities residing within their inner self. A person's entire being is constituted by their faith, as their conviction guides their thoughts, emotions, and actions. Consequently, whatever the nature of one's faith, so is their character and life. This verse emphasizes that faith is not merely an emotion but the fundamental basis of an individual's existence. It inspires us to recognize the nature of our own faith and strive to purify it.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.3)

shloka_text: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः।प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः।।17.4।।
translation: Those in the mode of goodness worship the celestial gods; those in the mode of passion worship demigods and demons; and others, in the mode of ignorance, worship ghosts and spirits.
meaning: This verse illustrates the distinct forms of worship corresponding to the three modes of material nature. Those in the mode of goodness worship celestial gods with a pure heart, leading them towards righteousness, knowledge, and peace. Individuals in the mode of passion worship demigods and demons, driven by desires for material gain, power, and fame. Conversely, those in the mode of ignorance, out of delusion, worship ghosts and spirits, which yields fear, superstition, and lower results. This classification clearly indicates that the purpose of worship and the nature of the deity worshipped reflect an individual's internal qualities.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.4)

shloka_text: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः।।17.5।।
translation: Those who perform severe austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, impelled by hypocrisy and egotism, and driven by desire, attachment, and force.
meaning: This verse describes individuals who undertake severe austerities contrary to scriptural injunctions. Such ascetics are filled with hypocrisy and egotism, aiming for self-praise or to impress others. Their penance is driven by lower tendencies like desire, attachment, and force, rather than a genuine wish for self-purification or God-realization. This type of austerity only inflicts physical suffering and hinders spiritual progress. Such actions are indicative of a tamasic disposition, which binds the individual.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.5)

shloka_text: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः।मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान्।।17.6।।
translation: Those senseless people torment the elements of the body and Me also, who dwell within the inner self; know them to be of demoniacal resolves.
meaning: Lord Krishna identifies such ascetics as possessing a demoniac nature. These ignorant individuals needlessly torment the elements of their own bodies, disrupting their physical and mental balance. Furthermore, they inflict suffering upon the Supreme Self, the Lord, who resides within the body, as the body is a temple of the Divine. Driven by their demoniac tendencies, such people pursue a self-destructive path. Their austerities are not aimed at self-welfare but at satisfying their ego or causing harm to others.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.6)

shloka_text: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः।यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु।।17.7।।
translation: Indeed, food, too, which is dear to all, is of three kinds. So are sacrifice, austerity, and charity. Hear from Me the distinctions among them.
meaning: Lord Krishna now presents a classification of various aspects of life based on the three modes of nature. He explains that just as faith is threefold, so too is food, which is dear to all individuals. Furthermore, significant religious acts like sacrifice, austerity, and charity also manifest in three distinct ways according to these modes. This classification helps us understand that our daily life choices and religious practices are influenced by our inherent qualities. The Lord will further elaborate on these three distinctions to provide Arjuna with clear knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.7)

shloka_text: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः।रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः।।17.8।।
translation: Foods that promote longevity, vitality, strength, health, happiness, and satisfaction—which are juicy, succulent, nourishing, and pleasing to the heart—are dear to those in the mode of goodness.
meaning: This verse describes the qualities of sattvic food. Sattvic food is that which enhances longevity, keeps the mind calm and cheerful, and bestows strength and health upon the body. Such foods are juicy, succulent, nourishing, and pleasing to the heart. These meals purify the body and mind, infusing the individual with positive energy and peace. Consuming sattvic food helps one progress towards spiritual advancement and attain mental stability.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.8)

shloka_text: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः।आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः।।17.9।।
translation: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry, and cause burning are dear to persons in the mode of passion, and they produce pain, grief, and disease.
meaning: This verse describes the characteristics of rajasic food. Rajasic food is typically bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and causes a burning sensation. Such foods are dear to people of rajasic temperament because they provide stimulation and sensory pleasure. However, these foods ultimately lead to pain, grief, and various diseases. Consuming rajasic food keeps the mind restless and creates imbalance in the body, thereby hindering spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.9)

shloka_text: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्।उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम्।।17.10।।
translation: Foods that are stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten, leftover, and impure are dear to persons in the mode of ignorance.
meaning: This verse describes the qualities of tamasic food. Tamasic food is that which is stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten, leftover, and impure. Such foods are dear to people of tamasic temperament because they increase their ignorance and lethargy. Consuming these foods leads to inertia, laziness, and disease in the body. Tamasic food pollutes the mind and leads an individual towards spiritual degradation, dulling their intellect.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.10)

shloka_text: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः।।17.11।।
translation: That sacrifice which is performed by those who do not desire any reward, in accordance with scriptural injunctions, with the conviction that it is one's duty to offer it, is of the nature of goodness.
meaning: This verse describes sattvic sacrifice. A sattvic sacrifice is one performed without any desire for results, solely as a duty, and in accordance with scriptural injunctions. In such a sacrifice, the mind is focused with the understanding that it is an act of service to God. This sacrifice paves the way for self-purification and spiritual advancement, as there is no room for selfishness. An individual performing a sattvic sacrifice acts selflessly, thereby attaining inner peace and contentment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.11)

shloka_text: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्।।17.12।।
translation: But, O best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be in the mode of passion which is performed with the desire for results or for the sake of pride.
meaning: This verse clarifies the characteristics of rajasic sacrifice. A rajasic sacrifice is one performed with the desire to achieve some result or merely for ostentation. In such a sacrifice, the individual's primary aim is to enhance their prestige, gain material benefits, or assert their superiority over others. This type of sacrifice lacks true faith and selflessness. While performing a rajasic sacrifice might bring temporary pleasure or social recognition, it spiritually binds the individual and does not provide inner peace.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.12)

shloka_text: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम्।श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते।।17.13।।
translation: That sacrifice which is performed without scriptural direction, without distribution of prasadam, without chanting of Vedic hymns, without remunerations to the priests, and without faith, is considered to be in the mode of ignorance.
meaning: This verse describes tamasic sacrifice. A tamasic sacrifice is one performed without scriptural direction, lacking distribution of food, proper chanting of mantras, offerings to priests, and most importantly, devoid of faith. Such sacrifices are mere pretense or performed out of ignorance, yielding no real benefit. Performing a tamasic sacrifice does not accrue any merit; instead, it plunges the individual deeper into ignorance and darkness. This action leads to spiritual degradation.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.13)

shloka_text: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम्।ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते।।17.14।।
translation: Worship of the Supreme Lord, Brahmins, the spiritual master, and elders; cleanliness, simplicity, celibacy, and non-violence—these are declared as the austerity of the body.
meaning: Lord Krishna here describes various aspects of bodily austerity. Respectful worship of the Supreme Lord, Brahmins, spiritual masters, and elders is a crucial component of physical penance. Maintaining bodily cleanliness and cultivating simplicity in thoughts and actions are also included. Practicing celibacy and refraining from harming any living being through thought, word, or deed (non-violence) also fall under bodily austerity. All these actions discipline the body and make it suitable for spiritual practice.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.14)

shloka_text: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते।।17.15।।
translation: Words that do not cause distress, are truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, as well as the regular recitation of Vedic scriptures—these are declared as the austerity of speech.
meaning: This verse describes the austerity of speech, which purifies an individual's communication. Speech should be non-disturbing, meaning calm and gentle. It must be truthful, yet also pleasant and beneficial, so that it creates a positive impact. Furthermore, the regular study and practice of the Vedas and scriptures constitute austerity of speech, as this enhances knowledge and sanctifies one's words. All these qualities make speech disciplined and effective, leading to spiritual development.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.15)

shloka_text: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः।भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते।।17.16।।
translation: Serenity of thought, gentleness, silence, self-control, and purity of purpose—these are declared as the austerity of the mind.
meaning: Lord Krishna here highlights the crucial aspects of mental austerity. Serenity of mind, meaning inner peace and contentment, forms the foundation of mental penance. Maintaining a gentle disposition, practicing silence to avoid unnecessary talk, and exercising self-control over senses and thoughts are also included. Most importantly, purity of purpose, meaning freedom from deceit, malice, and envy, is the essence of mental austerity. All these practices make the mind calm, stable, and focused, which are essential for spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.16)

shloka_text: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः।अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते।।17.17।।
translation: That threefold austerity, performed by steadfast persons with transcendental faith and without yearning for material rewards, is designated as being in the mode of goodness.
meaning: This verse identifies sattvic austerity. When all three types of penance—bodily, verbal, and mental—are performed by steadfast individuals with supreme faith and without desiring any material results, they are termed sattvic. The purpose of such austerity is self-purification and God-realization, not any material gain. Sattvic austerity bestows inner peace, knowledge, and spiritual advancement upon the individual. This penance helps liberate the person from the bondage of the modes of nature.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.17)

shloka_text: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्।।17.18।।
translation: That austerity which is performed for the sake of respect, honor, and adoration, and also with ostentation, is declared in this world to be rajasic, being flickering and temporary.
meaning: This verse describes the characteristics of rajasic austerity. Rajasic penance is that which is performed with the aim of gaining respect, honor, and adoration from others. Ostentation and showmanship are prominent in it, where an individual displays their austerities. The results of such penance are flickering and temporary, as they are based on external praise. While rajasic austerity might bring temporary social prestige, it does not provide inner peace or lasting spiritual benefit.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.18)

shloka_text: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः।परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।17.19।।
translation: That austerity which is performed with foolish obstinacy, by torturing oneself, or for the purpose of harming others, is described to be in the mode of ignorance.
meaning: This verse describes tamasic austerity. Tamasic penance is that which is performed with foolish obstinacy, by inflicting pain upon one's own body. The purpose of such austerity is not self-welfare; rather, it sometimes aims to harm or frighten others. This penance is a symbol of ignorance and cruelty, benefiting neither the ascetic nor society. Tamasic austerity pushes an individual further into darkness and bondage, completely halting their spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.19)

shloka_text: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्।।17.20।।
translation: That charity which is given with the understanding that it is worthy of charity, to one who cannot give in return, in the proper place, at the proper time, and to a worthy person, is stated to be in the mode of goodness.
meaning: This verse describes the qualities of sattvic charity. Sattvic charity is that which is given with the understanding that 'giving is a duty,' without any expectation of return. This charity is offered in the proper place (a sacred location), at the proper time (an auspicious moment), and to a worthy recipient (a deserving person). Such charity benefits both the giver and the receiver, as it embodies selflessness and purity. Sattvic charity aids spiritual progress and purifies the mind.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.20)

shloka_text: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्।।17.21।।
translation: But that charity which is given with the hope of a return, or with the expectation of a reward, and also reluctantly, is said to be in the mode of passion.
meaning: This verse clarifies the characteristics of rajasic charity. Rajasic charity is that which is given with the hope of a return, meaning with the desire to receive something in exchange. In this, the giver's objective is to gain some fruit or enhance their prestige. This charity is often given reluctantly or with difficulty, lacking true generosity of heart. While rajasic charity might bring temporary benefits or social recognition, it spiritually binds the individual and does not provide inner contentment.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.21)

shloka_text: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते।असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।17.22।।
translation: That charity which is given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect, and with contempt, is held to be of the nature of ignorance.
meaning: This verse describes tamasic charity. Tamasic charity is that which is given at an improper place (an unholy location) and an improper time (an inauspicious moment). This charity is offered to unworthy individuals, without any respect and with contempt. Such charity benefits neither the giver nor the receiver; instead, it increases ignorance and negativity. Tamasic charity pushes an individual further into darkness and bondage, hindering their spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.22)

shloka_text: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा।।17.23।।
translation: "Om Tat Sat"—this threefold designation of the Absolute Truth has been declared. From it, Brahmins, Vedas, and sacrifices were created in ancient times.
meaning: Lord Krishna here explains the significance of "Om Tat Sat." These three words constitute the threefold designation of Brahman, signifying its omnipresence, truth, and completeness. In ancient times, Brahmins, Vedas, and sacrifices were created from the utterance of these very words, serving as the foundation of spiritual life since the dawn of creation. 'Om' represents the primordial sound form of the Supreme, 'Tat' denotes its infinite existence, and 'Sat' signifies its eternal truth. This triad serves as a means to establish our connection with Brahman.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.23)

shloka_text: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्।।17.24।।
translation: Therefore, the acts of sacrifice, charity, and penance, prescribed by Vedic injunctions, are always begun by the expounders of the Vedas with the utterance of "Om."
meaning: This verse emphasizes the significance of uttering "Om." Since 'Om' symbolizes Brahman, expounders of the Vedas always commence all their acts of sacrifice, charity, and penance by uttering "Om." This utterance bestows purity and divinity upon the action, connecting it with Brahman. Beginning with 'Om' enhances concentration and faith in actions, making them more fruitful. This tradition ensures that all auspicious deeds are inspired by a spiritual purpose.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.24)

shloka_text: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि।।17.25।।
translation: Uttering the syllable "Tat," various acts of sacrifice, austerity, and charity are performed by seekers of liberation, without desiring fruitive rewards.
meaning: This verse clarifies the usage and purpose of the word "Tat." 'Tat' means 'That' or 'the Supreme Self.' Seekers of liberation, who do not desire fruitive results, perform their acts of sacrifice, austerity, and charity by uttering "Tat." This utterance signifies the sentiment that all actions are dedicated to the Supreme Self, and no personal gain is expected from them. The use of 'Tat' makes actions detached and helps the individual free themselves from worldly attachments.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.25)

shloka_text: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते।प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते।।17.26।।
translation: The word "Sat" is used in the sense of eternal existence and goodness, and also in the sense of auspiciousness. O Partha, the word "Sat" is also applied to an auspicious action.
meaning: Lord Krishna here explains the multifaceted meanings of the word "Sat." 'Sat' is used to express eternal existence (truth, being) and auspiciousness (goodness, excellence). This word denotes the eternal truth and goodness that is the fundamental nature of Brahman. Furthermore, any auspicious or excellent action is also referred to as 'Sat,' because that action is beneficial and conducive to welfare. The use of 'Sat' bestows purity and divinity upon actions, making them spiritually significant.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.26)

shloka_text: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते।।17.27।।
translation: Steadiness in sacrifice, penance, and charity is also pronounced as "Sat." And any action performed for the purpose of the Supreme is indeed described as "Sat."
meaning: This verse further clarifies the usage of the word "Sat." The steadfastness and stability observed in auspicious actions like sacrifice, penance, and charity are also referred to as 'Sat.' This stability reflects an individual's true faith and dedication. Furthermore, any action performed for the purpose of the Supreme, meaning for the pleasure of God, is also described as 'Sat.' This verse defines the quality of actions and the intention behind them through 'Sat,' thereby enhancing their spiritual value.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.27)

shloka_text: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह।।17.28।।
translation: O Partha, whatever sacrifice, charity, or penance is performed, or whatever else is done without faith, is termed "Asat." It is of no value either in this world or in the next.
meaning: This verse underscores the paramount importance of faith. Lord Krishna states that any action performed without faith—be it sacrifice, charity, penance, or any other deed—is termed "Asat." 'Asat' means unreal, useless, or ephemeral. Such actions yield no real fruit either in this world or in the next. Deeds performed without faith are merely physical or mechanical acts, devoid of spiritual essence. Therefore, faith is absolutely essential for spiritual advancement.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (17.28)

shloka_text: अर्जुन उवाच संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्। त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन।।18.1।।
translation: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, I wish to know the truth of sannyasa (renunciation of actions) and tyaga (renunciation of desires for the fruits of actions) distinctly, O Hrishikesha, O slayer of Keshi!
meaning: In this verse, Arjuna requests Lord Krishna to clarify the profound meanings of sannyasa and tyaga. He wishes to understand the true nature of these two terms and the distinction between them. Sannyasa is generally understood as the complete renunciation of actions, while tyaga refers to the abandonment of attachment to the fruits of actions. Arjuna's inquiry reflects the natural questions that arise in the human mind regarding spiritual practice. Lord Krishna proceeds to explain these concepts in detail in the subsequent verses.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.1)

shloka_text: श्री भगवानुवाच काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः। सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः।।18.2।।
translation: The Supreme Divine Personality said: The learned understand the renunciation of desire-prompted actions as sannyasa, and the wise declare the renunciation of the fruits of all actions as tyaga.
meaning: Lord Krishna presents the definitions of sannyasa and tyaga in this verse. He explains that sannyasa is the renunciation of desire-prompted actions, meaning those performed with an expectation of results. On the other hand, tyaga is defined as the relinquishment of attachment to the fruits of all actions. This distinction clarifies that sannyasa relates to the type of actions, while tyaga pertains to the mind's attitude towards the results of actions. The learned understand these two concepts in their true essence. Thus, Lord Krishna begins to resolve Arjuna's inquiry.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.2)

shloka_text: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे।।18.3।।
translation: Some learned persons declare that all actions should be given up as being inherently flawed, while others say that acts of sacrifice, charity, and penance should never be abandoned.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna mentions the various prevailing opinions regarding sannyasa and tyaga. Some scholars believe that all actions are inherently flawed and should therefore be abandoned. In contrast, other scholars hold the view that auspicious actions like sacrifice, charity, and penance should never be given up. This verse indicates that diverse perspectives on this subject have existed since ancient times. Lord Krishna presents these differing views to lead towards His own definitive conclusion. This discussion highlights the depth of understanding required for the nature of action and its proper execution.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.3)

shloka_text: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः।।18.4।।
translation: O best of the Bharatas, hear My conclusive opinion regarding tyaga (renunciation). O tiger among men, tyaga is indeed declared to be of three kinds.
meaning: Lord Krishna is now prepared to reveal His final and conclusive opinion on the subject of tyaga to Arjuna. He addresses Arjuna as 'best of the Bharatas' and 'tiger among men,' signifying his importance and worthiness. The Lord clarifies that tyaga is not merely of one kind, but is declared to be of three distinct types. This declaration forms the basis for the detailed explanation of sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic forms of tyaga in the subsequent verses. This classification helps in understanding the underlying motivation and the influence of the gunas behind actions. Thus, the Lord further elucidates the central message of the Gita.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.4)

shloka_text: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत्।यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्।।18.5।।
translation: Acts of sacrifice, charity, and penance should never be abandoned; they must certainly be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity, and penance are purifiers even for the wise.
meaning: Lord Krishna explicitly states here the actions that should not be abandoned. He declares that acts of sacrifice, charity, and penance must certainly be performed. These actions are described as purifiers even for the wise, highlighting their profound significance. This verse refutes the opinion of those who advise abandoning all actions, considering them inherently flawed. The Lord's instruction reinforces the principle of Karma Yoga, where actions are performed as a matter of duty. Through these actions, an individual can purify their consciousness.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.5)

shloka_text: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम्।।18.6।।
translation: O Partha, these very actions (sacrifice, charity, and penance) must certainly be performed by giving up attachment and the desire for their fruits. This is My definite and supreme opinion.
meaning: Lord Krishna further clarifies His previous statement, asserting that even actions like sacrifice, charity, and penance must be performed by relinquishing attachment and the desire for their fruits. This is His definite and supreme opinion, encapsulating the essence of Karma Yoga. True renunciation is not the abandonment of actions, but the abandonment of attachment to their results. This principle teaches an individual to remain unaffected by the outcomes while performing their duties. Thus, the Lord emphasizes the importance of selfless action, which paves the way for spiritual progress.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.6)

shloka_text: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते।मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः।।18.7।।
translation: The renunciation of prescribed duties is not proper. Abandoning them out of delusion is declared to be tamasic (in the mode of ignorance) renunciation.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the tamasic type of renunciation in this verse. He states that it is not proper to abandon prescribed duties, which are enjoined by the scriptures. If an individual renounces such duties out of delusion or ignorance, that renunciation is termed tamasic. Tamasic renunciation arises from ignorance, laziness, and confusion, causing a person to deviate from their true obligations. This type of renunciation neither leads to spiritual progress nor yields any auspicious results. Therefore, the Lord declares such abandonment to be improper and detrimental.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.7)

shloka_text: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत्।स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्।।18.8।।
translation: One who abandons a duty, considering it troublesome, out of fear of bodily discomfort, performs a rajasic (in the mode of passion) renunciation and certainly never attains the fruit of true renunciation.
meaning: In this verse, Lord Krishna describes the rajasic type of renunciation. If a person abandons a duty, considering it troublesome or out of fear of bodily discomfort, that renunciation is termed rajasic. One who performs such a renunciation certainly does not attain the fruit of true renunciation. Rajasic renunciation is motivated by selfishness, fear, and the desire for sensory pleasure, which does not liberate an individual from the bondage of action. This type of renunciation entangles a person further in attachment, thus the Lord declares it incomplete.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.8)

shloka_text: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन।सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः।।18.9।।
translation: O Arjuna, that prescribed action which is performed with the conviction, 'This is my duty,' by relinquishing attachment and indeed the desire for its fruits, is considered sattvic (in the mode of goodness) renunciation.
meaning: Lord Krishna describes the sattvic type of renunciation here, which He considers superior. He states that the prescribed action performed with the conviction, 'This is my duty,' by relinquishing attachment and the desire for its fruits, is indeed sattvic renunciation. This type of renunciation liberates an individual from the bondage of action and leads them towards spiritual progress. In sattvic renunciation, there is no abandonment of action itself, but rather the abandonment of attachment to the results of action. This is the ideal form of selfless action (Karma Yoga), which aids in the purification of the mind and the attainment of self-knowledge.
title: Daily Gita Reflection (18.9)

shloka_text: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते।त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः।।18.10।।
translation: The renouncer, endowed with the mode of goodness, intelligent, and free from doubts, neither hates disagreeable work nor is attached to agreeable work.
